```text
1	# `fleet-status` reports `unreachable` even though `ssh <host>` works interactively
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `just fleet-status` shows a host as ✗ `unreachable` with note like
5	  `PermissionDenied: Permission denied for user <user> on host <ip>`
6	- `just fleet-apply --hosts <host>` fails the same way at the readiness preflight
7	- Manually running `ssh <host>` (or `ssh <ssh_alias>`) succeeds — but **prompts
8	  for a password** before letting you in
9	- Other hosts in the same `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` succeed (they all use
10	  SSH key / `ssh-agent` / 1Password agent auth)
11	- The host's inventory entry has a `password_source = { type = "plain", value = "..." }`
12	  (or `bitwarden` / `prompt`) — and you reasonably assumed that covers SSH login
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-05-08, on `zyc_friend` (an IDC server reachable only via
15	password auth). User had set `password_source = { type = "plain", ... }` and
16	expected `fleet-status` / `fleet-apply` to use that for the SSH login.
17	
18	**Affects**: any host where `~/.ssh/config` doesn't yield a usable key (no
19	`IdentityFile`, no agent forward, key not authorised on remote, password-only
20	sshd policy).
21	
22	## Root cause
23	
24	In `scripts/fleet_apply.py`, `password_source` is **only** consumed by
25	`_resolve_passwords()` (~line 203) to populate `Host.sudo_password`, which is
26	then written to a 0600 temp file on the remote and exported as
27	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (see `build_remote_command()` ~line 426). That env
28	var is picked up by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` → `sudo_session_init` to skip
29	the `/dev/tty` prompt during chezmoi's `run_*` scripts.
30	
31	**SSH login itself uses `subprocess` → `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` (effectively)
32	with no `sshpass` involvement.** When key auth fails, sshd asks for a password,
33	`BatchMode` forbids it, the connection dies with `Permission denied`, and the
34	host is classified `unreachable` by `_classify_readiness()` (~line 2007).
35	
36	So the password schema works at two completely different stages:
37	
38	| Stage | Auth mechanism | Reads `password_source`? |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| SSH login (transport) | key / agent only | ❌ NO |
41	| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from `password_source` | ✅ YES |
42	
43	The schema doc (`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` lines
44	49–54) labels `type = "plain"` as "last resort — relies on file mode 0600",
45	which reads as if it covers everything. It doesn't say *what* it covers.
46	
47	## Why it's designed this way
48	
49	Three deliberate choices, listed so you don't "fix" this by accident:
50	
51	1. **No `sshpass` dependency.** Avoids extra binary install + maintenance, and
52	   most modern sshd configs ship with `PasswordAuthentication no` anyway.
53	2. **Parallel apply incompatible with TTY prompts.** `fleet-apply` runs N hosts
54	   concurrently; an interactive password prompt would deadlock the orchestrator.
55	3. **Security posture.** SSH password auth has known weaknesses (online
56	   brute-force surface). The repo philosophy nudges users toward key-based.
57	
58	## Fix (per-host)
59	
60	Recommended:
61	
62	```sh
63	ssh-copy-id <host>                              # push your pubkey
64	ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> true && echo OK     # verify key auth works non-interactively
65	just fleet-status                                # confirm host now classifies correctly
66	```
67	
68	### Gotcha: `ssh-copy-id` succeeds but ssh STILL asks for password
69	
70	Seen on `zyc_friend` (IDC server) 2026-05-08. `ssh-copy-id` reports
71	`Number of key(s) added: 1` and the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` entry IS on the
72	remote, but next login still prompts. `ssh -v` reveals:
73	
74	```
75	Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive
76	```
77	
78	Note `publickey` is **absent**. The remote sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no`
79	(common in corporate / IDC security baselines). The key was deposited but the
80	server refuses to consider it. Two consequences:
81	
82	1. `ssh-copy-id` itself runs over `keyboard-interactive` (PAM), not over
83	   key auth — it succeeds at the file-write step but proves nothing about
84	   future logins.
85	2. Even adding `sshpass` support to fleet-apply (the deferred TODO) wouldn't
86	   trivially work — `sshpass` defaults to the `password` method, but PAM-only
87	   sshds need `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`.
88	
89	Fix: ask the remote admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in
90	`/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (+ `systemctl reload sshd`). If they refuse, drop the
91	host from the fleet inventory and apply manually.
92	
93	Verify pubkey auth is allowed before troubleshooting your own keys:
94	
95	```sh
96	ssh -v <host> true 2>&1 | grep "Authentications that can continue"
97	# Must include `publickey` for fleet-apply to ever work.
98	```
99	
100	If the remote forbids key auth (rare; usually a misconfigured `sshd_config`
101	with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), edit the remote sshd or remove the host from
102	the fleet inventory and apply manually:
103	
104	```sh
105	ssh <host>
106	# inside the remote shell:
107	chezmoi update --apply
108	```
109	
110	## Detection
111	
112	Quick triage when a host shows `unreachable`:
113	
114	```sh
115	# 1. Does manual SSH work?
116	ssh <host> true && echo "ssh works"
117	
118	# 2. Does it work non-interactively (the mode fleet uses)?
119	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <host> true
120	# If this prompts or errors → no usable key auth → fleet can't reach it
121	```
122	
123	If step 1 prompts for a password but step 2 errors with `Permission denied
124	(publickey,password)`, you've hit this pitfall.
125	
126	## Related
127	
128	- `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema doc (consider
129	  amending the `password_source` comment to clarify it's sudo-only)
130	- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` → "Readiness probe" — describes the
131	  `_classify_readiness` state vocabulary
132	- `docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md` → "Non-interactive password injection" — the
133	  consumer side of `password_source` / `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
134	- `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md` — adjacent sudo-helper trap
135
```

330	(exit 2 on missing config) — readiness is the only command that's

332	
333	## Inventory file
334	
335	Path: `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. Seeded **once** by chezmoi from
336	[`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl).
337	[`just az-dev-vm`](az-dev-vm.md) also appends/updates a `[[hosts]]` entry here
338	automatically when it provisions an Azure dev VM (and removes it on
339	`az-dev-vm-down`).
340	The `create_private_` prefix means:
341	
342	- `create_` → chezmoi seeds the file on first apply, then never touches it
343	  again. Your edits survive every `chezmoi apply`.
344	- `private_` → file mode 0600. Safe to keep plaintext sudo passwords here.
345	- To reset the seed: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
346	
347	### Schema
348	
349	```toml
350	[defaults]                    # merged into every host (host keys override)
351	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # PATH binary; e.g. "~/.local/bin/chezmoi" if no-root
352	connect_timeout = 15
353	command_timeout = 1800
354	
355	[[hosts]]
356	name            = "lab-box"   # required, unique display name
357	ssh_alias       = "lab-box"   # preferred: matches `Host lab-box` in ~/.ssh/config
358	# OR explicit connection (used when no ssh_alias):
359	hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
360	user            = "dwlee"
361	port            = 22
362	identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
363	
364	no_root_machine = false       # MUST mirror the chezmoi `noRoot=` value used at
365	                              # `chezmoi init` time on that remote (see below)
366	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # override defaults per-host
367	local           = false       # set true to run chezmoi locally (no SSH); see
368	                              # "Local host execution" section below
369	extra_env       = { FOO = "bar" }   # extra env vars for the remote chezmoi run
370	
371	password_source = { type = "...", ... }   # see "Password sources" below
372	```
373	
374	### Password sources
375	
376	| `type` | Extra keys | Behaviour |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| `none` (default) | — | No password injected. Suitable for `no_root_machine = true` hosts. |
379	| `plain` | `value = "..."` | Read straight from TOML. Relies on file mode 0600. |
380	| `prompt` | — | `getpass()` once at startup, never persisted to disk. |
381	| `bitwarden` | `item = "ssh-host-sudo"` | `bw get password <item>` at startup. Requires `bw unlock` + `BW_SESSION` exported. |
382	
383	### `no_root_machine` semantics
384	
385	This flag **describes** the remote, it does not change it. Each remote was
386	configured at `chezmoi init` time with a `noRoot` boolean (see
387	[`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48`](../../.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)) that's now baked into
388	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` on that machine.
389	
390	- Set `no_root_machine = true` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = true` —
391	  fleet_apply skips sudo entirely (no password file written, run-scripts'
392	  `sudo_session_init` returns "non-interactive" branch and skips sudo work).
393	- Set `no_root_machine = false` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = false`
394	## How sudo password reaches the remote
395	
396	`scripts/fleet/apply.py` does **not** echo the password into the command line.
397	The remote command (assembled by `build_remote_command()`) reads stdin into
398	`~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` (mode 0600, `umask 077`), exports
399	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=$PWD/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass`, runs
400	`chezmoi update`, then `trap … EXIT` removes the file (even on crash).
401	
402	On the remote, `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh::sudo_session_init` was extended
403	with a non-interactive injection path: when `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
404	points to a readable file, the password is validated with `sudo -S -v`, then
405	adopted into the shared state dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/`)
406	exactly the same way an interactive prompt would be — including the watchdog
407	that holds the sudo timestamp warm and writes `ansible-become.yml` for
408	ansible roles. **Subsequent run-scripts inside the same `chezmoi update` see
409	the cached state and never re-prompt.**
410	
411	Pass file lifecycle:
412	- `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` is the orchestrator's drop-off; removed
413	  by the SSH command's `trap` once chezmoi exits.
414	- `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/sudo.pass` is the shared state dir
415	  managed by `sudo_shared.sh`; cleaned up by the existing watchdog when the
416	  ancestor `chezmoi` PID exits.
417	
418	## Connection: ssh_config alias vs explicit
419	
420	`asyncssh.connect(host=...)` reads `~/.ssh/config` like the OpenSSH client.
421	Prefer `ssh_alias`:
422	
423	```
424	# ~/.ssh/config
425	Host lab-box
426	    HostName 10.0.0.42
427	    User dwlee
428	    ProxyJump bastion
429	    IdentityAgent ~/.1password/agent.sock     # 1Password SSH agent
430	```
431	
432	```toml
433	# machines.toml
434	[[hosts]]
435	name      = "lab-box"
436	ssh_alias = "lab-box"          # ← inherits everything above, including ProxyJump
437	```
438	
439	If a host has no ssh_config entry, fall back to explicit
440	`hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file`.
441	
442	## Local host execution (`local = true`)
443	
444	To include the orchestrator machine itself in a fleet apply, add a host
445	with `local = true`:
446	
447	```toml
448	[[hosts]]
449	name            = "self"
450	local           = true
451	no_root_machine = true   # set false if your local apply needs sudo
452	```
453	
454	Local hosts skip asyncssh entirely — chezmoi runs as a direct
455	subprocess (`asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`) inheriting the
456	orchestrator's PATH, sudoers state, and tty. Sudo password injection
457	is not used; if chezmoi needs root it'll prompt on the parent terminal.
458	The `kill-orphans` subcommand also skips local hosts (killing local
459	chezmoi processes from the same shell session would kill `fleet_apply`
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# apply_with_sudo.sh — run `chezmoi apply` (or `chezmoi init --apply`) with
# sudo password injected via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`, for environments
# where the chezmoi-spawned run-script subprocess can't open /dev/tty
# (CentOS 7 + AD/LDAP user, missing pam_systemd, etc).
#
# Why this exists:
#   The shared sudo helper (scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) prompts on /dev/tty
#   when sudo isn't passwordless. Some Linux configurations break that path
#   — see pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md for the full
#   diagnosis. This wrapper bypasses the broken path by pre-staging the
#   password in a 0600 tmpfile and pointing the helper at it.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh                          # chezmoi apply
#   bash scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh --init <repo-url>        # chezmoi init --apply
#   bash scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh --pass-from-file FILE    # don't prompt; read from FILE
#   bash scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh --pass-from-env          # read $SUDO_PASSWORD env var
#   bash scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh --keep-file              # don't shred (debugging)
#
# Exit code: chezmoi's exit code (after shredding the password file).
#
# Security:
#   - tmpfile is created with umask 077 (mode 0600) under $TMPDIR.
#   - shredded on EXIT (any signal) unless --keep-file given.
#   - password is never put on the command line or in env after handoff.

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  sed -n '2,/^$/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
  exit "${1:-0}"
}

mode="apply"
repo_url=""
pass_source="prompt"
pass_file_in=""
keep_file=0

while (($#)); do
  case "$1" in
    --init)
      mode="init"
      shift
      [[ $# -eq 0 || "$1" == --* ]] && {
        echo "ERROR: --init requires a repo URL" >&2
        exit 2
      }
      repo_url="$1"
      shift
      ;;
    --pass-from-file)
      pass_source="file"
      shift
      [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && {
        echo "ERROR: --pass-from-file requires FILE" >&2
        exit 2
      }
      pass_file_in="$1"
```
</details></tool-use>

Based on the search results, here's a security comparison of the three sshpass methods:

## Security Ranking (Most to Least Secure)

**1. -f (File Descriptor) - Most Secure**

The -f flag is the most secure method, as the password lives in a file with restricted permissions, stays out of process listings, and doesn't linger in shell history. When using this method, it's critical to set proper file permissions (chmod 0400). This is the recommended approach for any scripted use of sshpass.

**2. -e (Environment Variable) - Moderate Security**

The -e flag reads the password from the SSHPASS environment variable, which is safer than -p because environment variables don't appear in ps output (on most systems). However, the password still exists in the process environment, so it's not bulletproof.

**3. -p (Command Line) - Least Secure**

The -p option should be considered the least secure of all sshpass's options, as all system users can see the password in the command line with a simple "ps" command. This is considered the least secure choice and shouldn't be used.

## Key Takeaway

Using -f or -e is safer than -p, and using -f with secure file permissions or -e with environment variables minimizes exposure.

1	# `fleet-status` reports `unreachable` even though `ssh <host>` works interactively
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `just fleet-status` shows a host as ✗ `unreachable` with note like
5	  `PermissionDenied: Permission denied for user <user> on host <ip>`
6	- `just fleet-apply --hosts <host>` fails the same way at the readiness preflight
7	- Manually running `ssh <host>` (or `ssh <ssh_alias>`) succeeds — but **prompts
8	  for a password** before letting you in
9	- Other hosts in the same `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` succeed (they all use
10	  SSH key / `ssh-agent` / 1Password agent auth)
11	- The host's inventory entry has a `password_source = { type = "plain", value = "..." }`
12	  (or `bitwarden` / `prompt`) — and you reasonably assumed that covers SSH login
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-05-08, on `zyc_friend` (an IDC server reachable only via
15	password auth). User had set `password_source = { type = "plain", ... }` and
16	expected `fleet-status` / `fleet-apply` to use that for the SSH login.
17	
18	**Affects**: any host where `~/.ssh/config` doesn't yield a usable key (no
19	`IdentityFile`, no agent forward, key not authorised on remote, password-only
20	sshd policy).
21	
22	## Root cause
23	
24	In `scripts/fleet_apply.py`, `password_source` is **only** consumed by
25	`_resolve_passwords()` (~line 203) to populate `Host.sudo_password`, which is
26	then written to a 0600 temp file on the remote and exported as
27	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (see `build_remote_command()` ~line 426). That env
28	var is picked up by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` → `sudo_session_init` to skip
29	the `/dev/tty` prompt during chezmoi's `run_*` scripts.
30	
31	**SSH login itself uses `subprocess` → `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` (effectively)
32	with no `sshpass` involvement.** When key auth fails, sshd asks for a password,
33	`BatchMode` forbids it, the connection dies with `Permission denied`, and the
34	host is classified `unreachable` by `_classify_readiness()` (~line 2007).
35	
36	So the password schema works at two completely different stages:
37	
38	| Stage | Auth mechanism | Reads `password_source`? |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| SSH login (transport) | key / agent only | ❌ NO |
41	| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from `password_source` | ✅ YES |
42	
43	The schema doc (`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` lines
44	49–54) labels `type = "plain"` as "last resort — relies on file mode 0600",
45	which reads as if it covers everything. It doesn't say *what* it covers.
46	
47	## Why it's designed this way
48	
49	Three deliberate choices, listed so you don't "fix" this by accident:
50	
51	1. **No `sshpass` dependency.** Avoids extra binary install + maintenance, and
52	   most modern sshd configs ship with `PasswordAuthentication no` anyway.
53	2. **Parallel apply incompatible with TTY prompts.** `fleet-apply` runs N hosts
54	   concurrently; an interactive password prompt would deadlock the orchestrator.
55	3. **Security posture.** SSH password auth has known weaknesses (online
56	   brute-force surface). The repo philosophy nudges users toward key-based.
57	
58	## Fix (per-host)
59	
60	Recommended:
61	
62	```sh
63	ssh-copy-id <host>                              # push your pubkey
64	ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> true && echo OK     # verify key auth works non-interactively
65	just fleet-status                                # confirm host now classifies correctly
66	```
67	
68	### Gotcha: `ssh-copy-id` succeeds but ssh STILL asks for password
69	
70	Seen on `zyc_friend` (IDC server) 2026-05-08. `ssh-copy-id` reports
71	`Number of key(s) added: 1` and the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` entry IS on the
72	remote, but next login still prompts. `ssh -v` reveals:
73	
74	```
75	Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive
76	```
77	
78	Note `publickey` is **absent**. The remote sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no`
79	(common in corporate / IDC security baselines). The key was deposited but the
80	server refuses to consider it. Two consequences:
81	
82	1. `ssh-copy-id` itself runs over `keyboard-interactive` (PAM), not over
83	   key auth — it succeeds at the file-write step but proves nothing about
84	   future logins.
85	2. Even adding `sshpass` support to fleet-apply (the deferred TODO) wouldn't
86	   trivially work — `sshpass` defaults to the `password` method, but PAM-only
87	   sshds need `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`.
88	
89	Fix: ask the remote admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in
90	`/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (+ `systemctl reload sshd`). If they refuse, drop the
91	host from the fleet inventory and apply manually.
92	
93	Verify pubkey auth is allowed before troubleshooting your own keys:
94	
95	```sh
96	ssh -v <host> true 2>&1 | grep "Authentications that can continue"
97	# Must include `publickey` for fleet-apply to ever work.
98	```
99	
100	If the remote forbids key auth (rare; usually a misconfigured `sshd_config`
101	with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), edit the remote sshd or remove the host from
102	the fleet inventory and apply manually:
103	
104	```sh
105	ssh <host>
106	# inside the remote shell:
107	chezmoi update --apply
108	```
109	
110	## Detection
111	
112	Quick triage when a host shows `unreachable`:
113	
114	```sh
115	# 1. Does manual SSH work?
116	ssh <host> true && echo "ssh works"
117	
118	# 2. Does it work non-interactively (the mode fleet uses)?
119	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <host> true
120	# If this prompts or errors → no usable key auth → fleet can't reach it
121	```
122	
123	If step 1 prompts for a password but step 2 errors with `Permission denied
124	(publickey,password)`, you've hit this pitfall.
125

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-sonnet-5 2026-07-02 03:59:12Z)**_

I have a complete picture now. Here is the full research report.

## 1. SSH mechanism: `asyncssh`, key/agent auth only — no password auth ever passed to it

Every fleet script that talks SSH (`scripts/fleet/apply.py`, `exec.py`, `tmux.py`, `info.py`, `pueue.py`) shares one connection-kwargs builder, `_connect_kwargs()`, defined once in `scripts/fleet/apply.py:558-578` and imported by the others:

```python
def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
    if host.user: kwargs["username"] = host.user
    if host.port: kwargs["port"] = host.port
    if host.identity_file:
        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
    return kwargs
```

Then `conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(host))` — grep confirms **9 call sites total** (apply.py has 6: main apply, readiness, status, kill-orphans, compact, tail; plus one each in exec.py/tmux.py/info.py/pueue.py), and **none** ever passes `password=` to `asyncssh.connect`. `known_hosts=None` just disables asyncssh's own host-key DB check (comment explains it relies on the user's `~/.ssh/known_hosts` from a prior manual SSH). `client_keys` is optional — when absent, asyncssh falls back to reading `~/.ssh/config` (per `host=ssh_alias`) and the local SSH agent, exactly like the OpenSSH client (confirmed in `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md:420`: `asyncssh.connect(host=...) reads ~/.ssh/config like the OpenSSH client`). So auth is 100% key/agent-based (including `IdentityAgent`/`ProxyJump` from ssh_config, e.g. 1Password SSH agent) — **asyncssh's own password-auth capability is never exercised**.

## 2. `password_source` types and resolution (`create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` + `apply.py`)

Type is `Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]` (`apply.py:61`), parsed in `load_hosts()` (`apply.py:134-140`) and resolved in `resolve_passwords()` (`apply.py:193-235`):

| type | extra key | resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `none` (default) | — | `sudo_password` stays `None` |
| `plain` | `value` | copied straight from TOML (`h.sudo_password = h.password_source_arg`) |
| `prompt` | — | `getpass.getpass()` once per host at startup, never persisted |
| `bitwarden` | `item` | `_bw_get_password(item)` runs `bw get password <item>` subprocess |

**Critically — this resolved value is used ONLY for remote sudo, never for SSH login.** The template itself (`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl:8-11`) says this explicitly:

```
# IMPORTANT: `password_source` is for the REMOTE `sudo` password ONLY (fed to
# chezmoi via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE for `run_*` scripts). It does NOT
# authenticate the SSH login itself — fleet always uses non-interactive SSH
# (key / agent auth). If `ssh <host>` prompts you for a password, the host
# will show as `unreachable` in `just fleet-status`.
```

## 3. `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — local sudo-session helper

This runs on the *target* machine (during `chezmoi apply`/`update` run-scripts), not the orchestrator. Key API (`docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md`):
- `sudo_session_init [label]` — idempotent; probes `NOPASSWD:ALL` first (`_sudo_is_truly_passwordless`), else prompts once via `read -rs pw < /dev/tty`, validates with `sudo -S -v -p '' <<<pw`, writes password to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/sudo.pass` (mode 0600) plus an `ansible-become.yml` YAML sidecar, spawns a detached watchdog (`setsid`/`nohup`) that keeps the sudo timestamp warm every 50s and self-destructs (`rm -rf` state dir) when the ancestor chezmoi PID exits.
- `sudo_run <cmd...>` — `sudo -S -p '' -- "$@" <"$CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASS_FILE"`, i.e. password piped via stdin redirection from the cached file, **never in argv or an env var**.
- Non-interactive branch (`apply.py:203-246`): if `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` env var points to a readable 0600 file, its contents are read, validated with `sudo -S -v`, then adopted into the same state-dir/watchdog machinery as an interactive prompt — then the env var itself is `unset`.

## 4. `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` — how fleet feeds sudo password over SSH

This is the bridge between `password_source` (orchestrator side) and `sudo_shared.sh` (remote side), built in `build_remote_command()` (`apply.py:242-488`):

```python
REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH = ".cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass"
...
pre = (
    f"umask 077; mkdir -p \"$(dirname {pass_path})\"; "
    f"cat > {pass_path}; chmod 600 {pass_path}; "
    f"export CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=\"$PWD/{REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH}\"; "
)
cleanup_extra = f" rm -f {pass_path};"
```

In `run_one()` (`apply.py:897-900`): after `conn.create_process(cmd, stdin=asyncssh.PIPE)`, the resolved `host.sudo_password` is written directly to the remote shell's stdin (`proc.stdin.write(stdin_text); proc.stdin.write_eof()`) — the remote `cat > sudo.pass` reads it until EOF. No PTY is requested deliberately (comment explains: with a PTY, `cat`'s stdin-EOF semantics require Ctrl-D, and `write_eof()` becomes a no-op). A `trap` removes the pass file on exit/crash. So: **password travels over the already-authenticated SSH channel's stdin stream**, never touches the remote command line/argv, and is deleted after use.

This IS the same underlying secret (whatever `password_source` resolved to) — but it is a **separate mechanism from SSH login auth**: `password_source` only ever feeds this sudo-injection path; SSH transport auth is untouched by it, confirmed by `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`'s table:

| Stage | Auth mechanism | Reads `password_source`? |
|---|---|---|
| SSH login (transport) | key / agent only | NO |
| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from `password_source` | YES |

## 5. Docs confirm the flow

`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md:394-416` (`## How sudo password reaches the remote`) matches the code exactly, and states plainly `scripts/fleet/apply.py does not echo the password into the command line`. `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md:135-136`: "`fleet hosts NAME` prompts for password: fleet always uses non-interactive SSH (key / agent auth). A password prompt means..." — reinforcing key-only SSH login as the model throughout the fleet tooling.

## 6. `sshpass` — NOT used anywhere in actual code/scripts; only discussed as a deferred TODO

Grep across the whole repo (excluding `.git`) turns up zero usage in any `.py`/`.sh`/ansible role. The only hits are:
- `TODO.md:80` and several `.specstory/history/*.md` copies of it — a backlog item: *"fleet-apply: optional `sshpass` / interactive-password SSH login support"* — an unimplemented, deferred (opt-in, default-off) feature idea triggered by host `zyc_friend` (IDC server with `PubkeyAuthentication no` + PAM `keyboard-interactive` sshd).
- `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md:32,51,85-87` — explicitly documents "**No `sshpass` involvement**" as the root cause of the `unreachable` classification pitfall, and lists "No `sshpass` dependency" as a deliberate design choice (avoids extra binary install, most modern sshd already disables `PasswordAuthentication`).
- `.specstory/history/2026-06-18_16-37-42Z-hash-alacritty-ls-permission.md:1511,3859,14711,14731` — a **separate, one-off manual workaround**, not part of the fleet tool: someone manually ran `brew install hudochenkov/sshpass/sshpass` and `SSHPASS='...' sshpass -e ssh ...` by hand to reach `zyc_friend` directly (bypassing `fleet` entirely) — this is history/transcript, not repo code.

Conclusion: `sshpass` the binary is never invoked by any script in this repo. It exists only as a documented gap/TODO and as ad-hoc manual usage recorded in session history.

## 7. Key-based auth is the default AND the only supported path — password is fallback only for sudo, not SSH

- **SSH login**: key/agent auth is not "primary with password fallback" — it is currently the **only** supported mechanism. There is no code path in any fleet script that would let asyncssh (or `ssh`) attempt password auth for the transport/login itself. A password-only host is a hard failure (`unreachable`), by design (per the pitfall doc's "why it's designed this way": avoids TTY-prompt deadlock under `fleet-apply`'s parallel execution, and nudges toward key-based security posture).
- **Sudo (post-login)**: password actually is the primary mechanism when `no_root_machine=false` — resolved via `password_source` (`plain`/`prompt`/`bitwarden`), or `none` to skip sudo entirely for `no_root_machine=true` hosts.

# Research: sshpass / SSH password automation, and how `fleet` handles it

## Context

User linked https://sshpass.com/ and https://github.com/kevinburke/sshpass and asked (1) whether
`sshpass` is the right tool for automating password-based SSH login, what the broader landscape of
alternatives looks like, and (2) whether this repo's `fleet` CLI (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`,
backed by `scripts/fleet/*.py`) uses a similar technique to connect to fleet hosts.

This is a pure research/explanation request — no code or doc changes were requested, and the user
didn't respond to confirm scope, so per the "just answer" default: **no files will be modified.**
The deliverable is a direct chat answer, synthesizing external research with the exact mechanism this
repo already uses (and has already documented as a deliberate, non-obvious design decision).

## What to deliver (chat answer, no file edits)

### Part 1 — sshpass and the broader landscape

- **What `sshpass` is**: a thin wrapper that answers OpenSSH's interactive password prompt
  non-interactively, via a pty trick. Two forks exist: the original (farrokhi, SourceForge mirror)
  and `kevinburke/sshpass` (a GitHub mirror of the same SourceForge source, read-only, no PR
  acceptance — not a functional fork, just a mirror for `go get`-able/brew-tap-able access).
- **Security tiers of sshpass's own flags** (worst → best):
  - `-p <pass>` — plaintext on argv, visible to any local user via `ps`. Worst option.
  - `-e` (`SSHPASS` env var) — not in `ps` output, but still readable via `/proc/<pid>/environ` on Linux.
  - `-f <file>` — password from a file descriptor/path; best when combined with `chmod 0400`. This is
    the "least bad" way to use sshpass if you must.
- **Why sshpass is broadly discouraged for production/scripted use**: plaintext password has to exist
  *somewhere* (env, file, vault) for sshpass to read it; it doesn't eliminate the "credential at rest"
  problem, it just moves where the plaintext briefly lives. Compliance frameworks (PCI-DSS/HIPAA/CIS)
  generally frown on plaintext-password SSH automation.
- **Better alternatives, roughly in order of preference for automation**:
  1. **SSH key-based auth** (ed25519/rsa key + `ssh-copy-id`) — no password in the loop at all; the
     gold standard for scripted/unattended SSH.
  2. **ssh-agent / IdentityAgent forwarding** (incl. 1Password SSH agent, YubiKey-backed keys) — keys
     never touch disk unencrypted; agent handles signing.
  3. **`expect`** — scriptable interactive-session automation; more flexible than sshpass (can handle
     arbitrary prompts, 2FA flows) but still needs the secret sourced from somewhere.
  4. **Secrets managers** (Vault, Bitwarden/1Password CLI, AWS Secrets Manager) feeding into key
     material or short-lived credentials, rather than long-lived plaintext passwords.
  5. **Library-level SSH with password auth** (Python `paramiko` supports password auth directly;
     `asyncssh` supports it too but is typically used for concurrent/async key-based fleets) — only
     meaningfully safer than sshpass if the password itself is sourced securely (vault/keyring), since
     the library still needs the plaintext in memory at connect time.
  - Net: **the tool matters less than where the plaintext secret lives and how briefly**. Keys avoid
    the problem entirely; sshpass/expect/paramiko-password all still require a plaintext secret at
    some point, so the real differentiator is secret sourcing + minimizing exposure window, not the
    ssh-automation tool itself.

### Part 2 — how `fleet` in this repo actually works (verified from code + existing docs)

Direct, concrete answer to "does fleet use something like sshpass": **No — fleet deliberately never
uses sshpass or any password for the SSH *login* itself.** Two completely separate stages, confirmed
by both code and this repo's own pitfall doc:

| Stage | Mechanism | Uses `password_source` / sshpass-like technique? |
|---|---|---|
| SSH login (transport) | `asyncssh.connect(**kwargs)` in `scripts/fleet/apply.py:_connect_kwargs` (558-578) — `client_keys` from `identity_file`, else falls back to `~/.ssh/config` + local ssh-agent (incl. 1Password SSH agent via `IdentityAgent`), exactly like the OpenSSH client. **`password=` is never passed.** | No |
| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `password_source` (`plain` / `prompt` / `bitwarden` / `none`) resolved in `resolve_passwords()` (apply.py:193-235); value is written to the **already-authenticated SSH channel's stdin** on the remote (`proc.stdin.write(...)`, no PTY, no argv, no env var) and consumed remotely via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` (`sudo_run` pipes it to `sudo -S` via file redirection, never argv/env). | Yes, but this is sudo-only, not SSH-login |

Key files to point at if the user wants to read code directly:

Why fleet is built this way (already documented as deliberate, not an oversight):
1. Avoids an extra binary dependency (`sshpass`) most hosts don't need.
2. Parallel `fleet-apply` runs N hosts concurrently — an interactive password prompt would deadlock.
3. Security posture: nudges every fleet host toward key-based auth rather than password auth.

## sshpass 與自動化 SSH 密碼登入的整體知識

**sshpass 是什麼**：一個用 pty trick 把密碼「餵」給 OpenSSH 互動式密碼提示的小工具。你連的兩個連結分別是官網（sshpass.com）和 `kevinburke/sshpass`——後者只是 SourceForge 原始碼的唯讀 GitHub mirror（不接受 PR），跟原始 `farrokhi/sshpass` 是同一份程式碼，不是功能性 fork。

**sshpass 三種密碼傳遞方式，安全性由差到好**：
- `-p <pass>`：明文寫在 argv，任何本機使用者 `ps` 就看得到 —— 最差，別用。
- `-e`（`SSHPASS` 環境變數）：不會出現在 `ps`，但 Linux 上仍可透過 `/proc/<pid>/environ` 讀到。
- `-f <file>`：從檔案讀密碼，搭配 `chmod 0400` 是「不得已要用 sshpass 時」最安全的方式。

**為什麼業界普遍不建議在正式環境用 sshpass**：不管用哪個 flag，明文密碼終究要「存在某處」才能被 sshpass 讀取——它沒有消除「靜態明文密碼」這個問題，只是搬動明文短暫存在的位置。PCI-DSS / HIPAA / CIS 之類的合規框架通常不喜歡明文密碼驅動的 SSH 自動化。

**比 sshpass 更好的替代方案（推薦順序）**：
1. **SSH key 驗證**（ed25519 + `ssh-copy-id`）—— 自動化/無人值守 SSH 的黃金標準，密碼完全不進入流程。
2. **ssh-agent / IdentityAgent forwarding**（含 1Password SSH agent、YubiKey）—— key 不會以未加密形式落地。
3. **`expect`** —— 比 sshpass 更靈活（可處理任意 prompt、2FA），但密碼一樣得從某處讀進來。
4. **Secrets manager**（Vault、Bitwarden/1Password CLI、AWS Secrets Manager）驅動 key 或短效憑證，取代長效明文密碼。
5. **Library 層級的密碼驗證**（Python `paramiko` 原生支援密碼登入；`asyncssh` 也支援，但通常用在 key-based 的並發連線）—— 只有在密碼本身來源夠安全（vault/keyring）時，才比 sshpass 更安全，因為 library 連線當下記憶體裡一樣要有明文密碼。

**結論**：工具本身不是重點，重點是**明文密碼存在哪裡、存在多久**。Key-based 驗證直接繞過整個問題；sshpass/expect/paramiko-password 都還是需要某個時刻有明文密碼，差別只在於怎麼安全地取得密碼、把曝露窗口壓到最小。

## fleet 是不是用類似 sshpass 的方法？—— 不是，而且是刻意設計

我讀了 `scripts/fleet/apply.py`、`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`、schema 樣板、以及這個 repo 自己寫好的 pitfall 文件，答案很明確：**fleet 完全不用 sshpass，SSH 登入本身也從不接受密碼**。分成兩個完全獨立的階段：

| 階段 | 機制 | 用到 sshpass 式技巧？ |
|---|---|---|
| **SSH 登入**（transport） | `asyncssh.connect(**kwargs)`（`scripts/fleet/apply.py:_connect_kwargs`, 558-578）—— 有 `identity_file` 就用它當 `client_keys`，沒有就退回讀 `~/.ssh/config` + 本機 ssh-agent（含 1Password SSH agent），跟原生 OpenSSH client 行為一致。**`password=` 參數從沒被傳過。** | ❌ 完全沒有 |
| **登入後的 remote `sudo`** | `password_source`（`plain`/`prompt`/`bitwarden`/`none`，`resolve_passwords()` @ apply.py:193-235）解出密碼後，**直接寫進已經驗證過的 SSH channel 的 stdin**（`proc.stdin.write(...)`，不開 PTY），遠端用 `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` 這個環境變數指到一個 0600 暫存檔，`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` 的 `sudo_run` 再用 `sudo -S` 讀那個檔案——密碼**從不出現在 argv 或環境變數裡**。 | ⚠️ 是，但這只餵 sudo，不餵 SSH 登入 |

這個 repo 已經自己寫了一篇 pitfall 文件精準描述這件事：[`pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`](pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md)。裡面記錄了一個真實案例：`zyc_friend`（一台 IDC 伺服器）的 sshd 設定 `PubkeyAuthentication no` + 只允許 `keyboard-interactive`（PAM），導致就算 `ssh-copy-id` 把 key 佈署上去了，登入還是會跳密碼提示，fleet 因此把它分類成 `unreachable`。

**這是刻意的設計，不是遺漏**（pitfall 文件裡列了三個理由）：
1. 不想引入 `sshpass` 這個額外的二進位依賴。
2. `fleet-apply` 會平行跑好幾台主機——互動式密碼提示會讓整個 orchestrator 卡死（deadlock）。
3. 安全立場：逼所有 fleet host 走 key-based 驗證。

而且 `TODO.md:80` 已經有一條**尚未實作、刻意延後**的 backlog 項目，設計草案已經寫好了：給 `password-only`/PAM-only 的少數主機一個 opt-in 的 sshpass fallback（含 `PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`、sshpass 缺裝時的 graceful fallback、以及並行安全性的考量）。如果你之後想真的動手做這個功能，可以直接從那條 TODO 接手。

**如果你自己手動要連 `zyc_friend` 這類 password-only 機器**（不透過 fleet），目前 repo 的 session 紀錄裡確實有人手動 `brew install hudochenkov/sshpass/sshpass` 然後 `SSHPASS='...' sshpass -e ssh ...` 過——用的是 `-e`（環境變數）這個安全性中等的做法，符合上面說的分級。

Sources:
- [Are there alternatives to sshpass for secure automation?](https://sshpass.com/are-there-alternatives-to-sshpass-for-secure-automation/)
- [sshpass - Login to ssh server with a password using a shell script (nixCraft)](https://www.cyberciti.biz/faq/noninteractive-shell-script-ssh-password-provider/)
- [SSH Password Authentication: Security Risks & Top 5 Alternatives (Frontegg)](https://frontegg.com/blog/ssh-password-authentication-security-risks-and-top-5-alternatives)
- [sshpass: Automate SSH Password Login on Linux and macOS](https://computingforgeeks.com/sshpass-ssh-login-with-password-linux-macos/)
- [sshpass(1) man page](https://linux.die.net/man/1/sshpass)
- [kevinburke/sshpass (GitHub mirror)](https://github.com/kevinburke/sshpass)

The deferred design sketch in TODO.md:80 says a real fix needs: (a) optional `sshpass -f` invocation when `password_source.ssh_login = true` (or a separate `ssh_password_source`), (b) `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password` to handle PAM-only sshds (sshpass defaults to `password` method only), (c) graceful fallback when `sshpass` not installed, (d) parallel-safe (no TTY prompts), (e) opt-in only — default stays key-only for security.

275	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
276	
277	- name: Set glab release architecture
278	  # Broadened to RedHat + decoupled from glab_check so the user-level
279	  # fallback works on CentOS 7 where the .deb install is skipped.
280	  when:
281	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
282	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
283	    glab_release_arch: >-
284	      {{
285	        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
286	        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
287	        else ''
288	      }}
289	
290	- name: Skip glab on unsupported architecture
291	  when:
292	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
293	    - glab_check.rc != 0
294	    - glab_release_arch == ''
295	  ansible.builtin.debug:
296	    msg: "glab skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"
297	
298	- name: Install glab from GitLab releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
299	  when:
300	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
301	    - glab_check.rc != 0
302	    - glab_release_arch != ''
303	  become: true
304	  tags: [sudo]
305	  block:
306	    - name: Get latest glab release
307	      ansible.builtin.uri:
308	        url: https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/gitlab-org%2Fcli/releases/permalink/latest
309	        return_content: true
310	      register: glab_release
311	
312	    - name: Download glab .deb package
313	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
314	        url: "https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases/{{ glab_release.json.tag_name }}/downloads/glab_{{ glab_release.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}_linux_{{ glab_release_arch }}.deb"
315	        dest: /tmp/glab.deb
316	        mode: '0644'
317	        timeout: 120
318	      retries: 3
319	      delay: 5
320	
321	    - name: Install glab .deb package
322	      ansible.builtin.apt:
323	        deb: /tmp/glab.deb
324	
325	    - name: Clean up glab .deb
326	      ansible.builtin.file:
327	        path: /tmp/glab.deb
328	        state: absent
329	
330	  rescue:
331	    - name: Warn glab installation failed
332	      ansible.builtin.debug:
333	        msg: "glab installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
334	
335	    - name: Clean up glab temp files after failure
336	      ansible.builtin.file:
337	        path: "{{ item }}"
338	        state: absent
339	      loop:
340	        - /tmp/glab.deb

342	# --- glab (user-level fallback) ---
343	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — glab is a Go
344	# static binary (no glibc dependency).
345	- name: Re-check if glab is installed
346	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
347	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v glab
348	  register: glab_recheck
349	  changed_when: false
350	  failed_when: false
351	  environment:
352	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
353	
354	- name: Install glab from GitLab releases (user-level, no sudo)
355	  when:
356	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
357	    - glab_recheck.rc != 0
358	    - glab_release_arch | default('') != ''
359	  block:
360	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (glab)
361	      ansible.builtin.file:
362	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
363	        state: directory
364	        mode: '0755'
365	
366	    - name: Get latest glab release (user)
367	      ansible.builtin.uri:
368	        url: https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/gitlab-org%2Fcli/releases/permalink/latest
369	        return_content: true
370	      register: glab_release_user
371	
372	    - name: Download glab tarball (user)
373	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
374	        url: "https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases/{{ glab_release_user.json.tag_name }}/downloads/glab_{{ glab_release_user.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}_linux_{{ glab_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
375	        dest: /tmp/glab.tar.gz
376	        mode: '0644'
377	        timeout: 120
378	      retries: 3
379	      delay: 5
380	
381	    - name: Extract and install glab (user)
382	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
383	        set -euo pipefail
384	        rm -rf /tmp/glab-extract
385	        mkdir -p /tmp/glab-extract
386	        tar -xzf /tmp/glab.tar.gz -C /tmp/glab-extract
387	        glab_bin="$(find /tmp/glab-extract -type f -path '*/bin/glab' | head -n 1)"
388	        install -m 0755 "$glab_bin" "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/glab"
389	      args:
390	        executable: /bin/bash
391	      changed_when: true
392	
393	    - name: Clean up glab temp files (user)
394	      ansible.builtin.file:
395	        path: "{{ item }}"
396	        state: absent
397	      loop:
398	        - /tmp/glab.tar.gz
399	        - /tmp/glab-extract
400	
401	  rescue:
402	    - name: Warn glab (user) installation failed
403	      ansible.builtin.debug:
404	        msg: "glab (user) installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
405	
406	    - name: Clean up glab (user) temp files after failure
407	      ansible.builtin.file:
408	        path: "{{ item }}"
409	        state: absent
410	      loop:
411	        - /tmp/glab.tar.gz
412	        - /tmp/glab-extract

607	  when:
608	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
609	    - zoxide_check.rc != 0
610	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
611	    curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/install.sh | sh
612	  args:
613	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts.env.HOME }}/.local/bin/zoxide"
614	  failed_when: false

618	  when:
619	    - zoxide_install_result is defined
620	    - zoxide_install_result.rc is defined

625	# --- eza ---
626	- name: Check if eza is installed
627	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
628	  ansible.builtin.command: eza --version
629	  register: eza_check
630	  changed_when: false
631	  failed_when: false
632	
633	- name: Install eza via official installer (Debian/Ubuntu)
634	  when:
635	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
636	    - eza_check.rc != 0
637	  become: true
638	  tags: [sudo]
639	  block:
640	    - name: Add eza GPG key
641	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
642	        mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
643	        wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eza-community/eza/main/deb.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
644	      args:
645	        creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
646	
647	    # deb822_repository (apt_repository is deprecated, removed in
648	    # ansible-core 2.25) writes the .sources file WITHOUT running
649	    # `apt update`, so we verify reachability ourselves and roll the file
650	    # back when the repo is broken/unreachable (GFW hosts) — a leftover
651	    # broken source would otherwise fail the base role's cache update on
652	    # every subsequent run. The GitHub-release fallback below installs eza
653	    # in that case. Requires python3-debian (installed by the base role).
654	    - name: Remove legacy one-line eza source (pre-deb822 format)
655	      ansible.builtin.file:
656	        path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gierens.list
657	        state: absent
658	
659	    - name: Add eza repository (deb822)
660	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
661	        name: gierens
662	        types: deb
663	        uris: http://deb.gierens.de
664	        suites: stable
665	        components: main
666	        signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
667	      ignore_errors: true
668	      register: eza_repo
669	
670	    - name: Refresh apt cache (eza repo)
671	      when: eza_repo is succeeded
672	      ansible.builtin.apt:
673	        update_cache: true
674	      ignore_errors: true
675	
676	    # The apt module treats a partially-failed `apt update` (one unreachable
677	    # source, others fine) as SUCCESS-with-warnings, so its failed/succeeded
678	    # status can't tell us whether the gierens repo actually works. Probe
679	    # deterministically: eza resolvable from deb.gierens.de ⇒ keep + install;
680	    # otherwise roll the .sources file back so it can't slow down / break
681	    # later apt updates, and let the GitHub fallback below take over.
682	    - name: Check eza is resolvable from the gierens repo
683	      when: eza_repo is succeeded
684	      ansible.builtin.command: apt-cache policy eza
685	      register: eza_policy
686	      changed_when: false
687	      failed_when: false
688	
689	    - name: Remove eza repository (broken or unreachable)
690	      when:
691	        - eza_repo is succeeded
692	        - "'deb.gierens.de' not in (eza_policy.stdout | default(''))"
693	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
694	        name: gierens
695	        state: absent
696	
697	    - name: Install eza from repository
698	      ansible.builtin.apt:
699	        name: eza
700	        state: present
701	      when: "'deb.gierens.de' in (eza_policy.stdout | default(''))"
702	      ignore_errors: true
703	  rescue:
704	    - name: Warn eza apt install failed
705	      ansible.builtin.debug:
706	        msg: "eza apt install failed (likely broken third-party repo) — will try GitHub fallback"
707	
708	# --- eza (user-level fallback) ---
709	# Upstream publishes a musl tarball for x86_64 only. aarch64 has just
710	# `unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`, which can break on Jammy when upstream CI uses a
711	# newer glibc. Split the user fallback by arch:
712	#   - x86_64: switch to `eza_x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`.
713	#   - aarch64: probe Linuxbrew; install via brew if present, otherwise skip
714	#     with an explicit warning.
715	- name: Re-check if eza is installed
716	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
717	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v eza
718	  register: eza_recheck
719	  changed_when: false
720	  failed_when: false
721	
722	- name: Install eza musl from GitHub releases (user-level, x86_64)
723	  when:
724	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
725	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0
726	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
727	  block:
728	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (eza)
729	      ansible.builtin.file:
730	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
731	        state: directory
732	        mode: '0755'
733	
734	    - name: Get latest eza release
735	      ansible.builtin.uri:
736	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/eza-community/eza/releases/latest
737	        return_content: true
738	      register: eza_release
739	
740	    - name: Download eza musl binary (x86_64)
741	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
742	        url: "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/download/{{ eza_release.json.tag_name }}/eza_x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
743	        dest: /tmp/eza.tar.gz
744	        mode: '0644'
745	        timeout: 120
746	      retries: 3
747	      delay: 5
748	
749	    - name: Extract eza to ~/.local/bin
750	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
751	        src: /tmp/eza.tar.gz
752	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
753	        remote_src: true
754	
755	    - name: Clean up eza tarball
756	      ansible.builtin.file:
757	        path: /tmp/eza.tar.gz
758	        state: absent
759	
760	  rescue:
761	    - name: Warn eza installation failed
762	      ansible.builtin.debug:
763	        msg: "eza installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
764	
765	    - name: Clean up eza temp files after failure
766	      ansible.builtin.file:
767	        path: "{{ item }}"
768	        state: absent
769	      loop:
770	        - /tmp/eza.tar.gz
771	
772	# --- eza (aarch64 user fallback: brew or skip — no upstream musl asset) ---
773	- name: Detect Linuxbrew for eza user fallback (Debian/Ubuntu, aarch64)
774	  when:
775	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
776	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0
777	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
778	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
779	  args:
780	    executable: /bin/bash
781	  register: eza_brew_probe
782	  changed_when: false
783	
784	- name: Install eza via Linuxbrew (user fallback, aarch64, brew available)
785	  when:
786	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
787	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0
788	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
789	    - eza_brew_probe is defined
790	    - eza_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
791	  community.general.homebrew:
792	    name: eza
793	    state: present
794	
795	- name: Warn eza cannot be installed safely (aarch64, no brew)
796	  when:
797	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
798	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0
799	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
800	    - (eza_brew_probe is not defined) or (eza_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim == '')
801	  ansible.builtin.debug:
802	    msg: >-
803	      eza skipped on aarch64: upstream publishes only `unknown-linux-gnu`
804	      tarball for aarch64 which may require a newer glibc than Jammy (2.35).
805	      Install Linuxbrew (`brew install eza`) or wait for an upstream musl
806	      arm64 build.
807	
808	# --- git-delta ---
809	# Delta can start successfully but crash when reading stdin if bat's binary
810	# theme cache was built by an incompatible bat version. Verify by actually
811	# feeding delta an empty diff, not only by checking `--version`.
812	# Glibc landscape:
813	#   - x86_64: upstream publishes `unknown-linux-musl` (static, glibc-independent).
814	#     User-level fallback now uses it (was `unknown-linux-gnu` until the
815	#     centos7-noroot.md sweep). Works on glibc 2.17.
816	#   - aarch64: only `unknown-linux-gnu` assets exist, and delta 0.19.x briefly
817	#     required glibc 2.39 (unavailable on Jammy). We therefore:
818	#       1) sudo path (apt .deb) is Debian/Ubuntu-only.
819	#       2) aarch64 falls through to Linuxbrew (`brew install git-delta`) or
820	#          skips with a clear debug message rather than silently pulling a
821	#          glibc-risky binary.
822	- name: Check if delta is installed
823	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
824	  ansible.builtin.shell: printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
825	  args:
826	    executable: /bin/bash
827	  register: delta_check
828	  changed_when: false
829	  failed_when: false
830	
831	- name: Skip git-delta on unsupported architecture
832	  when:
833	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
834	    - delta_check.rc != 0
835	    - target_architecture not in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
836	  ansible.builtin.debug:
837	    msg: "git-delta skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"
838	
839	- name: Install git-delta .deb (Debian/Ubuntu, x86_64)
840	  when:
841	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
842	    - delta_check.rc != 0
843	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
844	  become: true
845	  tags: [sudo]
846	  block:
847	    - name: Get latest delta release
848	      ansible.builtin.uri:
849	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dandavison/delta/releases/latest
850	        return_content: true
851	      register: delta_release

853	    - name: Download git-delta .deb package

856	        dest: /tmp/git-delta.deb
857	        mode: '0644'
858	        timeout: 120
859	      retries: 3
860	      delay: 5
861	
862	    - name: Install delta .deb package
863	      ansible.builtin.apt:
864	        deb: /tmp/git-delta.deb
865	
866	    - name: Clean up delta .deb

869	        state: absent

871	  rescue:

881	# --- git-delta (aarch64: brew or skip — no upstream musl asset) ---
882	- name: Detect Linuxbrew for git-delta (Debian/Ubuntu, aarch64)
883	  when:
884	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
885	    - delta_check.rc != 0
886	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
887	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
888	  args:
889	    executable: /bin/bash
890	  register: delta_brew_probe
891	  changed_when: false
892	
893	- name: Install git-delta via Linuxbrew (Debian/Ubuntu, aarch64, brew available)
894	  when:
895	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
896	    - delta_check.rc != 0
897	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
898	    - delta_brew_probe is defined
899	    - delta_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
900	  community.general.homebrew:
901	    name: git-delta
902	    state: present
903	
904	- name: Warn git-delta cannot be installed safely (aarch64, no brew)
905	  when:
906	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
907	    - delta_check.rc != 0
908	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
909	    - (delta_brew_probe is not defined) or (delta_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim == '')
910	  ansible.builtin.debug:
911	    msg: >-
912	      git-delta skipped on aarch64: upstream publishes only `unknown-linux-gnu`
913	      assets, which historically require glibc >= 2.39 and may fail on Jammy
914	      (glibc 2.35). Install Linuxbrew (`brew install git-delta`) or wait for
915	      an upstream musl arm64 build.
916	
917	# --- git-delta (user-level fallback) ---
918	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — x86_64 uses the
919	# upstream `unknown-linux-musl` tarball (glibc-independent). aarch64 still
920	# has no upstream musl; that path stays Debian-only (Linuxbrew aarch64 on
921	# CentOS 7 is not a typical setup we support).
922	- name: Re-check if delta is installed
923	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
924	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v delta && printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
925	  args:
926	    executable: /bin/bash
927	  register: delta_recheck
928	  changed_when: false
929	  failed_when: false
930	
931	- name: Install git-delta tarball (user-level, no sudo, x86_64)
932	  when:
933	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
934	    - delta_recheck.rc != 0
935	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
936	  block:
937	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (delta)
938	      ansible.builtin.file:
939	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
940	        state: directory
941	        mode: '0755'
942	
943	    - name: Get latest delta release (user)
944	      ansible.builtin.uri:
945	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dandavison/delta/releases/latest
946	        return_content: true
947	      register: delta_release_user
948	
949	    - name: Download delta musl tarball (user)
950	      # Switched from `-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` to the musl variant
951	      # so CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17) can install it without source build. The
952	      # gnu tarball historically required glibc 2.39 on aarch64 too.
953	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
954	        url: "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
955	        dest: /tmp/delta.tar.gz
956	        mode: '0644'
957	        timeout: 120
958	      retries: 3
959	      delay: 5
960	
961	    - name: Extract delta (user)
962	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
963	        src: /tmp/delta.tar.gz
964	        dest: /tmp
965	        remote_src: true
966	
967	    - name: Install delta to ~/.local/bin
968	      ansible.builtin.copy:
969	        src: "/tmp/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/delta"
970	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/delta"
971	        mode: '0755'
972	        remote_src: true
973	
974	    - name: Clean up delta temp files (user)
975	      ansible.builtin.file:
976	        path: "{{ item }}"
977	        state: absent
978	      loop:
979	        - /tmp/delta.tar.gz
980	        - "/tmp/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
981	
982	  rescue:
983	    - name: Warn git-delta (user) installation failed
984	      ansible.builtin.debug:
985	        msg: "git-delta (user) installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
986	
987	    - name: Clean up git-delta (user) temp files after failure
988	      ansible.builtin.file:
989	        path: "{{ item }}"
990	        state: absent
991	      loop:
992	        - /tmp/delta.tar.gz

999	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
1000	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
1001	  args:

1029	# --- diffnav ---
1030	- name: Check if diffnav is installed
1031	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1032	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v diffnav
1033	  register: diffnav_check
1034	  changed_when: false
1035	  failed_when: false
1036	  environment:
1037	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
1038	
1039	- name: Set diffnav release architecture
1040	  # Broadened to RedHat + decoupled from diffnav_check so the user-level
1041	  # fallback works on CentOS 7 where the sudo .deb install is skipped.
1042	  when:
1043	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1044	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
1045	    diffnav_release_arch: >-
1046	      {{
1047	        'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
1048	        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
1049	        else ''
1050	      }}
1051	
1052	- name: Skip diffnav on unsupported architecture
1053	  when:
1054	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1055	    - diffnav_check.rc != 0
1056	    - diffnav_release_arch == ''
1057	  ansible.builtin.debug:
1058	    msg: "diffnav skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"
1059	
1060	- name: Install diffnav from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
1061	  when:
1062	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1063	    - diffnav_check.rc != 0
1064	    - diffnav_release_arch != ''
1065	  become: true
1066	  tags: [sudo]
1067	  block:
1068	    - name: Get latest diffnav release
1069	      ansible.builtin.uri:
1070	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dlvhdr/diffnav/releases/latest
1071	        return_content: true
1072	      register: diffnav_release
1073	
1074	    - name: Download diffnav tarball

1076	        url: "https://github.com/dlvhdr/diffnav/releases/download/{{ diffnav_release.json.tag_name }}/diffnav_Linux_{{ diffnav_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
1077	        dest: /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1078	        mode: '0644'
1079	        timeout: 120
1080	      retries: 3
1081	      delay: 5
1082	
1083	    - name: Extract and install diffnav
1084	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
1085	        set -euo pipefail
1086	        rm -rf /tmp/diffnav-extract
1087	        mkdir -p /tmp/diffnav-extract
1088	        tar -xzf /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz -C /tmp/diffnav-extract
1089	        diffnav_bin="$(find /tmp/diffnav-extract -type f -name diffnav | head -n 1)"
1090	        install -m 0755 "$diffnav_bin" /usr/local/bin/diffnav
1091	      args:
1092	        executable: /bin/bash
1093	      changed_when: true
1094	
1095	    - name: Clean up diffnav temp files
1096	      ansible.builtin.file:
1097	        path: "{{ item }}"
1098	        state: absent
1099	      loop:
1100	        - /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1101	        - /tmp/diffnav-extract
1102	
1103	  rescue:
1104	    - name: Warn diffnav installation failed
1105	      ansible.builtin.debug:
1106	        msg: "diffnav installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
1107	
1108	    - name: Clean up diffnav temp files after failure
1109	      ansible.builtin.file:
1110	        path: "{{ item }}"
1111	        state: absent
1112	      loop:
1113	        - /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1114	        - /tmp/diffnav-extract

1293	# --- tldr ---
1294	- name: Check if tldr is installed
1295	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1296	  ansible.builtin.command: tldr --version
1297	  register: tldr_check
1298	  changed_when: false
1299	  failed_when: false
1300	
1301	- name: Check for system npm
1302	  when:
1303	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1304	    - tldr_check.rc != 0
1305	  ansible.builtin.command: command -v npm
1306	  register: system_npm_check
1307	  changed_when: false
1308	  failed_when: false
1309	
1310	- name: Install tldr via npm (Debian/Ubuntu, system-level)
1311	  when:
1312	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1313	    - tldr_check.rc != 0
1314	    - system_npm_check.rc == 0
1315	  become: true
1316	  tags: [sudo]
1317	  community.general.npm:
1318	    name: tldr
1319	    global: true
1320	    state: present
1321	  ignore_errors: true
1322	
1323	# --- tldr (user-level fallback) ---
1324	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — but note this
1325	# uses `mise exec -- npm`, and `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` omits node
1326	# on oldEL (CentOS 7) per the glibc 2.17 baseline. On EL7 mise falls back
1327	# to system node (often missing or too old) and this task no-ops via the
1328	# `mise not found` branch. Live with it; tldr is non-critical.
1329	- name: Re-check if tldr is installed
1330	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1331	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v tldr
1332	  register: tldr_recheck
1333	  changed_when: false
1334	  failed_when: false
1335	
1336	- name: Install tldr via mise npm (user-level, no sudo)
1337	  when:
1338	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1339	    - tldr_recheck.rc != 0
1340	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
1341	    if [ -x "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise" ]; then
1342	      {{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise exec -- npm install -g tldr
1343	    elif command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1344	      mise exec -- npm install -g tldr
1345	    else
1346	      echo "mise not found, skipping tldr install" >&2
1347	      exit 0
1348	    fi
1349	  args:
1350	    executable: /bin/bash
1351	  changed_when: true
1352	  ignore_errors: true
1353	
1354	# --- glow ---
1355	- name: Check if glow is installed
1356	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1357	  ansible.builtin.command: glow --version
1358	  register: glow_check
1359	  changed_when: false
1360	  failed_when: false
1361	  environment:
1362	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
1363	
1364	- name: Set glow release architecture
1365	  when:
1366	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1367	    - glow_check.rc != 0
1368	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
1369	    glow_release_arch: >-
