1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
6	#   "tyro>=0.9",
7	#   "rich>=13.9",
8	# ]
9	# ///
10	"""
11	scripts/fleet/apply.py — Run `chezmoi update --init` (or `apply` / `diff`)
12	across a fleet of remote hosts in parallel, with optional sudo password
13	injection. (Renamed from `scripts/fleet_apply.py` on 2026-05-13 alongside
14	the `fleet chezmoi` namespace refactor.)
15	
16	Why this exists:
17	    Pushing dotfile changes to N machines by hand (ssh, type password, wait,
18	    grep logs) is error-prone. This wraps that flow:
19	
20	      * Host list + connection details live in ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
21	      * Connection prefers ssh_config alias (ProxyJump, IdentityAgent, etc. all
22	        kept) — falls back to explicit hostname/user/port/identity_file.
23	      * Sudo password sources: plaintext (TOML), interactive prompt (asked once
24	        at startup), Bitwarden CLI (`bw get password <item>`), or omitted.
25	      * Per-host `no_root_machine = true` skips sudo entirely (matches the
26	        chezmoi `noRoot=true` init choice on that host).
27	      * Live Rich table of progress + per-host log files under
28	        logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
29	
30	Exit code: number of failed hosts (0 = all good, capped at 125).
31	
32	See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full schema, examples, troubleshooting.
33	"""
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import asyncio
37	import dataclasses
38	import getpass
39	import os
40	import re
41	import shlex
42	import subprocess
43	import sys
44	import time
45	import tomllib
46	from datetime import datetime, timezone
47	from pathlib import Path
48	from typing import Annotated, Literal
49	
50	import asyncssh
51	import tyro
52	from rich.console import Console
53	from rich.live import Live
54	from rich.table import Table
55	
56	
57	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	# Data model
59	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	
61	PasswordSourceType = Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]
62	
63	
64	@dataclasses.dataclass
65	class Host:
66	    """One remote machine. See machines.toml schema in docs."""
67	
68	    name: str
69	    ssh_alias: str | None = None
70	    hostname: str | None = None
71	    user: str | None = None
72	    port: int | None = None
73	    identity_file: str | None = None
74	    no_root_machine: bool = False
75	    chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
76	    # When True, bypass SSH entirely and run chezmoi as a local
77	    # subprocess on the orchestrator machine. Useful for including the
78	    # control box itself in a fleet apply (e.g. you keep your own
79	    # workstation in sync with the same `just fleet-apply` invocation).
80	    # Local hosts skip all SSH-specific config (ssh_alias/hostname/
81	    # user/port/identity_file are ignored) and reuse the caller's
82	    # ambient PATH so chezmoi_path = "auto" still works without the
83	    # remote-style PATH augmentation. Sudo password injection is
84	    # skipped — chezmoi inherits the caller's tty/sudoers state.
85	    local: bool = False
86	    extra_env: dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
87	    # Resolved later (not from TOML directly)
88	    password_source_type: PasswordSourceType = "none"
89	    password_source_arg: str | None = None  # plain value, bw item id, etc.
90	    sudo_password: str | None = None  # populated by resolve_passwords()
91	
92	
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	# TOML loading
95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	
97	DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = Path(
98	    os.environ.get("FLEET_CONFIG")
99	    or (Path.home() / ".config" / "fleet" / "machines.toml")
100	).expanduser()
101	
102	
103	def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
104	    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).
105	
106	    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
107	    `password_source` table is normalized into (type, arg) on Host.
108	    """
109	    if not path.exists():
110	        raise FileNotFoundError(
111	            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
112	            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
113	            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
114	        )
115	    with path.open("rb") as f:
116	        data = tomllib.load(f)
117	
118	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
119	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
120	    if not raw_hosts:
121	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
122	
123	    hosts: list[Host] = []
124	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
125	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
126	        name = raw.get("name")
127	        if not name:
128	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
129	        if name in seen_names:
130	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
131	        seen_names.add(name)
132	
133	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
134	        ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
135	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
136	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
137	            raise ValueError(
138	                f"{path}: host {name!r} has invalid password_source.type={ps_type!r}"
139	            )
140	        ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")
141	
142	        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
143	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
144	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
145	        host = Host(
146	            **host_kwargs,
147	            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
148	            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
149	        )
150	
151	        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
152	        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:
153	            raise ValueError(
154	                f"{path}: host {name!r} must define either `ssh_alias` "
155	                f"(preferred) or `hostname` (or set `local = true` to run "
156	                f"on the orchestrator machine without SSH)."
157	            )
158	        hosts.append(host)
159	    return hosts, defaults
160	
161	
162	
163	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	# Password resolution
165	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
166	
167	
168	def _bw_get_password(item: str) -> str:
169	    """Call `bw get password <item>`; raise on failure with a helpful message."""
170	    try:
171	        result = subprocess.run(
172	            ["bw", "get", "password", item],
173	            capture_output=True,
174	            text=True,
175	            timeout=30,
176	            check=False,
177	        )
178	    except FileNotFoundError as e:
179	        raise RuntimeError(
180	            "`bw` (Bitwarden CLI) not found in PATH — install with "
181	            "`npm install -g @bitwarden/cli` or set password_source.type to "
182	            "'plain'/'prompt'/'none'."
183	        ) from e
184	    if result.returncode != 0:
185	        stderr = (result.stderr or "").strip()
186	        raise RuntimeError(
187	            f"bw get password {item!r} failed (rc={result.returncode}): {stderr}\n"
188	            f"Hint: run `bw unlock` first; ensure BW_SESSION is exported."
189	        )
190	    return result.stdout.strip("\n")
191	
192	
193	def resolve_passwords(hosts: list[Host], console: Console) -> list[Host]:
194	    """Mutates each host.sudo_password in-place. Returns the same list.
195	
196	    For `prompt` hosts: asks once each on stdin (NOT batched — different
197	    machines may have different passwords). For `bitwarden`: one `bw` call per
198	    host. For `plain`: copies value through. For `none`: leaves None.
199	
200	    Hosts whose resolution FAILS keep sudo_password=None; run_one() then treats
201	    them as "no password available" (fail-fast at sudo phase unless
202	    no_root_machine=true).
203	    """
204	    for h in hosts:
205	        if h.password_source_type == "none":
206	            continue
207	        if h.password_source_type == "plain":
208	            h.sudo_password = h.password_source_arg or ""
209	            if not h.sudo_password:
210	                console.print(
211	                    f"[yellow]warn[/]: host {h.name!r} password_source=plain but value is empty"
212	                )
213	            continue
214	        if h.password_source_type == "prompt":
215	            try:
216	                h.sudo_password = getpass.getpass(
217	                    f"sudo password for [{h.name}] {h.user or ''}@"
218	                    f"{h.ssh_alias or h.hostname}: "
219	                )
220	            except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
221	                console.print(f"[yellow]warn[/]: host {h.name!r} prompt cancelled")
222	                h.sudo_password = None
223	            continue
224	        if h.password_source_type == "bitwarden":
225	            if not h.password_source_arg:
226	                console.print(
227	                    f"[red]error[/]: host {h.name!r} password_source=bitwarden missing `item`"
228	                )
229	                continue
230	            try:
231	                h.sudo_password = _bw_get_password(h.password_source_arg)
232	            except RuntimeError as e:
233	                console.print(f"[red]error[/]: {h.name}: {e}")
234	                h.sudo_password = None
235	    return hosts
236	
237	
238	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
239	# Remote command construction
240	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
241	
242	# Path the orchestrator writes the password to on the remote (0600, in $HOME).
243	# Picked up by sudo_session_init via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE — see the
244	# corresponding extension in scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh.
245	REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH = ".cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass"
246	# Per-run log dir on the remote. fleet-apply tees chezmoi's combined output
247	# here so a dropped SSH session doesn't lose progress visibility — `just
248	# fleet-apply-tail HOST` reads the latest file. Survives across runs (one
249	# file per timestamp); see _gc_local_logs / `--keep-logs` for retention.
250	REMOTE_LOG_DIR = ".cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs"
251	# Same layout for local hosts so --status / --tail can probe both kinds
252	# uniformly. Absolute path; the SSH side uses the relative form because
253	# the remote shell starts in $HOME.
254	LOCAL_LOG_DIR = Path.home() / ".cache" / "chezmoi-fleet" / "logs"
255	
256	
257	def build_remote_command(
258	    host: Host,
259	    mode: Literal["update", "apply", "diff"],
260	    init: bool,
261	    force: bool = False,
262	    keep_going: bool = False,
263	    run_id: str = "adhoc",
264	    keep_logs: int = 10,
265	    apply_path: str = "",
266	    branch: str = "",
267	    force_checkout: bool = False,
268	) -> str:
269	    """Build the single shell command sent over SSH.
270	
271	    Three concerns are baked in:
272	
273	    1. Sudo password injection (when host.sudo_password is set): write password
274	       to ~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass (0600 via umask 077), export
275	       CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE, run chezmoi, then `trap … EXIT` removes
276	       the pass file even if chezmoi crashes.
277	
278	    2. Pager neutralisation: `PAGER=cat` and chezmoi-specific overrides force
279	       non-paged output. ts_nas-style hosts where `bat` panics on a missing
280	       theme would otherwise hang forever in a pager subprocess (no TTY → bat
281	       still tries to spawn).
282	
283	    3. Process-group cleanup so a local Ctrl+C / SSH channel close kills the
284	       remote chezmoi tree, not just the wrapper shell:
285	         * `set -m` enables job control so each backgrounded child gets its
286	           own process group (= -$pid kills the whole tree).
287	         * `trap '… kill -TERM -$cz_pid …' INT TERM HUP` propagates the
288	           controller's signal — asyncssh sends SIGHUP when the channel
289	           closes (request_pty=True ensures the remote side delivers it).
290	         * `wait $cz_pid` then proxies chezmoi's real exit status back.
291	       Without this, an interrupted run leaves an orphan `chezmoi update`
292	       on the remote that holds the git source dir lock and burns CPU until
293	       it self-terminates.
294	    """
295	    # `--no-pager` is a chezmoi global flag — it tells chezmoi to write
296	    # paged subcommand output (diff, status) straight to stdout instead of
297	    # spawning the configured pager. Critical for non-TTY runs because
298	    # chezmoi's default pager is whatever the user configured (often bat /
299	    # less), which can panic or block forever when its own stdin/stdout
300	    # aren't a terminal. Setting `PAGER=cat` is NOT enough — chezmoi reads
301	    # its own `pager` config key and ignores PAGER.
302	    #
303	    # `chezmoi_path == "auto"` (the default) defers binary lookup to the
304	    # remote: PATH is augmented with every plausible install location
305	    # (Linuxbrew, Homebrew x86/arm64, snap, ~/.local/bin, ~/bin) so a
306	    # non-interactive shell — which doesn't source ~/.zshrc and therefore
307	    # often lacks ~/.local/bin — still finds chezmoi. To pin a specific
308	    # binary, set `chezmoi_path = "/abs/path/to/chezmoi"` per-host.
309	    # Bare "chezmoi" (no slash, no path) is treated the same as "auto" —
310	    # users who hand-wrote that value still benefit from PATH augmentation,
311	    # because rc=127 "command not found" is the most common first-run
312	    # failure on hosts where ~/.local/bin isn't in non-interactive PATH.
313	    chezmoi_path = host.chezmoi_path or "auto"
314	    if chezmoi_path == "auto" or "/" not in chezmoi_path:
315	        cz = shlex.quote(chezmoi_path if chezmoi_path != "auto" else "chezmoi")
316	        path_prefix = (
317	            'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:'
318	            '/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:'
319	            '/usr/local/bin:/snap/bin:$PATH"; '
320	        )
321	    else:
322	        cz = shlex.quote(chezmoi_path)
323	        path_prefix = ""
324	    cz_global = f"{cz} --no-pager"
325	    # `--force` makes chezmoi auto-overwrite local drift on the remote
326	    # (the "X has changed since chezmoi last wrote it" prompt) instead of
327	    # opening /dev/tty for input — we run without a PTY, so the prompt
328	    # would die with "could not open a new TTY". `--keep-going` continues
329	    # past per-file errors so one bad template doesn't abort the whole
330	    # apply. Both are off by default; opt in via CLI.
331	    #
332	    # `--force` is destructive: any hand-edits made on the remote box are
333	    # silently replaced with the canonical template render. Acceptable
334	    # for a "push the dotfiles repo to my fleet" workflow because managed
335	    # files shouldn't be edited in place.
336	    sub_flags = ""
337	    if force:
338	        sub_flags += " --force"
339	    if keep_going:
340	        sub_flags += " --keep-going"
341	    if mode == "update":
342	        sub = f"{cz_global} update{sub_flags}"
343	        if init:
344	            sub += " --init"
345	    elif mode == "apply":
346	        sub = f"{cz_global} apply{sub_flags}"
347	        # apply_path mode: scope to one target + skip run_* scripts so an
348	        # ansible / Brewfile change doesn't trigger the slow re-run when
349	        # all you wanted was to push a dotfile edit. `--exclude=scripts`
350	        # is the chezmoi knob; the path is appended last so any per-mode
351	        # flags (--force, --keep-going) come first.
352	        #
353	        # IMPORTANT: this branch deliberately bypasses `chezmoi update`,
354	        # which means the remote source dir is NOT auto-pulled. Prepend an
355	        # explicit `git pull` of the source-path so the remote checkout
356	        # has the latest commit before we re-render the target. We use
357	        # `chezmoi source-path` (no args) to discover the source dir on
358	        # the remote — works regardless of where the user installed it.
359	        # NB: when --branch is set the git prelude below replaces this
360	        # plain pull with a checkout-of-branch sequence, so we skip it
361	        # to avoid double-pulling.
362	        if apply_path and not branch:
363	            sub = (
364	                f'_src=$({cz_global} source-path) && '
365	                f'git -C "$_src" pull --ff-only --quiet && '
366	                f"{sub} --exclude=scripts {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"
367	            )
368	        elif apply_path:
369	            sub = f"{sub} --exclude=scripts {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"
370	    else:  # diff
371	        # `chezmoi diff` doesn't take --force / --keep-going — it's
372	        # read-only and never prompts.
373	        sub = f"{cz_global} diff"
374	        if apply_path:
375	            sub += f" {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"
376	
377	    # --branch BRANCH: pin the remote source dir to a feature branch
378	    # before the chezmoi invocation, so you can iterate on a topic branch
379	    # without polluting main. Default merge strategy is --ff-only (fail
380	    # loud on divergence so you notice). --force-checkout swaps in
381	    # `reset --hard origin/BRANCH` to nuke any local divergence — useful
382	    # when you're rebasing the topic branch and want hosts to follow.
383	    #
384	    # Implementation: fetch only that ref, checkout (creating local
385	    # tracking branch on first run via -B), then sync. We use chezmoi's
386	    # configured source dir (not assumed path) for portability across
387	    # hosts that installed chezmoi to different prefixes.
388	    if branch:
389	        br = shlex.quote(branch)
390	        if force_checkout:
391	            sync = f'git -C "$_src" reset --hard origin/{branch} --quiet'
392	        else:
393	            sync = f'git -C "$_src" merge --ff-only origin/{branch} --quiet'
394	        prelude = (
395	            f'_src=$({cz_global} source-path) && '
396	            f'git -C "$_src" fetch origin {br} --quiet && '
397	            f'git -C "$_src" checkout -B {br} origin/{branch} --quiet && '
398	            f"{sync}"
399	        )
400	        # If sub already starts with a `_src=…` prefix (apply_path branch
401	        # above), strip it — the prelude defines _src already.
402	        if sub.startswith("_src="):
403	            # Find the first ' && ' after _src=... and take everything after
404	            # the next chezmoi/source-path stanza. Easier: just rebuild.
405	            # The apply_path branch sets sub to "_src=… && git pull && CHEZMOI…"
406	            # — we want only the CHEZMOI part. Split on ' && ' and keep the
407	            # last segment(s).
408	            parts = sub.split(" && ", 2)
409	            sub = parts[-1] if len(parts) >= 3 else sub
410	        sub = f"{prelude} && {sub}"
411	
412	    # Belt-and-braces: if any sub-tool chezmoi invokes (git, ansible) honours
413	    # PAGER / GIT_PAGER, force them non-paged too. NB: chezmoi itself does
414	    # NOT honour these — that's why --no-pager above is required.
415	    pager_env = "PAGER=cat GIT_PAGER=cat "
416	    extra_env = " ".join(f"{k}={shlex.quote(v)}" for k, v in host.extra_env.items())
417	    env_prefix = path_prefix + pager_env + (f"{extra_env} " if extra_env else "")
418	
419	    pass_path = shlex.quote(REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH)
420	    if host.sudo_password is None:
421	        pre = ""
422	        cleanup_extra = ""
423	    else:
424	        pre = (
425	            f"umask 077; "
426	            f"mkdir -p \"$(dirname {pass_path})\"; "
427	            f"cat > {pass_path}; chmod 600 {pass_path}; "
428	            f"export CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=\"$PWD/{REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH}\"; "
429	        )
430	        cleanup_extra = f" rm -f {pass_path};"
431	
432	    # Process-tree cleanup: a `trap` on INT/TERM/HUP forwards the signal to
433	    # chezmoi's PID, then to its whole subtree via `pkill -P`. Combined with
434	    # request_pty=True on the asyncssh side (which causes SSH to deliver
435	    # SIGHUP to the remote shell when the channel closes), this guarantees a
436	    # local Ctrl+C / dropped connection actually stops chezmoi instead of
437	    # leaving an orphan that holds the source-dir git lock and burns CPU.
438	    # `wait $_cz_pid` proxies chezmoi's real exit status back to the SSH client.
439	    #
440	    # Tee to ~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/<run_id>.log via process
441	    # substitution so the controller's `--tail` mode (or a plain
442	    # `ssh HOST tail -f`) can follow progress even after the SSH session
443	    # this command was launched from disappears. `$!` after process
444	    # substitution is the BACKGROUND chezmoi job, not tee — confirmed in
445	    # bash 4+/zsh 5+ which is what we target. The `.exit` sidecar file lets
446	    # `--status` distinguish "still running" from "finished, here's the rc"
447	    # without having to pgrep again.
448	    log_path = f"{REMOTE_LOG_DIR}/{run_id}.log"
449	    exit_path = f"{REMOTE_LOG_DIR}/{run_id}.exit"
450	    log_q = shlex.quote(log_path)
451	    exit_q = shlex.quote(exit_path)
452	    log_setup = (
453	        f"mkdir -p {shlex.quote(REMOTE_LOG_DIR)}; "
454	        f"rm -f {exit_q}; "
455	    )
456	    # Log GC: keep only the N most recent .log files (and matching .exit
457	    # sentinels) in REMOTE_LOG_DIR. Runs AFTER chezmoi finishes, BEFORE
458	    # `exit $_rc`, so if it crashes the rc proxy still works. `tail -n
459	    # +N+1` selects everything past the keep window. keep_logs=0 disables.
460	    if keep_logs > 0:
461	        gc = (
462	            f"_d={shlex.quote(REMOTE_LOG_DIR)}; "
463	            f"_keep={keep_logs}; "
464	            f"ls -1t \"$_d\"/*.log 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((_keep+1)) | "
465	            f"  while read -r _f; do "
466	            f"    rm -f \"$_f\" \"${{_f%.log}}.exit\"; "
467	            f"  done; "
468	        )
469	    else:
470	        gc = ""
471	    return (
472	        f"{pre}"
473	        f"{log_setup}"
474	        f"_cleanup() {{ "
475	        f"  [ -n \"${{_cz_pid:-}}\" ] && {{ "
476	        f"    pkill -TERM -P $_cz_pid 2>/dev/null; "
477	        f"    kill -TERM $_cz_pid 2>/dev/null; "
478	        f"  }};{cleanup_extra} "
479	        f"}}; "
480	        f"trap _cleanup INT TERM HUP; "
481	        f"{env_prefix}{sub} </dev/null > >(tee -a {log_q}) 2>&1 & "
482	        f"_cz_pid=$!; "
483	        f"wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; "
484	        f"echo $_rc > {exit_q} 2>/dev/null || true; "
485	        f"{gc}"
486	        f"trap - INT TERM HUP;{cleanup_extra} "
487	        f"exit $_rc"
488	    )

492	# Per-host execution
493	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
494	
495	
496	@dataclasses.dataclass
497	class HostStatus:
498	    """Live state shared between run_one() and the Rich table renderer."""
499	
500	    host: Host
501	    # pending | connecting | running | done | failed | skipped | drift
502	    # `drift` = chezmoi exited non-zero but the only error was its inability
503	    #           to prompt for an unexpected target change while running
504	    #           non-interactively (i.e. a real drift on the remote machine
505	    #           that --keep-going skipped). Treated as a warning, not a fail.
506	    state: str = "pending"
507	    last_line: str = ""
508	    started_at: float | None = None
509	    finished_at: float | None = None
510	    rc: int | None = None
511	    log_path: Path | None = None
512	    error: str | None = None
513	    drift_files: list[str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
514	
515	
516	# Regex matching the chezmoi error emitted when --keep-going hits a target
517	# whose contents changed since chezmoi last wrote it AND there is no TTY to
518	# prompt the user with. Captured group 1 is the relative target path so we
519	# can list it in the summary. Example line:
520	#   chezmoi: .config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml: could not open a new
521	#       TTY: open /dev/tty: device not configured
522	_DRIFT_RE = re.compile(
523	    r"^chezmoi: (\S+): could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty: ",
524	)
525	
526	
527	def _classify_drift(diag_lines: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
528	    """Return (is_pure_drift, [drift_paths]).
529	
530	    `is_pure_drift` is True iff every non-blank input line matches
531	    `_DRIFT_RE`. Used by run_one()/run_one_local() to demote rc!=0 from
532	    `failed` to `drift`.
533	
534	    Callers feed the lines this should consider:
535	      * run_one_local() passes real stderr lines (chezmoi runs directly).
536	      * run_one() passes only `chezmoi:`-prefixed lines from the merged
537	        stdout+stderr stream, since the remote wrapper does
538	        `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1` and we still want to ignore git-pull
539	        progress, "Already up to date.", etc.
540	
541	    Conservative on purpose: any unrecognised line means we keep the
542	    `failed` classification so real errors are not silently swallowed.
543	    """
544	    drift_paths: list[str] = []
545	    for raw in diag_lines:
546	        line = raw.strip()
547	        if not line:
548	            continue
549	        m = _DRIFT_RE.match(line)
550	        if m:
551	            drift_paths.append(m.group(1))
552	            continue
553	        # Anything else in stderr → not a pure-drift case.
554	        return False, []
555	    return bool(drift_paths), drift_paths
556	
557	
558	def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
559	    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs.
560	
561	    asyncssh reads ~/.ssh/config by default for the `host` arg. When ssh_alias
562	    is set we pass it as `host` and let asyncssh resolve hostname/user/port/
563	    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.
564	    """
565	    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
566	    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
567	    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
568	    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
569	    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
570	    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
571	    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
572	    if host.user:
573	        kwargs["username"] = host.user
574	    if host.port:
575	        kwargs["port"] = host.port
576	    if host.identity_file:
577	        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
578	    return kwargs
579	
580	
581	def _gc_local_logs(keep: int) -> None:
582	    """Trim LOCAL_LOG_DIR to the `keep` most recent .log files (+ .exit).
583	
584	    Mirrors the remote GC done by build_remote_command. keep<=0 disables.
585	    Silent on errors (best-effort cleanup).
586	    """
587	    if keep <= 0:
588	        return
589	    try:
590	        logs = sorted(
591	            LOCAL_LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"),
592	            key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
593	            reverse=True,
594	        )
595	    except OSError:
596	        return
597	    for stale in logs[keep:]:
598	        for ext in (".log", ".exit"):
599	            try:
600	                (LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{stale.stem}{ext}").unlink(missing_ok=True)
601	            except OSError:
602	                pass
603	
604	
605	async def run_one_local(
606	    status: HostStatus,
607	    log_dir: Path,
608	    mode: Literal["update", "apply", "diff"],
609	    init: bool,
610	    command_timeout: int,
611	    force: bool = False,
612	    keep_going: bool = False,
613	    keep_logs: int = 10,
614	    apply_path: str = "",
615	    branch_warning: str = "",
616	) -> None:
617	    """Execute one local host: spawn `chezmoi` directly via subprocess.
618	
619	    Bypasses asyncssh entirely. Reuses the orchestrator's PATH, sudoers
620	    state (no password injection — chezmoi inherits the parent tty),
621	    and `~/.local/share/chezmoi` source. Output is streamed to the same
622	    per-host log file used by SSH hosts so the rich live table is
623	    consistent. command_timeout is honoured via asyncio.wait_for.
624	    """
625	    host = status.host
626	    log_path = log_dir / f"{host.name}.log"
627	    status.log_path = log_path
628	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
629	    status.started_at = loop.time()
630	
631	    # Build a flat argv (no shell) so we don't need quoting / pager dance.
632	    chezmoi_bin = host.chezmoi_path if (host.chezmoi_path and host.chezmoi_path != "auto") else "chezmoi"
633	    argv: list[str] = [chezmoi_bin, "--no-pager"]
634	    if mode == "update":
635	        argv.append("update")
636	        if init:
637	            argv.append("--init")
638	    elif mode == "apply":
639	        argv.append("apply")
640	    else:
641	        argv.append("diff")
642	    if mode != "diff":
643	        if force:
644	            argv.append("--force")
645	        if keep_going:
646	            argv.append("--keep-going")
647	    # apply_path mode: skip run_* scripts and scope to the single target.
648	    # Mirrors build_remote_command's apply_path branch above.
649	    if apply_path and mode == "apply":
650	        argv.extend(["--exclude=scripts", apply_path])
651	    elif apply_path and mode == "diff":
652	        argv.append(apply_path)
653	
654	    log_fp = log_path.open("w", buffering=1)
655	    log_fp.write(f"# fleet-apply host={host.name} mode={mode} init={init} (local)\n")
656	    if branch_warning:
657	        # Surface the skip explicitly in the log so users grepping for
658	        # "branch" don't think the flag was honoured silently.
659	        log_fp.write(
660	            f"# warning: --branch={branch_warning} ignored for local host "
661	            f"(local source is your editor's working tree; switch branches "
662	            f"manually with git if you really mean to)\n"
663	        )
664	    log_fp.write(f"# argv: {argv}\n\n")
665	
666	    # Mirror the remote layout: write a second copy to LOCAL_LOG_DIR/<run_id>.log
667	    # so `just fleet-apply-status` / `--tail self` (= local) can find this run
668	    # using the same code path as SSH hosts. Also drop a .exit sentinel when
669	    # done. log_dir.name is the timestamp like "20260422T140446Z".
670	    LOCAL_LOG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
671	    cache_log = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{log_dir.name}.log"
672	    cache_exit = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{log_dir.name}.exit"
673	    cache_exit.unlink(missing_ok=True)
674	    cache_fp = cache_log.open("w", buffering=1)
675	
676	    env = {**os.environ, "PAGER": "cat", "GIT_PAGER": "cat", **host.extra_env}
677	    proc = None
678	    stderr_lines: list[str] = []
679	    try:
680	        status.state = "running"
681	        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
682	            *argv,
683	            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
684	            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
685	            env=env,
686	        )
687	
688	        async def _drain(stream: asyncio.StreamReader, prefix: str) -> None:
689	            while True:
690	                line = await stream.readline()
691	                if not line:
692	                    return
693	                text = line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\n")
694	                log_fp.write(f"[{prefix}] {text}\n")
695	                cache_fp.write(f"{text}\n")  # plain combined for tail -F
696	                status.last_line = text
697	                if prefix == "err":
698	                    stderr_lines.append(text)
699	
700	        async with asyncio.timeout(command_timeout):
701	            # Spawn the three coroutines but key the wait on a kill -0 poll —
702	            # NOT on proc.wait() OR an asyncio.gather of all three. Reason:
703	            # chezmoi's run_onchange_* scripts (ansible, brew bundle, mas,
704	            # etc.) routinely leave background children that inherit our
705	            # stdout/stderr fds and outlive their parent script.
706	            #
707	            # Two layers of asyncio quirk make this tricky:
708	            #   1. asyncio.gather(_drain, _drain, proc.wait) blocks because
709	            #      _drain waits on stream EOF, which only fires when ALL fd
710	            #      holders close — orphan grandchildren never close ours.
711	            #   2. proc.wait() ALONE also blocks: asyncio's
712	            #      BaseSubprocessTransport._try_finish only fires
713	            #      _process_exited when proc.returncode is set AND all
714	            #      stdin/stdout/stderr pipes are closed. So even
715	            #      `await proc.wait()` waits for the orphans.
716	            #
717	            # Workaround: poll `os.kill(pid, 0)` (signal 0 = existence check,
718	            # doesn't actually signal) at 100ms intervals. When that throws
719	            # ProcessLookupError, chezmoi itself is gone — the orphans are
720	            # someone else's problem. We don't waitpid() directly because
721	            # asyncio's child watcher owns the zombie reap.
722	            #
723	            # See pitfalls/fleet-apply-self-stuck-running.md for the full
724	            # debugging story including the failed first-fix attempt.
725	            stdout_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain(proc.stdout, "out"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
726	            stderr_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain(proc.stderr, "err"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
727	
728	            async def _wait_for_chezmoi_exit() -> None:
729	                while True:
730	                    try:
731	                        os.kill(proc.pid, 0)
732	                        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
733	                    except ProcessLookupError:
734	                        # chezmoi is gone. Give asyncio's watcher up to 5s to
735	                        # set returncode (it'll do so once the SIGCHLD fires
736	                        # and the child watcher reaps).
737	                        for _ in range(50):
738	                            if proc.returncode is not None:
739	                                return
740	                            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
741	                        return
742	
743	            # Phase 1: wait for chezmoi itself to exit (not the orphans).
744	            await _wait_for_chezmoi_exit()
745	            # Phase 2: give drains a short grace period to flush any
746	            # buffered output that's already in flight, then cancel them.
747	            # 5s is enough for any sane buffer; orphan-held pipes will
748	            # never EOF so we MUST cancel rather than wait.
749	            grace = 5.0
750	            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(
751	                [stdout_task, stderr_task],
752	                timeout=grace,
753	                return_when=asyncio.ALL_COMPLETED,
754	            )
755	            for task in pending:
756	                task.cancel()
757	            if pending:
758	                await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
759	                # Note for future debugging: if pending is non-empty,
760	                # an orphan child of chezmoi is holding our pipes open.
761	                # Most common offenders on macOS: brew bundle, mas
762	                # install, ansible homebrew tasks. Use lsof -p $$ |
763	                # grep -i pipe + pgrep -af 'brew|mas|ansible' to find
764	                # them. This is benign — chezmoi's exit code is correct.
765	                log_fp.write(
766	                    f"\n# fleet-apply: {len(pending)} stream(s) still open "
767	                    f"{grace}s after chezmoi exit (orphan child holding "
768	                    f"stdout/stderr fds — see pitfalls/"
769	                    f"fleet-apply-self-stuck-running.md). Output below "
770	                    f"this point may be truncated.\n"
771	                )
772	            # If asyncio still hasn't set returncode (very rare — child
773	            # watcher race), reap manually so status.rc isn't None.
774	            if proc.returncode is None:
775	                try:
776	                    pid, raw_status = os.waitpid(proc.pid, os.WNOHANG)
777	                    if pid != 0 and hasattr(proc, "_transport"):
778	                        proc._transport._returncode = (  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
779	                            os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(raw_status)
780	                        )
781	                except (ChildProcessError, AttributeError, OSError):
782	                    pass
783	        status.rc = proc.returncode or 0
784	        if status.rc == 0:
785	            status.state = "done"
786	        else:
787	            is_drift, paths = _classify_drift(stderr_lines)
788	            if is_drift:
789	                status.state = "drift"
790	                status.drift_files = paths
791	            else:
792	                status.state = "failed"
793	    except TimeoutError:
794	        status.state = "failed"
795	        status.rc = -1
796	        status.error = f"command_timeout {command_timeout}s exceeded"
797	        if proc and proc.returncode is None:
798	            proc.terminate()
799	            try:
800	                await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=5)
801	            except TimeoutError:
802	                proc.kill()
803	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
804	        status.state = "failed"
805	        status.rc = -1
806	        status.error = str(e)
807	        log_fp.write(f"\n# exception: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\n")
808	    finally:
809	        # Freeze elapsed by stamping finished_at — the live renderer keys
810	        # off this field to stop the clock (see _render_table). Setting a
811	        # bare `status.elapsed` attr (the previous bug) was a no-op because
812	        # HostStatus doesn't declare it AND the renderer never reads it,
813	        # so the `self` row kept ticking even after state=done.
814	        status.finished_at = loop.time()
815	        log_fp.close()
816	        cache_fp.close()
817	        # Write the sentinel last so a `--status` poll sees the rc only
818	        # after the cache log has been fully flushed (avoids the race
819	        # where a probe sees "finished" but tail -F is still mid-line).
820	        try:
821	            cache_exit.write_text(f"{status.rc if status.rc is not None else -1}\n")
822	        except OSError:
823	            pass
824	        # GC after writing sentinel so the just-finished run is itself
825	        # in the keep window.
826	        _gc_local_logs(keep_logs)
827	
828	
829	async def run_one(
830	    status: HostStatus,
831	    log_dir: Path,
832	    mode: Literal["update", "apply", "diff"],
833	    init: bool,
834	    connect_timeout: int,
835	    command_timeout: int,
836	    force: bool = False,
837	    keep_going: bool = False,
838	    keep_logs: int = 10,
839	    apply_path: str = "",
840	    branch: str = "",
841	    force_checkout: bool = False,
842	) -> None:
843	    """Execute one host: connect, stream output to log + status, set rc/state."""
844	    host = status.host
845	    if host.local:
846	        # --branch is intentionally NOT honoured for local hosts: the local
847	        # source dir IS your editor's working tree, switching it under your
848	        # feet would be hostile. Warn (via the log) but continue with the
849	        # local working tree as-is.
850	        await run_one_local(
851	            status, log_dir, mode, init, command_timeout,
852	            force=force, keep_going=keep_going, keep_logs=keep_logs,
853	            apply_path=apply_path, branch_warning=branch,
854	        )
855	        return
856	    log_path = log_dir / f"{host.name}.log"
857	    status.log_path = log_path
858	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
859	    status.started_at = loop.time()
860	
861	    cmd = build_remote_command(
862	        host, mode=mode, init=init, force=force, keep_going=keep_going,
863	        run_id=log_dir.name, keep_logs=keep_logs, apply_path=apply_path,
864	        branch=branch, force_checkout=force_checkout,
865	    )
866	    log_fp = log_path.open("w", buffering=1)  # line-buffered
867	    log_fp.write(f"# fleet-apply host={host.name} mode={mode} init={init}\n")
868	    log_fp.write(f"# remote-cmd: {cmd}\n\n")
869	
870	    proc = None
871	    conn = None
872	    try:
873	        status.state = "connecting"
874	        async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
875	            conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(host))
876	        try:
877	            status.state = "running"
878	            # Feed password (if any) via stdin: build_remote_command's `cat >`
879	            # reads exactly until EOF, so we send the password line then EOF.
880	            # asyncssh streams default to text mode (encoding='utf-8'); we
881	            # write str, not bytes — passing bytes triggers
882	            # `TypeError: utf_8_encode() argument 1 must be str, not bytes`.
883	            stdin_text = (host.sudo_password + "\n") if host.sudo_password else ""
884	            # NB: we deliberately do NOT request a PTY here. Two reasons:
885	            #   1. With a PTY, the wrapper's `cat > sudo.pass` reads from a
886	            #      TTY where stdin EOF requires a literal Ctrl+D byte; our
887	            #      `proc.stdin.write_eof()` becomes a no-op and `cat` hangs.
888	            #   2. PTY-attached chezmoi may re-enable colored output / sniff
889	            #      the terminal width. PAGER=cat already covers the pager
890	            #      side; lack-of-TTY makes the rest behave like CI.
891	            # Cleanup on local Ctrl+C / timeout is handled by:
892	            #   * Wrapper's `trap … pkill -TERM -P $_cz_pid` (in build_remote_command).
893	            #   * Explicit `proc.terminate()` + `conn.close()` in the
894	            #     except/finally clauses below — closing the SSH channel
895	            #     causes the remote shell to get SIGPIPE on its next write,
896	            #     and the wrapper's trap fires.
897	            proc = await conn.create_process(cmd, stdin=asyncssh.PIPE)
898	            if stdin_text:
899	                proc.stdin.write(stdin_text)
900	            proc.stdin.write_eof()
901	
902	            # The remote wrapper does `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1`, so chezmoi's
903	            # stderr is merged into stdout before asyncssh sees it — i.e.
904	            # `proc.stderr` is effectively always empty here. To classify
905	            # drift we collect chezmoi's own diagnostic lines (those
906	            # prefixed with `chezmoi:`) from BOTH streams. Non-chezmoi
907	            # output (git pull progress, "Already up to date.", etc.) is
908	            # excluded so it doesn't trip _classify_drift's conservative
909	            # "any unrecognised line → failed" rule. See pitfalls notes
910	            # and CLAUDE.md "Process substitution + sentinel are
911	            # load-bearing" — we cannot un-merge the streams.
912	            diag_lines: list[str] = []
913	
914	            async def _drain(stream, label: str) -> None:
915	                async for line in stream:
916	                    text = line.rstrip("\n")
917	                    log_fp.write(f"[{label}] {text}\n")
918	                    if text.strip():
919	                        status.last_line = text[:120]
920	                    if text.lstrip().startswith("chezmoi:"):
921	                        diag_lines.append(text)
922	
923	            async with asyncio.timeout(command_timeout):
924	                await asyncio.gather(
925	                    _drain(proc.stdout, "out"),
926	                    _drain(proc.stderr, "err"),
927	                )
928	                result = await proc.wait()
929	            status.rc = result.exit_status if result.exit_status is not None else 1
930	            if status.rc == 0:
931	                status.state = "done"
932	            else:
933	                is_drift, paths = _classify_drift(diag_lines)
934	                if is_drift:
935	                    status.state = "drift"
936	                    status.drift_files = paths
937	                else:
938	                    status.state = "failed"
939	        finally:
940	            if conn is not None:
941	                conn.close()
942	                try:
943	                    await conn.wait_closed()
944	                except Exception:
945	                    pass
946	    except asyncio.CancelledError:
947	        # User Ctrl+C or task-group cancellation: best-effort terminate the
948	        # remote process before re-raising. proc.terminate() sends SIGTERM
949	        # via the SSH channel; closing the connection then triggers SIGHUP
950	        # on the remote shell as a belt-and-braces backstop.
951	        status.state = "failed"
952	        status.error = "cancelled by controller"
953	        log_fp.write(f"\n[fleet-apply] CANCELLED: terminating remote process\n")
954	        if proc is not None:
955	            try:
956	                proc.terminate()
957	            except Exception:
958	                pass
959	        if conn is not None:
960	            try:
961	                conn.close()
962	            except Exception:
963	                pass
964	        raise
965	    except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
966	        status.state = "failed"
967	        status.rc = status.rc or 1
968	        status.error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
969	        log_fp.write(f"\n[fleet-apply] FAILED: {status.error}\n")
970	        # If timeout fired while chezmoi was still running, terminate it so
971	        # we don't leave an orphan on the remote.
972	        if proc is not None and proc.exit_status is None:
973	            try:
974	                proc.terminate()
975	            except Exception:
976	                pass
977	    finally:
978	        status.finished_at = loop.time()
979	        log_fp.close()
980

982	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
983	# Live table renderer + summary
984	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
985	
986	_STATE_STYLE = {
987	    "pending": "dim",
988	    "connecting": "cyan",
989	    "running": "yellow",
990	    "done": "green",
991	    "failed": "red bold",
992	    "skipped": "magenta",
993	    "drift": "yellow bold",
994	}
995	
996	
997	def _render_table(statuses: list[HostStatus], elapsed_now: float) -> Table:
998	    table = Table(title="fleet-apply", expand=True)
999	    table.add_column("host", style="bold")
1000	    table.add_column("state")
1001	    table.add_column("elapsed", justify="right")
1002	    table.add_column("rc", justify="right")
1003	    table.add_column("last", overflow="ellipsis", max_width=80)
1004	    for s in statuses:
1005	        if s.started_at is None:
1006	            elapsed = "-"
1007	        else:
1008	            end = s.finished_at if s.finished_at is not None else elapsed_now
1009	            elapsed = f"{end - s.started_at:5.1f}s"
1010	        rc = "-" if s.rc is None else str(s.rc)
1011	        style = _STATE_STYLE.get(s.state, "white")
1012	        table.add_row(
1013	            s.host.name,
1014	            f"[{style}]{s.state}[/]",
1015	            elapsed,
1016	            rc,
1017	            s.last_line,
1018	        )
1019	    return table
1020	
1021	
1022	async def _live_render_loop(
1023	    statuses: list[HostStatus], live: Live, stop_event: asyncio.Event
1024	) -> None:
1025	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
1026	    while not stop_event.is_set():
1027	        live.update(_render_table(statuses, loop.time()))
1028	        try:
1029	            await asyncio.wait_for(stop_event.wait(), timeout=0.4)
1030	        except TimeoutError:
1031	            pass
1032	    live.update(_render_table(statuses, loop.time()))
1033	
1034	
1035	def _print_summary(console: Console, statuses: list[HostStatus]) -> int:
1036	    """Print summary; return number of failed hosts.
1037	
1038	    `drift` hosts are reported as warnings but do NOT count toward the
1039	    return value — a drift means chezmoi successfully ran every other file
1040	    and only refused to overwrite a hand-edited target. The user is expected
1041	    to resolve them manually (re-run with --force, or merge changes back to
1042	    source). See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md → Conflict handling.
1043	    """
1044	    fails = [s for s in statuses if s.state == "failed"]
1045	    skips = [s for s in statuses if s.state == "skipped"]
1046	    drifts = [s for s in statuses if s.state == "drift"]
1047	    console.print()
1048	    console.print(
1049	        f"[bold]Summary[/]: {len(statuses)} hosts, "
1050	        f"[green]{sum(1 for s in statuses if s.state == 'done')} ok[/], "
1051	        f"[red]{len(fails)} failed[/], "
1052	        f"[yellow]{len(drifts)} drift[/], "
1053	        f"[magenta]{len(skips)} skipped[/]"
1054	    )
1055	    for s in fails:
1056	        console.print(
1057	            f"  [red]✗[/] {s.host.name}  rc={s.rc}  "
1058	            f"log=[cyan]{s.log_path}[/]"
1059	            + (f"  err={s.error}" if s.error else "")
1060	        )
1061	    for s in drifts:
1062	        files = ", ".join(s.drift_files) if s.drift_files else "?"
1063	        console.print(
1064	            f"  [yellow]⚠[/] {s.host.name}  drift in: {files}  "
1065	            f"log=[cyan]{s.log_path}[/]  "
1066	            f"[dim](resolve: --force, or sync edits back to source)[/]"
1067	        )
1068	    for s in skips:
1069	        console.print(f"  [magenta]·[/] {s.host.name}  reason={s.error or 'skipped'}")
1070	    return len(fails)
1071
