```text
1	# Fleet apply — multi-host `chezmoi update` orchestrator
2	
3	> **TL;DR** — `just fleet-apply` runs `chezmoi update --init` on every host
4	> listed in `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, in parallel, with optional sudo
5	> password injection sourced from plaintext / interactive prompt / Bitwarden
6	> CLI. Per-host logs land under `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`
7	> and the process exits with the number of failed hosts (capped at 125).
8	>
9	> **Before applying, run [`just fleet-status`](#readiness-probe-just-fleet-status)** — a read-only pre-flight probe that predicts what `fleet-apply` would do per host (up-to-date / behind / drift / busy / toml-mismatch / not-init / unreachable / ...).
10	
11	Implementation: [`scripts/fleet/apply.py`](../../scripts/fleet/apply.py)
12	(uv inline-script: `asyncssh` + `tyro` + `rich`).
13	
14	See also: [fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md](fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md) for an
15	archaeological comparison against the author's 2018-era Fabric `fabfile.py`
16	on RaspPi-Cluster — same problem shape, ~7 years of operational lessons
17	encoded into the current implementation.
18	
19	## The fleet-* command family at a glance
20	
21	The fleet- recipes split into **three layers** of concern. Pick the right one based on what you want to do:
22	
23	| Recipe | What it does | Side effects | When to use |
24	|---|---|---|---|
25	| `just fleet-edit` | Open `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` in `$EDITOR` (seeds an empty template on first run) | Edits inventory file only | First-time setup, adding/removing hosts |
26	| `just fleet-status` | **Pre-flight readiness probe** — predicts what `fleet-apply` would do per host | None (read-only, ~1.5s/host) | **Before** `fleet-apply`, to triage which hosts need attention |
27	| `just fleet-status-quick` | Same as `fleet-status` but skips remote `git fetch` (~0.5s/host) | None | Offline / quick re-check |
28	| `just fleet-apply-dry-run` | Run `chezmoi diff` on every host (full template render comparison) | Reads remote source dir; no writes | Detailed file-by-file preview after `fleet-status` flagged something |
29	| `just fleet-diff HOST` | `chezmoi diff` on ONE host, serial output | None | Inspecting exactly what one host would change |
30	| `just fleet-apply` | `chezmoi update --init` on every host (= `git pull` + re-render `chezmoi.toml` + `apply` + run_* scripts) | **Mutates remotes** | The actual deploy |
31	| `just fleet-apply-file PATH` | `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` on every host (skips ansible / Brewfile) | Mutates only that one target | Vibe loop — fast feedback for one dotfile |
32	| `just fleet-apply-branch BRANCH` | Pin remotes to a feature branch before applying | Mutates remotes + checks out branch on remote source dir | Iterating on a topic branch across the fleet |
33	| `just fleet-apply-one HOST` | Apply to a single host in `--serial` mode (debug-friendly output) | Mutates that host | Targeted apply / debugging |
34	| `just fleet-apply-status` | **Process-liveness probe** — is a chezmoi/ansible run still going on each host? | None (read-only) | After Ctrl+C'ing controller, to see which remotes are still busy |
35	| `just fleet-apply-watch` | Same as `fleet-apply-status` but polls every 10s until everyone idle | None | Passive "wait for fleet to settle" cursor |
36	| `just fleet-apply-tail HOST` | Live-tail the latest fleet-apply log on `HOST` over a fresh SSH session | None | Re-attach to a still-running run after Ctrl+C |
37	| `just fleet-apply-compact` | Post-mortem summary across the fleet (final task, runtime, slow tasks, exit code) | None (reads remote logs) | After a finished run, when per-host `--tail` is too noisy |
38	| `just fleet-apply-kill` | `pkill -TERM` then `-KILL` chezmoi/ansible on every host | **Kills processes** | Cleanup after Ctrl+C left orphans |
39	
40	> **Common naming confusion**: `fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`. The first is a pre-apply readiness probe ("would `fleet-apply` succeed right now?"), the second is a process-liveness probe ("is a `fleet-apply` still running?"). They answer different questions and are usually used in different phases of your workflow.
41	
42	### Typical workflows
43	
44	```bash
45	# Daily: push to repo, then deploy.
46	git push
47	just fleet-status              # pre-flight check — anything need attention?
48	just fleet-apply               # actual deploy
49	
50	# Vibe loop: edit one file, push, fast-apply across fleet.
51	git add .config/zsh/aliases.zsh && git commit -m "..." && git push
52	just fleet-apply-file .config/zsh/aliases.zsh
53	
54	# After Ctrl+C'ing a long fleet-apply: where am I?
55	just fleet-apply-status        # which hosts still running?
56	just fleet-apply-watch         # wait until everyone idle
57	just fleet-apply-tail lab-box  # re-attach to one host's log
58	just fleet-apply-kill          # nuke leftover orphans
59	
60	# After fleet-apply finished, want a summary:
61	just fleet-apply-compact
62	```
63	
64	## Umbrella `fleet` binary
65	
66	`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` (deployed as `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet`) is a
67	thin umbrella that exposes the same operations as the `just fleet-*` recipes
68	under a `fleet chezmoi <action>` namespace, plus generic primitives
69	`fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` / `fleet exec` that work on
70	any host regardless of deploy tool. The advantage over `just`: it works
71	from any cwd, not just inside the chezmoi source tree.
72	
73	**The bare top-level forms `fleet apply` / `status` / `diff` / `tail` /
74	`kill` / `compact` were removed on 2026-05-13** so the top level stays
75	reserved for generic deploy-tool-agnostic primitives. Chezmoi-specific
76	actions now live under `fleet chezmoi <action>`. The `just fleet-*`
77	recipes are unaffected — they call `scripts/fleet/apply.py` directly
78	with its underlying flags.
79	
80	| Umbrella subcommand | Equivalent `just` recipe |
81	|---|---|
82	| `fleet chezmoi apply [...]` | `just fleet-apply` (and `fleet-apply-dry-run`, `fleet-apply-one`, `fleet-apply-file`, `fleet-apply-branch[-force]`) |
83	| `fleet chezmoi status` | `just fleet-status` (readiness probe) |
84	| `fleet chezmoi status --quick` | `just fleet-status-quick` |
85	| `fleet chezmoi status --live` | `just fleet-apply-status` (process-liveness probe) |
86	| `fleet chezmoi status --live --watch 10` | `just fleet-apply-watch` |
87	| `fleet chezmoi diff HOST` | `just fleet-diff HOST` |
88	| `fleet chezmoi tail HOST[:RUN_ID]` | `just fleet-apply-tail HOST` |
89	| `fleet chezmoi kill` | `just fleet-apply-kill` |
90	| `fleet chezmoi compact` | `just fleet-apply-compact` |
91	| `fleet edit` | `just fleet-edit` |
92	| `fleet tmux [...]` | (new) — see below |
93	| `fleet info [...]` | (new) — see below |
94	| `fleet pueue [...]` | (new) — cross-host pueue queue summary; `--ai` for cleanability + recovery hints via local `pqsum`. See [docs/tools/pueue.md](../tools/pueue.md). |
95	| `fleet exec [OPTS] -- CMD [...]` | (new) — cross-host argv-list command runner. Argv after `--` is safe by default (no shell expansion). `--shell bash\|zsh` for pipes/globs, `--login` for rc-loaded env, `--ai` for succeeded/differed/failed classification. See [docs/tools/fleet-exec.md](../tools/fleet-exec.md). |
96	| `fleet hosts [NAME\|--list*]` | (new) — TV-style picker for SSH'ing into a fleet host. Backed by `tv fleet-hosts` (cable shells out to `fleet hosts --list-tsv` / `--describe` / NAME). `fleet hosts NAME` skips the picker; `--list-tsv` / `--list-json` for scripts. See [docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md](../tools/fleet-hosts.md). |
97	
98	The umbrella discovers the chezmoi source dir at runtime via `chezmoi
99	source-path` (falls back to `~/.local/share/chezmoi`) so it can `import` the
100	shared `scripts/fleet/` package and the legacy `scripts/fleet/apply.py`. From
101	inside the source tree, `just fleet *ARGS` invokes the same binary directly
102	(works before the first `chezmoi apply` lands `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet`).
103	
104	The existing `just fleet-*` recipes still call `./scripts/fleet/apply.py`
105	directly and are unaffected by the umbrella — they remain the muscle-memory
106	path for repo work. Pick whichever feels right: same code under the hood.
107	
108	### Note on `fleet chezmoi status` overload
109	
110	`fleet chezmoi status` has two modes. Default (`fleet chezmoi status` /
111	`--quick`) is the **pre-flight readiness probe** — read-only, ~1.5s/host,
112	predicts what `fleet chezmoi apply` would do. Adding `--live` flips it to
113	the **process-liveness probe** — does each host have a chezmoi/ansible
114	run in flight right now?
115	The same overload is what `just fleet-status` vs `just fleet-apply-status`
116	expresses across two recipe names; the umbrella collapses it under one
117	subcommand because both flavors answer "what is the state of `apply` on
118	each host" — just at different time horizons (would-it-succeed vs
119	is-it-running).
120	
121	## `fleet tmux` — cross-host tmux session summary
122	
123	Quick "what's open where" across the fleet:
124	
125	```bash
126	fleet tmux                                  # all hosts, default Rich table
127	fleet tmux --hosts self,ts_nas              # subset
128	fleet tmux --deep                           # include pane tails (slower)
129	fleet tmux --json                           # pipeable per-host JSON
130	```
131	
132	Per-host execution strategy (`scripts/fleet/tmux.py`):
133	
134	1. **Prefer**: invoke remote `~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json`
135	   (chezmoi deploys this on every managed host). Emits the `Session` / `Window`
136	   dataclasses as JSON — same schema `tsum` uses locally.
137	2. **Fallback**: run raw `tmux list-sessions -F ...` + `tmux list-windows -a -F ...`
138	   over SSH, then reconstruct the same JSON shape locally. Used when the `.py`
139	   isn't deployed (e.g. minimal host) or fails (e.g. version mismatch).
140	3. **None**: host has no tmux server / no tmux installed → row shows `0`
141	   sessions with `source=none`.
142	4. **N/A**: host unreachable → row renders `N/A` with the SSH error class,
143	   and the rest of the fleet keeps going.
144	
145	Output columns: `HOST | SOURCE | SESSIONS | WINDOWS | ATTACHED | LAST_ATTACHED |
146	TOP_SESSION | ms`. `SOURCE` colors hint at the path used: green=py,
147	yellow=raw, dim=none, red=N/A.
148	
149	**Not yet implemented**: `--with-summary` (LLM aggregate across hosts). Stub
150	that errors out with a hint to use `tsum` per-host or pipe `--json` to an
151	external tool.
152	
153	**Cross-file invariant** (from `CLAUDE.md`): if you add a field to the
154	`Session` / `Window` dataclass in
155	`dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`, the raw-fallback parser
156	in `scripts/fleet/tmux.py:_parse_raw` MUST be updated to reconstruct it.
157	
158	## `fleet info` — cross-host system status
159	
160	Curated 8-column snapshot of every host: OS, CPU, RAM, disk, load, uptime,
161	docker containers, chezmoi drift.
162	
163	```bash
164	fleet info                                   # default curated view, 8 modules
165	fleet info --hosts self                      # subset
166	fleet info --modules cpu,mem,disk            # only these
167	fleet info --full                            # all modules (+ gpu, network)
168	fleet info --ff                              # also dump fastfetch JSON per host
169	fleet info --json | jq .                     # pipeable
170	```
171	
172	**Module catalog** (each gracefully degrades to `—` when the underlying tool
173	is missing — no GPU, no docker, no chezmoi on the host, etc.):
174	
175	| Module | Linux source | macOS source |
176	|---|---|---|
177	| `os` | `lsb_release -ds` or `/etc/os-release` `PRETTY_NAME` | `sw_vers` |
178	| `cpu` | `/proc/cpuinfo` model name + `nproc` | `sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string` + `hw.ncpu` |
179	| `mem` | `/proc/meminfo` (`MemTotal` - `MemAvailable`) | `sysctl hw.memsize` + `vm_stat` pages |
180	| `disk` | `df -k /` (root partition) | same (POSIX) |
181	| `load` | `/proc/loadavg` | `sysctl vm.loadavg` |
182	| `uptime` | `/proc/uptime` | `date +%s` - `sysctl kern.boottime` |
183	| `docker` | `docker ps -q \| wc -l` (running + total) | same |
184	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi status` line count + commits behind | same |
185	| `gpu` (extra) | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.used,memory.total` | `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` chipset |
186	| `network` (extra) | `hostname -f` + `hostname -I` | `hostname` + `ipconfig getifaddr en0` |
187	| (with `--ff`) | `fastfetch --format json` (full dump appended per host) | same |
188	
189	The probe is one bash blob per host: `MOD_<name>=<value>` (or `ERR:<msg>`)
190	lines parsed back into structured Python objects. Per-module failure inside a
191	host is isolated (row stays alive); per-host SSH failure renders the whole
192	row as `N/A`.
193	
194	Exit code = number of hosts that failed end-to-end (capped at 125).
195	
196	## When to use
197	
198	You edited dotfiles on the workstation, pushed to the repo's git remote, and
199	now want every laptop / VM / lab box to pick up the change without sshing into
200	each one and typing the sudo password by hand.
201	
202	## When NOT to use
203	
204	- This tool **does not** push the dotfiles repo itself — every remote runs
205	  `chezmoi update`, which does `git pull` on the remote's source dir. Your
206	  changes must already be reachable by the remotes (push to GitHub / your
207	  internal git host first).
208	- It does not run `just upgrade-*` on remotes. That's a separate concern; this
209	  tool stays scoped to chezmoi apply.
210	- It does not provision new hosts. Each remote must already have `chezmoi`
211	  installed and `chezmoi init` completed at least once.
212	
213	## Readiness probe (`just fleet-status`)
214	
215	`fleet-apply` defaults to `chezmoi update --init`, which is **three things in
216	sequence** under the hood:
217	
218	1. `git -C <source> pull` — bring in new template commits
219	2. `chezmoi init` — re-render `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` (re-evaluates `promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` calls; **NEW prompt keys without saved answers will fail non-interactively** with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY`)
220	3. `chezmoi apply` — render templates, write targets, run `run_*` scripts (ansible, Brewfile, etc.)
221	
222	The readiness probe inspects each host once over SSH and predicts what each of
223	those three sub-steps would do, **without changing anything**. Cheaper than
224	`fleet-apply-dry-run` (which runs full `chezmoi diff`) and more actionable
225	than `fleet-apply-status` (which only sees live processes, not pending
226	drift / missing init / new prompt keys).
227	
228	```bash
229	just fleet-status                              # all hosts, with `git fetch`
230	just fleet-status --hosts lab-box,vps-tokyo    # subset
231	just fleet-status-quick                        # skip remote `git fetch` (faster, may show stale 'behind')
232	just fleet-status --readiness-json | jq .      # machine-readable
233	```
234	
235	### State matrix
236	
237	The probe classifies each host into exactly one primary state and zero or
238	more secondary notes (e.g. a `behind` host with drift will show
239	`behind: 3 commits, drift: 2 files` in the notes column).
240	
241	| State | Symbol | Meaning | Recovery |
242	|---|---|---|---|
243	| `up-to-date` | ✓ green | Source dir at `origin/HEAD`, no drift, init done | Nothing to do |
244	| `ready-to-update` | ↻ blue | Source is behind origin → `fleet-apply` will pull + apply cleanly | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
245	| `behind` | → cyan | Same as `ready-to-update` but used when there are also other notes (drift / dirty co-existing) | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
246	| `drift` | ⚠ yellow | Remote target was hand-edited; would trigger "could not open a new TTY" prompt without `--force`. With default `--keep-going`, applies the rest of the fleet and skips this file | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a `*.local` override |
247	| `dirty` | ⚠ yellow | Remote source dir has uncommitted changes (someone hand-edited the template on the remote) | ssh in & commit/stash before applying |
248	| `ahead` | ? magenta | Remote source dir has local commits not on origin — `git pull` would diverge | ssh in & `git push` or reset before applying |
249	| `busy` | ⏳ yellow | A `chezmoi update/apply/init` or `ansible-playbook` is already running, OR the chezmoi state lock is held | Wait, then re-probe; OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state |
250	| `init-in-progress` | ⏳ yellow | Source dir is missing/incomplete BUT a `chezmoi update/apply/init` PID is alive — typically mid-clone, or paused at an interactive prompt in another SSH session. Distinct from `no-source` (which is permanent until human intervention) | Wait for the in-flight init to finish, OR ssh in & check the other session |
251	| `toml-mismatch` | ! yellow bold | The local `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` declares prompt keys (`promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` / etc.) that are missing from the remote's saved `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. **This is the `david_ubuntu` failure mode** — `fleet-apply` will crash on this host with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY` on `chezmoi init` | ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts |
252	| `not-init` | ✗ red | `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` doesn't exist — host was never `chezmoi init`'d | ssh in & run `chezmoi init` interactively (one-off; needs TTY) |
253	| `no-source` | ✗ red | `chezmoi source-path` returns nothing or the path is not a git repo | ssh in & re-init (or fix custom `chezmoi.toml` `sourceDir =`) |
254	| `no-chezmoi` | ✗ red | `chezmoi` binary not found in augmented PATH | ssh in & install chezmoi (`curl https://chezmoi.io/get \| sh`) |
255	| `unreachable` | ✗ red | SSH connection failed (timeout, auth, host key, network) | check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent |
256	
257	### Output format
258	
259	```
260	fleet-status — readiness probe across 6 host(s)
261	                                readiness probe
262	┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
263	┃ host       ┃ state                  ┃ notes                                    ┃
264	┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
265	│ self       │ ✓ up-to-date           │                                          │
266	│ hanru_mac  │ ↻ ready-to-update      │ behind: 3 commits                        │
267	│ ts_nas     │ ⏳ busy                │ pids=12345                               │
268	│ jingle207  │ ⚠ drift                │ drift: .config/mise/config.toml          │
269	│ david_ub   │ ! toml-mismatch        │ missing prompt keys: installTunnelTools  │
270	│ idc-srv    │ ✗ unreachable          │ TimeoutError: 30s                        │
271	└────────────┴────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘
272	
273	Hints:
274	  ✗ unreachable (1: idc-srv)
275	      → check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent
276	  ! toml-mismatch (1: david_ub)
277	      → ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts (their default values are usually fine)
278	  ⏳ busy (1: ts_nas)
279	      → wait for the running run, OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state
280	  ⚠ drift (1: jingle207)
281	      → `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a *.local override
282	  ↻ ready-to-update (1: hanru_mac)
283	      → `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` (or whole fleet)
284	
285	Summary: 2/6 hosts ready for `just fleet-apply`, 4 need attention
286	```
287	
288	### Exit code
289	
290	Always 0 (probe is informational). Use `--readiness-json` and parse for
291	fine-grained gating in CI:
292	
293	```bash
294	# Pre-apply gate: refuse to apply if any host is unreachable.
295	if just fleet-status --readiness-json | jq -e 'any(.state == "unreachable")' >/dev/null; then
296	    echo "abort: at least one host unreachable"
297	    exit 1
298	fi
299	just fleet-apply
300	```
301	
302	### How `toml-mismatch` works
303	
304	The probe greps the **local** `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` for `promptBool` /
305	`promptString` / `promptInt` / `promptChoice` (with or without `Once`)
306	calls and extracts the second positional argument (the prompt key name).
307	Then it compares against the set of top-level keys in the remote's saved
308	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. Any keys missing on the remote = the
309	remote will trigger an interactive prompt during `chezmoi update --init`,
310	which has no TTY → fails with the familiar `could not open a new TTY`.
311	
312	False positives are unlikely — only newly-added prompt keys trigger this
313	state. False negatives are possible (e.g. if you wrap a prompt in a
314	template conditional that the remote's profile evaluates to false), but
315	those don't actually break `fleet-apply` either, so they're not a regression.
316	
317	### Empty inventory UX
318	
319	`just fleet-status` on a fresh box without `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`
320	exits 0 with:
321	
322	```
323	no fleet configured yet — Fleet config not found: ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
324	hint: run `just fleet-edit` to add machines, then re-run `just fleet-status`.
325	```
326	
327	`just fleet-edit` itself seeds an empty template (with `[defaults]` and a
328	commented-out `[[hosts]]` example) on first run, so you don't need to
329	remember the schema. `just fleet-apply` keeps its old strict behaviour
330	(exit 2 on missing config) — readiness is the only command that's
331	forgiving here.
332	
333	## Inventory file
334	
335	Path: `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. Seeded **once** by chezmoi from
336	[`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl).
337	[`just az-dev-vm`](az-dev-vm.md) also appends/updates a `[[hosts]]` entry here
338	automatically when it provisions an Azure dev VM (and removes it on
339	`az-dev-vm-down`).
340	The `create_private_` prefix means:
341	
342	- `create_` → chezmoi seeds the file on first apply, then never touches it
343	  again. Your edits survive every `chezmoi apply`.
344	- `private_` → file mode 0600. Safe to keep plaintext sudo passwords here.
345	- To reset the seed: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
346	
347	### Schema
348	
349	```toml
350	[defaults]                    # merged into every host (host keys override)
351	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # PATH binary; e.g. "~/.local/bin/chezmoi" if no-root
352	connect_timeout = 15
353	command_timeout = 1800
354	
355	[[hosts]]
356	name            = "lab-box"   # required, unique display name
357	ssh_alias       = "lab-box"   # preferred: matches `Host lab-box` in ~/.ssh/config
358	# OR explicit connection (used when no ssh_alias):
359	hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
360	user            = "dwlee"
361	port            = 22
362	identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
363	
364	no_root_machine = false       # MUST mirror the chezmoi `noRoot=` value used at
365	                              # `chezmoi init` time on that remote (see below)
366	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # override defaults per-host
367	local           = false       # set true to run chezmoi locally (no SSH); see
368	                              # "Local host execution" section below
369	extra_env       = { FOO = "bar" }   # extra env vars for the remote chezmoi run
370	
371	password_source = { type = "...", ... }   # see "Password sources" below
372	```
373	
374	### Password sources
375	
376	| `type` | Extra keys | Behaviour |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| `none` (default) | — | No password injected. Suitable for `no_root_machine = true` hosts. |
379	| `plain` | `value = "..."` | Read straight from TOML. Relies on file mode 0600. |
380	| `prompt` | — | `getpass()` once at startup, never persisted to disk. |
381	| `bitwarden` | `item = "ssh-host-sudo"` | `bw get password <item>` at startup. Requires `bw unlock` + `BW_SESSION` exported. |
382	
383	### `no_root_machine` semantics
384	
385	This flag **describes** the remote, it does not change it. Each remote was
386	configured at `chezmoi init` time with a `noRoot` boolean (see
387	[`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48`](../../.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)) that's now baked into
388	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` on that machine.
389	
390	- Set `no_root_machine = true` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = true` —
391	  fleet_apply skips sudo entirely (no password file written, run-scripts'
392	  `sudo_session_init` returns "non-interactive" branch and skips sudo work).
393	- Set `no_root_machine = false` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = false`
394	## How sudo password reaches the remote
395	
396	`scripts/fleet/apply.py` does **not** echo the password into the command line.
397	The remote command (assembled by `build_remote_command()`) reads stdin into
398	`~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` (mode 0600, `umask 077`), exports
399	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=$PWD/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass`, runs
400	`chezmoi update`, then `trap … EXIT` removes the file (even on crash).
401	
402	On the remote, `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh::sudo_session_init` was extended
403	with a non-interactive injection path: when `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
404	points to a readable file, the password is validated with `sudo -S -v`, then
405	adopted into the shared state dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/`)
406	exactly the same way an interactive prompt would be — including the watchdog
407	that holds the sudo timestamp warm and writes `ansible-become.yml` for
408	ansible roles. **Subsequent run-scripts inside the same `chezmoi update` see
409	the cached state and never re-prompt.**
410	
411	Pass file lifecycle:
412	- `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` is the orchestrator's drop-off; removed
413	  by the SSH command's `trap` once chezmoi exits.
414	- `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/sudo.pass` is the shared state dir
415	  managed by `sudo_shared.sh`; cleaned up by the existing watchdog when the
416	  ancestor `chezmoi` PID exits.
417	
418	## Connection: ssh_config alias vs explicit
419	
420	`asyncssh.connect(host=...)` reads `~/.ssh/config` like the OpenSSH client.
421	Prefer `ssh_alias`:
422	
423	```
424	# ~/.ssh/config
425	Host lab-box
426	    HostName 10.0.0.42
427	    User dwlee
428	    ProxyJump bastion
429	    IdentityAgent ~/.1password/agent.sock     # 1Password SSH agent
430	```
431	
432	```toml
433	# machines.toml
434	[[hosts]]
435	name      = "lab-box"
436	ssh_alias = "lab-box"          # ← inherits everything above, including ProxyJump
437	```
438	
439	If a host has no ssh_config entry, fall back to explicit
440	`hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file`.
441	
442	## Local host execution (`local = true`)
443	
444	To include the orchestrator machine itself in a fleet apply, add a host
445	with `local = true`:
446	
447	```toml
448	[[hosts]]
449	name            = "self"
450	local           = true
451	no_root_machine = true   # set false if your local apply needs sudo
452	```
453	
454	Local hosts skip asyncssh entirely — chezmoi runs as a direct
455	subprocess (`asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`) inheriting the
456	orchestrator's PATH, sudoers state, and tty. Sudo password injection
457	is not used; if chezmoi needs root it'll prompt on the parent terminal.
458	The `kill-orphans` subcommand also skips local hosts (killing local
459	chezmoi processes from the same shell session would kill `fleet_apply`
460	itself). All other features — log files, live table, `--force`,
461	`--keep-going`, `--command-timeout`, parallelism — work identically.
462	
463	`ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file` are ignored
464	when `local = true`. `chezmoi_path = "auto"` still works (subprocess
465	inherits the calling shell's PATH, which is where the orchestrator
466	itself found `chezmoi`).
467	
468	## Commands
469	
470	```bash
471	just fleet-edit                                 # edit ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml ($EDITOR)
472	just fleet-status                               # readiness probe (use BEFORE apply — see § Readiness probe)
473	just fleet-status-quick                         # readiness probe, skip remote `git fetch`
474	just fleet-apply                                # parallel, all hosts, update --init
475	just fleet-apply-dry-run                        # `chezmoi diff` instead of update
476	just fleet-apply-one lab-box                    # single host, --serial mode
477	just fleet-apply --hosts lab-box,vps-tokyo      # subset
478	just fleet-apply --exclude throwaway-vm         # all except
479	just fleet-apply --max-parallel 3               # throttle SSH fan-out
480	just fleet-apply --no-init                      # `chezmoi apply` (skip update)
481	just fleet-apply --serial                       # one at a time, no live table
482	just fleet-apply --command-timeout 600          # tighter timeout for warm fleets
483	just fleet-apply-kill                           # kill orphan chezmoi/ansible on every host
484	```
485	
486	### Vibe-loop recipes (fast iteration)
487	
488	```bash
489	just fleet-diff lab-box                         # `chezmoi diff` on ONE host, serial output
490	just fleet-apply-file .zshrc                    # apply ONE file across the fleet, skip ansible
491	just fleet-apply-file .config/zsh/aliases.zsh --hosts lab-box
492	just fleet-apply-branch feature/new-tmux        # pin remotes to a branch (ff-only)
493	just fleet-apply-branch-force feature/new-tmux  # … allow `git reset --hard` (after rebase)
494	```
495	
496	`fleet-apply-file PATH` is the headline vibe-loop command:
497	
498	- Skips `chezmoi update` (and thus the slow `run_*` scripts: ansible, Brewfile, Linuxbrew refresh).
499	- Prepends `git -C $(chezmoi source-path) pull --ff-only` so the remote checkout has your latest commit before `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` re-renders just that one target.
500	- PATH is a chezmoi *target* path (relative to `$HOME`), e.g. `.zshrc`, `.config/tmux/tmux.conf`, `.gitconfig`. NOT a source path like `dot_zshrc`.
501	- Round-trip on a warm fleet is typically ~5-15 seconds per host vs 5-30 minutes for a full `fleet-apply`.
502	- You still need to `git push` first — the remote runs `git pull` on its checkout. Local hosts (`local = true`) skip the pull because the source IS your editor's working tree.
503	- Drift / `--force` semantics are unchanged: pass `--force` if you've also edited the file by hand on the remote and want to overwrite.
504	
505	`fleet-apply-branch BRANCH` lets you iterate on a feature branch without polluting `main`:
506	
507	- Each remote runs `git fetch origin BRANCH && git checkout -B BRANCH origin/BRANCH && git merge --ff-only origin/BRANCH` before `chezmoi apply`.
508	- Mode is forced to `apply` (since `chezmoi update` would re-pull `main` and undo the checkout).
509	- Default merge is `--ff-only`: fails loud if the remote checkout has divergence. Use `fleet-apply-branch-force` (which adds `--force-checkout`) to swap in `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` — necessary after you've force-pushed a rebased topic branch.
510	- Local hosts ignore `--branch` entirely: their source dir is your working tree, switching it under your editor would be hostile. The skip is logged.
511	- Compose with `--apply-only-path` for the fastest possible loop: `just fleet-apply --branch tmp/test --apply-only-path .config/foo/bar.toml --hosts lab-box`.
512	
513	
514	## Conflict handling: `--force` vs `--keep-going`
515	
516	When a remote file has drifted from what chezmoi last wrote (someone
517	edited it directly on the host), chezmoi normally prompts on `/dev/tty`
518	to ask whether to overwrite. fleet_apply runs without a PTY, so that
519	prompt dies with `chezmoi: <file>: could not open a new TTY: open
520	/dev/tty: no such device or address`. Two flags control the response:
521	
522	| Flag | Default | Effect on the conflicting file | Effect on the rest of the apply |
523	|---|---|---|---|
524	| `--keep-going` / `--no-keep-going` | **on** | Left **unchanged** (no override) | Continues — other files still apply |
525	| `--force` / `--no-force` | **off** | **Overwritten** with template render | Same |
526	
527	Default combination (`--keep-going`, no `--force`) = **non-destructive**:
528	all clean files apply, drifted files are skipped. fleet_apply parses the
529	chezmoi stderr; if the host's *only* failure is "could not open a new TTY"
530	on one or more drifted targets, it classifies the host as **`drift`**
531	(yellow `⚠`) instead of **`failed`** (red `✗`). The summary lists the
532	drifted files per host so you know exactly what needs attention:
533	
534	```
535	Summary: 5 hosts, 3 ok, 1 failed, 1 drift, 0 skipped
536	  ✗ david_ubuntu  rc=1  log=…/david_ubuntu.log     # real failure
537	  ⚠ hanru_mac     drift in: .config/foo.toml       # only a drift skip
538	                  log=…/hanru_mac.log
539	                  (resolve: --force, or sync edits back to source)
540	```
541	
542	Drift hosts do **not** count toward the process exit code — only `failed`
543	hosts do. This is intentional: drift is a "do something later" signal, not
544	a CI failure. If a host has BOTH a drift skip AND an unrelated error
545	(ansible task, network timeout, etc.) it will be classified as `failed`,
546	not `drift`, so real errors are never silently downgraded.
547	
548	To resolve a drift, either:
549	
550	- Migrate the drift into a per-machine override file (e.g. `~/.gitconfig.local`,
551	  see below) and re-run.
552	- Or run `just fleet-apply --force` once to let the canonical template win
553	  (also accepts `--hosts <name>` to scope it).
554	- Or, for a single file you've already decided about, ssh in and run
555	  `chezmoi apply --force <relpath>` directly — fastest fix when the
556	  template is right but the target is stale.
557	
558	## Per-machine git overrides (`~/.gitconfig.local`)
559	
560	Common drift on `.gitconfig` is host-specific git config that legitimately
561	belongs to that one machine — `[safe] directory = /mnt/NAS/...` (host-mounted
562	NAS), `[credential "https://gitlab.com"]` (glab CLI helper), `[http] proxy = ...`
563	(corporate proxy), etc. Putting these in the chezmoi-managed
564	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` is wrong (they don't apply to other hosts);
565	hand-editing them onto each remote also fails because every fleet apply
566	then trips the "drifted from template" prompt.
567	
568	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` therefore ends with:
569	
570	```gitconfig
571	[include]
572	    path = ~/.gitconfig.local
573	```
574	
575	`include.path` is silently skipped by git when the file doesn't exist
576	(no error), so machines without overrides are unaffected. `~/.gitconfig.local`
577	is git-ignored by chezmoi via `.chezmoiignore` — chezmoi will never seed,
578	overwrite, or diff it. Same self-managed pattern as `~/.zshrc.adhoc`
579	for shell customisations.
580	
581	To migrate per-host lines that already drifted on a remote:
582	
583	```bash
584	ssh <host> 'chezmoi --no-pager diff .gitconfig'   # see what diverged
585	ssh <host> bash -s <<'EOF'
586	  # Move the host-specific block out of the managed file:
587	  # (manually copy the [safe] / [credential] / [http] sections from
588	  # ~/.gitconfig into ~/.gitconfig.local with your editor of choice)
589	  ${EDITOR:-vi} ~/.gitconfig.local
590	  ${EDITOR:-vi} ~/.gitconfig         # delete the migrated lines
591	EOF
592	just fleet-apply-one <host>                       # should now be clean
593	```
594	
595	## Timeouts
596	
597	| Flag | Default | Rationale |
598	|---|---|---|
599	| `--connect-timeout` | 30 s | SSH banner + auth handshake. Bump for high-latency or relay-heavy hosts. |
600	| `--command-timeout` | 7200 s (2 h) | Generous to cover first-run apply: Linuxbrew install (10–20 min) + 22 ansible roles + Brewfile cask downloads (GUI apps; can be 20+ min on slow links) + python_uv_tools / npm / cargo bootstrap. After your fleet is past first-run, drop to e.g. `--command-timeout 600` (10 min) — steady-state re-apply on a warm machine usually finishes in 1–5 min. |
601	
602	If `--command-timeout` fires, the orchestrator sends SIGTERM via the SSH
603	channel **and** closes the channel (which delivers SIGHUP to the remote
604	shell, which the wrapper's trap propagates to chezmoi). The remote should
605	fully exit within seconds.
606	
607	### When a host hangs
608	
609	`command_timeout` is the **outer** budget — it kills the entire chezmoi+ansible chain when blown. Ansible itself has **no per-task timeout**, so a stuck `npm install`, `apt update` retry loop, or `git clone` against a slow mirror will burn the whole 2-hour budget if you let it.
610	
611	Typical hang symptoms:
612	
613	- `--status` shows the host as `running pids=...` for tens of minutes
614	- `--tail HOST` log stops at a `[N] TASK · …` line and never advances
615	- Drilling into the remote: `ssh HOST pstree -p $PID` shows `python3 → /bin/sh -c "… npm install …"` (or apt / git / cargo equivalents) at the leaf
616	
617	Recovery flow:
618	
619	1. **Identify the stuck task** via `--tail HOST` (last visible TASK number) and `ssh HOST pstree` to confirm the leaf process.
620	2. **Kill the run**: `just fleet-apply-kill --hosts HOST` — broadcasts `pkill -TERM` then `-KILL` to chezmoi/ansible/orphans.
621	3. **Bound the next attempt**: re-run with `--command-timeout 600` (or whatever's reasonable for steady-state) so a recurrence won't burn 2 hours again.
622	4. **If the same task keeps stuck**: it's an ansible role / network issue, not a fleet-apply bug. Add `timeout: 300` or `async: 600 poll: 30` to the offending ansible task in `dot_ansible/roles/<role>/tasks/main.yml`.
623	
624	`abandoned` state in `--status` (red, "no sentinel — wrapper SIGKILL'd?") means a previous run died abnormally — the wrapper got SIGKILL before its trap could write the exit sentinel. Common causes: parent OOM-killed, manual `kill -9`, or process-tree teardown cascading from a hung child. Treat it as a failure that left no recovery breadcrumb.
625	
626	## Killing orphans, checking status, re-attaching
627	
628	Local Ctrl+C, network drop, laptop sleep, or any other premature
629	disconnect is handled three ways:
630	
631	1. **In-band cleanup**: `build_remote_command()` wraps chezmoi in a shell
632	   wrapper with `trap '… pkill -TERM -P $_cz_pid …' INT TERM HUP`. asyncssh
633	   uses `request_pty='force'`, so the SSH channel close delivers SIGHUP to
634	   that wrapper shell on the remote — chezmoi (and any ansible-playbook
635	   children) get SIGTERM-ed and the wrapper proxies the exit code back.
636	   In practice this fires whenever asyncssh actually closes the channel
637	   (which is most cases, including normal SIGINT on the controller).
638	
639	2. **Out-of-band rescue**: if even the in-band trap didn't fire (e.g.
640	   `kill -9` on `scripts/fleet/apply.py`, or asyncssh closed the channel
641	   "cleanly" without a HUP delivery), the remote chezmoi/ansible may
642	   still be running:
643	
644	   ```bash
645	   just fleet-apply-kill                       # all hosts
646	   just fleet-apply-kill --hosts lab-box       # specific host
647	   ```
648	
649	   This connects to each host and runs `pkill -TERM -u "$(id -un)" -x
650	   chezmoi`, then `pkill -TERM -x ansible-playbook` and `ansible`, waits
651	   1 s, then SIGKILLs anything still alive. No chezmoi command is sent,
652	   so this is safe to run any time the fleet looks "stuck".
653	
654	3. **Status probe + live tail re-attach** (added after observing that
655	   asyncssh + a slow laptop-side kill sometimes leaves remote work
656	   running for many minutes silently):
657	
658	   ```bash
659	   just fleet-apply-status                     # which hosts are still busy?
660	   just fleet-apply-status --hosts ts_nas      # one host
661	   just fleet-apply-watch                      # poll every 10s until idle
662	   just fleet-apply-tail jingle207             # follow latest run on this host
663	   just fleet-apply-tail jingle207:20260422T140446Z
664	                                               # pin a specific run id
665	   ```
666	
667	   Each remote run tees chezmoi's combined stdout/stderr to
668	   `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/<run_id>.log` and drops a sentinel
669	   `<run_id>.exit` file containing the final exit code when the run
670	   finishes. `--status` reads both: it shows `running` (live PIDs +
671	   their numbers), `finished` (with the exit code), or `idle` per host,
672	   plus the last 5 lines of the latest log inline for quick context.
673	   `--tail` does a `tail -F` on the log over a fresh SSH session and
674	   exits cleanly when the sentinel appears (or you Ctrl+C the viewer
675	   — the remote run keeps going).
676	
677	   `--watch N` (or `just fleet-apply-watch` which presets N=10) repeats
678	   `--status` every N seconds until every host reports finished/idle,
679	   then exits 0. Use this as a passive "wait for the fleet to settle"
680	   cursor after killing the controller — no need to keep pressing
681	   ↑↩ to re-poll. Subsequent polls suppress the per-host log tail to
682	   keep output compact.
683	
684	   **Self / `local = true` hosts** are first-class here: their logs
685	   land in `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/` on the orchestrator (same
686	   dir, no SSH round-trip). `--status` and `--tail self` work
687	   identically to SSH hosts. The PID filter excludes the probe's own
688	   process and parent so a `--status` invocation doesn't see itself.
689	
690	   Both probes are read-only: they never send a chezmoi command and
691	   never kill anything. Combine with `fleet-apply-kill` if you decide
692	   the remote work should stop.
693	
694	### Log retention
695	
696	Each per-host log dir keeps the **10 most recent** runs (`.log` +
697	`.exit` pair); older pairs are deleted at the end of the next run.
698	Override with `--keep-logs N` (`N=0` disables GC entirely if you want
699	to accumulate forever — you'll need to `rm -rf ~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/
700	logs` periodically yourself). GC happens AFTER the sentinel is
701	written, so the just-finished run is always inside the keep window.
702	
703	## Exit codes
704	
705	| Exit | Meaning |
706	|---|---|
707	| 0 | All selected hosts finished `chezmoi update` with rc 0, or only had recoverable drift skips (state = `drift`) |
708	| `N` (1–125) | `N` hosts genuinely failed (rc != 0 with errors *other than* drift skips, SSH error, timeout, or skipped due to missing sudo password) |
709	| 125 | More than 125 hosts failed (capped) |
710	| 2 | Config error (missing TOML, malformed schema) |
711	
712	`drift` hosts intentionally do NOT count as failures — see "Conflict
713	handling" above. They appear in the summary as `⚠` so a human notices, but
714	CI / cron loops keep passing as long as no real errors occur.
715	
716	## Logs
717	
718	Per-host log file: `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`. Each line is
719	prefixed `[out]` or `[err]`. The first two lines record the host metadata and
720	the **literal** remote command sent (which contains no password — only the
721	shell that pipes stdin into the pass file).
722	
723	`logs/` is **not** in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` because it lives in the source
724	repo only when you run `just fleet-apply` from inside the repo. Add it to
725	your local `.gitignore` if you don't already have one for build artifacts.
726	
727	## Troubleshooting
728	
729	- **`zsh:1: command not found: chezmoi` / rc=127** — non-interactive SSH
730	  shells don't source `~/.zshrc`, so `~/.local/bin` (or wherever your
731	  package manager put chezmoi) is not on PATH. The default
732	  `chezmoi_path = "auto"` already augments PATH with `~/.local/bin`,
733	  `~/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin`,
734	  `/usr/local/bin`, `/snap/bin` before invoking chezmoi — covers ~all
735	  installs. If your binary lives elsewhere, pin it explicitly:
736	  ```toml
737	  [[hosts]]
738	  name         = "weird-box"
739	  chezmoi_path = "/opt/custom/bin/chezmoi"
740	  ```
741	  Run `ssh <host> command -v chezmoi` (interactive) vs
742	  `ssh <host> 'command -v chezmoi'` (non-interactive) to see the gap.
743	- **`chezmoi: <file>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty: no such device or address`** —
744	  the file drifted on the remote and chezmoi tried to prompt. With the
745	  default `--keep-going`, the file is left untouched and the rest of
746	  the apply continues (host still reports rc!=0 so drift is visible).
747	  See [Conflict handling](#conflict-handling---force-vs---keep-going)
748	  for the resolution flow; for `.gitconfig` specifically, migrate the
749	  per-host lines to [`~/.gitconfig.local`](#per-machine-git-overrides-gitconfiglocal)
750	  instead of using `--force`.
751	- **`bw get password` fails** — run `bw unlock`, then `export BW_SESSION=...`.
752	- **`asyncssh.PermissionDenied`** — the alias resolves but auth failed.
753	  Test with `ssh <alias> echo ok` first; if you use the 1Password agent,
754	  ensure `IdentityAgent` is set in ssh_config and the agent is unlocked.
755	- **First-time host rejected with "Host key verification failed"** —
756	  fleet_apply uses `known_hosts=None` (= skip its own check, defer to your
757	  `~/.ssh/known_hosts`). Run `ssh <alias>` manually once to TOFU the key.
758	- **Remote chezmoi prompts for the noRoot question and stalls** — the host
759	  was never `chezmoi init`'d. SSH in and run `chezmoi init` once interactively.
760	- **Sudo phase fails immediately on a no_root_machine=false host** — the
761	  password the orchestrator resolved was wrong. The remote
762	  `sudo_shared.sh` rejects it with an explicit message in stderr (caught in
763	  the per-host log).
764	- **Host hangs forever during `chezmoi diff` / `update`** — usually chezmoi
765	  spawned its configured pager (`bat`, `delta`, `less`) which blocked
766	  waiting for terminal input. fleet_apply already passes `--no-pager` to
767	  every chezmoi invocation, but if you've added a custom subcommand /
768	  hookScript that bypasses chezmoi's pager handling, kill the orphan with
769	  `just fleet-apply-kill --hosts <host>` and check that subcommand for
770	  pager / `read` calls.
771	- **Run looks dead after Ctrl+C** — when you Ctrl+C `scripts/fleet/apply.py`
772	  asyncio cancels each task, which calls `proc.terminate()` and closes the
773	  SSH connection. The remote wrapper's trap catches the resulting SIGHUP
774	  and SIGTERMs the chezmoi tree. If anything still survives, run
775	  `just fleet-apply-kill` to broadcast `pkill -TERM` (then SIGKILL) to
776	  every host's `chezmoi` / `ansible-playbook` / `ansible` processes.
777	
778	## Related docs
779	
780	- [`docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md`](sudo-session.md) — full `sudo_shared.sh`
781	  helper API, including the `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` env-injection path
782	  this tool relies on.
783	- [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](upgrades.md) — for upgrading tools on a
784	  remote, ssh in and run `just upgrade-all` there. fleet_apply intentionally
785	  stays scoped to chezmoi apply only.
786	- [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md) — repo invariants, including why
787	  `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` (so `scripts/fleet/apply.py` is never
788	  deployed to `$HOME` and only ever runs from the repo).
789

1991	    """Return the set of prompt-key names declared in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl.

1993	    Used to detect the david_ubuntu failure mode: a NEW promptBoolOnce was

2009	def _classify_readiness(
2010	    fields: dict[str, str],
2011	    drift: list[str],
2012	    expected_keys: set[str],
2013	) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
2014	    """Map probe fields → (primary state, list of secondary notes).
2015	
2016	    Priority order (most actionable first):
2017	      unreachable > no-chezmoi > not-init > init-in-progress > no-source
2018	        > toml-mismatch > busy > dirty > drift > behind > ahead
2019	        > ready-to-update > up-to-date
2020	
2021	    `init-in-progress` outranks `no-source` because the former is a
2022	    transient state (chezmoi is mid-clone or paused at an interactive
2023	    prompt) while the latter is a permanent failure that needs human
2024	    intervention. The probe's SSH script promotes `no-source` ⇒
2025	    `init-in-progress` if it sees an active chezmoi update/apply/init
2026	    PID; we just trust that signal here.
2027	
2028	    Secondary notes carry context the primary state hides (e.g. a
2029	    `behind` host with drift will show "drift: 2 files" in notes).
2030	    """
2031	    notes: list[str] = []
2032	
2033	    # Hard blockers (early exit from probe → only STATE field set).
2034	    state = fields.get("STATE", "")
2035	    if state in {"no-chezmoi", "not-init", "no-source"}:
2036	        return state, notes
2037	    if state == "init-in-progress":
2038	        busy_pids = fields.get("BUSY_PIDS") or ""
2039	        if busy_pids:
2040	            notes.append(f"pids={busy_pids}")
2041	        return state, notes
2042	
2043	    # toml-mismatch: prompt keys present in template but missing on remote.
2044	    if expected_keys:
2045	        remote_keys = set(
2046	            k for k in (fields.get("TOML_KEYS") or "").split(",") if k
2047	        )
2048	        missing = expected_keys - remote_keys
2049	        if missing:
2050	            preview = ", ".join(sorted(missing)[:3])
2051	            extra = (
2052	                ""
2053	                if len(missing) <= 3
2054	                else f" (+{len(missing) - 3} more)"
2055	            )
2056	            notes.append(f"missing prompt keys: {preview}{extra}")
2057	            return "toml-mismatch", notes
2058	
2059	    busy_pids = fields.get("BUSY_PIDS") or ""
2060	    if busy_pids:
2061	        if busy_pids == "chezmoi-state-locked":
2062	            notes.append("chezmoi state lock held (parallel run in progress)")
2063	        else:
2064	            notes.append(f"pids={busy_pids}")
2065	        return "busy", notes
2066	
2067	    behind = int(fields.get("BEHIND") or 0)
2068	    ahead = int(fields.get("AHEAD") or 0)
2069	    dirty = int(fields.get("DIRTY") or 0)
2070	    drift_count = len(drift)
2071	
2072	    # Build secondary notes regardless of primary state.
2073	    branch = fields.get("BRANCH") or ""
2074	    if branch and branch not in {"main", "master"}:
2075	        notes.append(f"branch={branch}")
2076	    if behind:
2077	        notes.append(f"behind: {behind} commit{'s' if behind != 1 else ''}")
2078	    if ahead:
2079	        notes.append(f"ahead: {ahead} commit{'s' if ahead != 1 else ''}")
2080	    if dirty:
2081	        notes.append(f"dirty: {dirty} file{'s' if dirty != 1 else ''}")
2082	    if drift_count:
2083	        # First drift entry as preview; chezmoi status format is
2084	        # "MM <relpath>" (two status chars + path) so strip the prefix.
2085	        first = drift[0]
2086	        first_path = first[3:] if len(first) > 3 and first[2] == " " else first
2087	        more = (
2088	            ""
2089	            if drift_count == 1
2090	            else f" (+{drift_count - 1} more)"
2091	        )
2092	        notes.append(f"drift: {first_path}{more}")
2093	
2094	    # Primary classification.
2095	    if dirty:
2096	        return "dirty", notes
2097	    if ahead and not behind:
2098	        return "ahead", notes
2099	    if drift_count:
2100	        # Drift without git changes = remote target was hand-edited.
2101	        # Counts as actionable (would block apply without --force) but
2102	        # apply itself would proceed past it with --keep-going (default).
2103	        return "drift", notes
2104	    if behind:
2105	        return "ready-to-update", notes
2106	    return "up-to-date", notes

2111	
2112	    Mirrors _build_readiness_probe_cmd but uses Python subprocess + Path
2113	    APIs directly. Skips the busy probe filter for self-process / parent
2114	    (mirrors _probe_local). Returns the same (fields, drift_lines) shape.

52	
53	```
54	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│ Phase 0 — Bootstrap (run_once_before_*)                                 │
56	│   curl-installer: Homebrew, uv, mise                                    │
57	│   apt: build-essential, git, curl (Linux prereqs for Linuxbrew)         │
58	│   apt: libffi-dev, libyaml-dev, python3-dev (Linux non-noRoot only)     │
59	│   uv: ansible-core (pinned Python 3.13)                                 │
60	│   ansible-galaxy: community.general collection                          │
61	│   mise: install runtimes from ~/.config/mise/config.toml                │
62	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
63	                                  │
64	                                  ▼
65	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
66	│ Phase 1 — chezmoi apply (config file deploy)                            │
67	│   Deploys dot_* files; doesn't install tools directly                   │
68	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
69	                                  │
70	                                  ▼
71	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
72	│ Phase 2 — Ansible (run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles)                 │
73	│   Runs all 26 roles; each dispatches to its underlying manager          │
74	│   (brew / apt / mise / uv / npm / cargo / gem / dotnet / curl / gh-rel) │
75	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
76	                                  │
77	                                  ▼
78	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
79	│ Phase 3 — Brew bundle (run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle)               │
80	│   `brew bundle --no-upgrade` against ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile*       │
81	│   Mostly GUI casks (macOS); skipped unless Brew/AI/gaming apps enabled  │
82	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
83	                                  │
84	                                  ▼
85	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
86	│ Phase 4 — Per-application onchange scripts                              │
87	│   Completion regen (run_after_50_generate_completions)                  │
88	│   bat theme cache (run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme)                     │
89	│   ble.sh compile (run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh)                  │
90	│   Global skills restore (run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills)   │
91	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
92	```
93	
94	The bootstrap is **single-source-of-truth** for the foundational tools
95	that everything else depends on. If you find yourself wanting to add
96	`mise` / `uv` / Homebrew elsewhere, the answer is almost always "extend
97	the bootstrap, then assume it in the role". The Linux noRoot path
98	(`profile=ubuntu_server` or RHEL/CentOS without sudo) skips the apt
99	prereqs and Linuxbrew, falling back to per-tool curl-installers and
100	GitHub releases — coverage is intentionally narrower (no GUI, no
101	system-wide installs).
102	
103	---
104	
105	## Per-manager catalog
106	
107	Each subsection below covers one manager. Format:
108	
109	- **Owns** — what tools end up under this manager's control
110	- **How a tool gets there** — the canonical "I want to add tool X via this manager" recipe
111	- **Per-OS notes** — branching when relevant
112	- **Upgrade path** — link to the matching category in `upgrades.md`
113	
114	The ansible roles section is split into thematic subsections because
115	26 roles in one table is unreadable.
116	
117	### 1. Bootstrap scripts (pre-chezmoi)
118	
119	**Files**: `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`,
120	`run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`,
121	`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
122	
123	**Owns** — the four foundational managers that everything else
124	assumes:
125	
126	| Tool | Mechanism | Per-OS |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| **Homebrew** | `Homebrew/install` curl script | macOS always; Linux only when `installBrewApps=true` & non-noRoot & arch∈{amd64,arm64}. Mirrors via `HOMEBREW_*_GIT_REMOTE` (Aliyun / USTC / BFSU / TUNA) when `useChineseMirror=true` |
129	| **uv** | `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` | all OSes if missing |
130	| **mise** | `curl https://mise.run \| sh`, with direct `mise.jdx.dev/mise-latest-linux-${arch}[-musl]` fallback (musl forced when glibc < 2.28) | all OSes; arch detection (x64/arm64/armv7) |
131	| **ansible-core** | `uv tool install --force --python 3.13 ansible-core` | all OSes; force-refreshes if existing ansible runs on Python < 3.10 |
132	| **ansible-galaxy: community.general** | `ansible-galaxy collection install --force-with-deps` | all OSes |
133	| **mise runtimes** | `mise install --yes` (consumes `~/.config/mise/config.toml`) | all OSes — see [§ mise](#4-mise-runtime-versions) |
134	
135	**Linux prereqs (apt)** to make Linuxbrew + mise Ruby + ansible-cryptography
136	buildable: `build-essential`, `procps`, `curl`, `file`, `git` (always);
137	`libffi-dev`, `libyaml-dev`, `python3-dev` (non-noRoot only).
138	
139	**Intel-Mac-only side script**: `run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`
140	runs `softwareupdate -i` for Xcode CLT, then `brew cleanup` +
141	`brew link --overwrite git`.
142	
143	**One-shot migrations**: `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
144	moves a legacy config file (`~/.config/opencode/config.json` →
145	`opencode.json`). Not an install.
146	
147	**Adding to bootstrap**: only when the new tool is required *before*
148	ansible runs — e.g. ansible itself, mise (because ansible roles call
149	`mise exec`), uv (because some roles call `uv tool install`). Otherwise
150	prefer an ansible role.
151	
152	### 2. Homebrew (formulae + casks)
153	
154	Three Brewfile templates + scattered `community.general.homebrew[_cask]`
155	tasks in ansible roles. The split is **macOS-centric**: Linux Brewfile is
156	empty, Linuxbrew use happens role-by-role.
157	
158	#### 2.1 Brewfiles
159	
160	| File | Owns |
161	|---|---|
162	| `Brewfile.tmpl` (shared) | General macOS GUI support when `installBrewApps=true`: tap `nikitabobko/tap`, formulae `mas`, `tailscale` |
163	| `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` | All GUI casks — see table below |
164	| `Brewfile.linux.tmpl` | Empty (commented-out placeholders only) |
165	
166	**macOS casks** (~25 active, gated by feature flags):
167	
168	| Cask | Gating |
169	|---|---|
170	| `alacritty`, `warp`, `cmux`, `cursor`, `visual-studio-code` | `installBrewApps` |
171	| `claude`, `opencode-desktop`, `antigravity` | `installAiDesktopApps` |
172	| `chatgpt`, `codex-app` | `installAiDesktopApps` + arm64 |
173	| `codeisland` (tap `wxtsky/tap`) | `installAiDesktopApps` |
174	| `ollama-app` | `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools` |
175	| `steam` | `installGamingApps` |
176	| `nikitabobko/tap/aerospace`, `alt-tab`, `raycast`, `maccy`, `scroll-reverser`, `the-unarchiver`, `applite` | `installBrewApps` |
177	| `discord` | `installBrewApps` |
178	| `arc` | `installBrewApps` |
179	| `obsidian`, `google-drive`, `grammarly-desktop`, `super-productivity` | `installBrewApps` |
180	| `spotify`, `anki` | `installBrewApps` |
181	| `tailscale-app` | `installBrewApps` |
182	| `dbeaver-community` | `installBrewApps` |
183	| `superset` | `installBrewApps` + arm64 |
184	
185	Many more entries exist in commented-out form (minecraft, telegram,
186	openvpn-connect, etc.) — uncomment to enable.
187	
188	#### 2.2 Role-driven brew (formulae + casks)
189	
190	Most CLI formulae land via ansible roles, not the Brewfile. Examples:
191	
192	- `base/tasks/main.yml`: `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`
193	- `devtools/tasks/main.yml`: large set — `bat`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`, `zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`, `taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`, `shellcheck`, `shfmt`, `bats-core`, `git-graph`
194	- `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`: `claude-code` (cask), `codex` (cask), `gemini-cli` (formula), `rtk` (formula), `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar` (all with tap setup)
195	- `networking_tools/`: `nmap`, `arp-scan`, `mtr`, `iperf3`, `doggo`, `httpie`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `speedtest` (tap `teamookla/speedtest`), `ngrok`, `cloudflared`
196	- `media_tools/`: `ffmpeg`, `imagemagick`, `exiftool`, `vips`
197	- `iac_tools/`: `azure-cli`, `hashicorp/tap/terraform`, `opentofu`
198	- `llm_tools/`: `llmfit`, `models`, `ollama`
199	- `security_tools/`: `gitleaks`
200	- `starship/`, `atuin/`, `neovim/`, `bash/` (gawk), `zsh/` — each installs its primary tool via homebrew formula on macOS
201	- `pueue` (from `rust_cargo_tools/`): macOS uses homebrew formula
202	
203	**Per-OS dispatch** is the universal pattern in roles: macOS branch uses
204	`community.general.homebrew` / `homebrew_cask`; Linux branches use apt,
205	Linuxbrew (when present), or GitHub releases. See each role for the
206	explicit `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` guard.
207	
208	**Tap inventory** (added by various roles): `nikitabobko/tap`,
209	`wxtsky/tap` (CodeIsland), `hashicorp/tap` (terraform),
210	`teamookla/speedtest`, `specstoryai/tap`, `steipete/tap` (CodexBar),
211	`marcus/tap` (td, sidecar), `dlvhdr/formulae`, `raine/workmux`.
212	
213	**Adding via homebrew**: prefer a brew formula/cask only when the tool
214	is macOS-shipped and Linux equivalents go via apt or release tarball.
215	Linux-first tools rarely belong in the Brewfile.
216	
217	#### 2.3 Homebrew prefix dispatch helper
218	
219	`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::_uv_install_style` (and mirrored helpers in
220	`python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`) inspect whether a binary lives under
221	`brew --prefix` to decide between `brew upgrade <pkg>` and the tool's
222	native self-update. This avoids the "I `uv self update` on a brew-uv
223	host and silently no-op" trap — see
224	[`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
225	
226	### 3. Ansible roles
227	
228	26 roles under `dot_ansible/roles/`. Triggered by
229	`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
230	(re-runs when any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes
231	— SHA256-tracked).
232	
233	**Universal patterns**:
234	
235	- `state: present` / `creates:` — install-only, no silent upgrades
236	- Per-OS branching via `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` (or `["Debian", "RedHat"]`)
237	- `tags: [sudo]` on any `become: true` task (so noRoot mode skips them — see [`pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md))
238	- `failed_when: false` + `register:` for "is the tool installed?" probes
239	- Linux user-level fallback to `~/.local/bin` when distro package is missing or too old (handles RHEL/CentOS + noRoot + Apple-Silicon-not-bottled scenarios)
240	
241	**Role feature flags** (set in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` via prompts):
242	`installBrewApps`, `installAiDesktopApps`, `installCodingAgents`,
243	`installLlmTools`, `installPythonUvTools`, `installJsCliTools`,
244	`installDotnetTools`, `installIacTools`, `installMediaTools`,
245	`installNetworkingTools`, `installTunnelTools`, `installBitwarden`,
246	`installGamingApps`, `installInputMethod`, `installAuditd`. Roles gate themselves on the
247	matching flag; the bundle script `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` defines
248	profile presets (`minimal`, `cloud-vm` planned, default-developer, …).
249	
250	#### 3.1 Base / shared CLI
251	
252	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
253	|---|---|---|
254	| `base` | `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`, `gcc`/`build-essential`/`make` | macOS: brew formulae · Debian: apt (`fd-find` + `/usr/bin/fd` symlink) · RedHat: yum · `just` always via `curl https://just.systems/install.sh` · Linux user-level GitHub-release fallback to `~/.local/bin` for ripgrep/fd/jq/git-lfs |
255	| `homebrew` | (no installs — refresh + cleanup only, 24h-throttled) | n/a |
256	| `atuin` | `atuin` shell history sync | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://setup.atuin.sh \| sh -s -- --non-interactive` → `~/.atuin/bin/` |
257	| `nerdfonts` | `font-hack-nerd-font` | macOS: brew cask · Linux: download `Hack.zip` from `nerd-fonts/releases/latest` → `~/.local/share/fonts` + `fc-cache -fv` |
258	
259	#### 3.2 Shells (`bash`, `zsh`, `starship`)
260	
261	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
262	|---|---|---|
263	| `bash` | `gawk` (ble.sh dep, unconditional); homebrew `bash` 5.x + `/etc/shells` + `chsh` (macOS only when `primary_shell="bash"`) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum |
264	| `zsh` | system `zsh` package; **source-build zsh 5.9** to `~/.local` on RHEL/CentOS 7 if system zsh < 5.3; `chsh` when `primary_shell="zsh"` (default) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum + ncurses-devel source build fallback. oh-my-zsh + plugins ship as externals (§12) |
265	| `starship` | `starship` prompt | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://starship.rs/install.sh \| sh -s -- --yes` → sudo `/usr/local/bin` → user `~/.local/bin` fallback |
266	
267	The `primaryShell` chezmoi prompt gates the `chsh` call only — both
268	shells deploy their configs everywhere. See AGENTS.md → "`primaryShell`
269	choice gates `chsh` only" hard invariant.
270	
271	#### 3.3 DevTools (mega-role)
272	
273	Single role, ~50 tools — the kitchen sink for terminal-life CLIs.
274	There's a backlog item ([`backlog/devtools-role-split.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/devtools-role-split.md))
275	considering whether to break this up.
276	
277	**macOS** (homebrew, taps: `dlvhdr/formulae` for `gh-dash`,
278	`raine/workmux`): `bat`, `bats-core`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`,
279	`git-graph`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`,
280	`zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`,
281	`workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`,
282	`taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`,
283	`yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`,
284	`shellcheck`, `shfmt`.
285	
286	**Linux** — per-tool dispatch. The pattern is **apt/yum (system) →
287	GitHub release tarball or installer (user)**:
288	
289	| Tool | Linux mechanism (preferred → fallback) |
290	|---|---|
291	| `gh` | GitHub `.deb` → user tarball |
292	| `glab` | GitHub `.deb` → user tarball |
293	| `bat` | apt + `/usr/bin/bat` symlink → GitHub musl release |
294	| `bats` | apt → GitHub release `install.sh` |
295	| `zoxide` | `curl install.sh` |
296	| `eza` | gierens.de apt repo → user GitHub musl → brew aarch64 |
297	| `git-delta` | `.deb` (x86_64) → brew aarch64 → user GitHub musl |
298	| `diffnav` | user GitHub release |
299	| `gh-dash` | `gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash` |
300	| `git-graph` | user GitHub release (x86_64 only) |
301	| `tldr` | system npm or `mise exec -- npm install -g tldr` |
302	| `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `duckdb` | user GitHub release tarballs |
303	| `rclone` | official installer or GitHub release |
304	| `thefuck` | `uv tool install thefuck` (Python 3.11, distutils workaround) |
305	| `shellcheck`, `shfmt` | apt or release |
306	| `direnv` | apt or installer |
307	| `yazi`, `superfile`, `btop`, `zellij`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux` | Linuxbrew or GitHub release |
308	| `tmux` | apt → `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage` AppImage to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` when system version < 3.3 (required by `display-menu` popup) — see AGENTS.md "Tmux popup menu ≥ 3.3 required" |
309	| `htop`, `pandoc` | apt |
310	| `taplo`, `television (tv)`, `lnav`, `grc`, `tailspin (tspin)`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr` | mix of apt + release |
311	| `ccze` | apt only (Linux-only tool, no macOS equivalent) |
312	
313	#### 3.4 Coding agents
314	
315	Role: `dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`. Gated on
316	`installCodingAgents`. **The most heterogeneous role** — every agent
317	ships via a different mechanism upstream, and the role mirrors that.
318	
319	| Agent | macOS | Linux | Notes / source lines |
320	|---|---|---|---|
321	| `terminal-notifier` / `libnotify-bin` | brew formula / apt (Debian) | apt (Debian only) | notifier helpers, lines 9–29 |
322	| **Claude Code** | brew cask `claude-code` | `curl https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` → `~/.claude/local/bin/claude` | lines 33–71; arch skip for non-amd64/arm64 |
323	| **OpenCode** | `curl https://opencode.ai/install \| bash -s -- --no-modify-path` → `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` | same | lines 73–107. Cross-platform unified install; `--no-modify-path` keeps installer from editing chezmoi-managed shell rc. See [`pitfalls/opencode-docker-opentui-glibc-loader-missing.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/opencode-docker-opentui-glibc-loader-missing.md) for the container-image variant |
324	| **Cursor CLI** (`cursor-agent`) | `curl https://cursor.com/install \| bash` | same | lines 112–124; brew cask was abandoned due to code-signing |
325	| **GitHub Copilot CLI** | npm `@githubnext/github-copilot-cli` (global) | `mise exec -- npm install -g` | lines 134–168 |
326	| **OpenAI Codex CLI** | brew cask `codex` | `mise exec -- npm install -g @openai/codex` | lines 172–236 |
327	| **Gemini CLI** | brew formula `gemini-cli` → npm `@google/gemini-cli` fallback | `mise exec -- npm install -g` | lines 240–300 |
328	| **Antigravity CLI** (`agy` + `agyc` symlink) | `curl https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` patched mid-flight via `sed` → `--skip-path --skip-aliases` | same | lines 317–355. Two gotchas: (a) name collision with the Antigravity IDE — collision-free `agyc` symlink keys the AICAP stack; (b) installer mutates shell profiles by default — patched away. Both documented in-source |
329	| **RTK** | brew formula `rtk` | `curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh \| sh` → `~/.local/bin/rtk` | lines 359–413 |
330	| **SpecStory** | brew tap `specstoryai/tap` + formula → GitHub release zip fallback | GitHub release tarball | lines 417–595 |
331	| **CodexBar** | brew tap `steipete/tap` + cask (arm64 only) | Linuxbrew → GitHub release `steipete/CodexBar` | lines 599–764 |
332	| **td** | brew tap `marcus/tap` + formula | Linuxbrew → GitHub release `marcus/td` | lines 768–975. Includes "is current td Sidecar-compatible?" version check; removes conflicting formula if not |
333	| **sidecar** | brew tap `marcus/tap` + formula | Linuxbrew → GitHub release `marcus/sidecar` | lines 979–1149 |
334	| **Specify CLI** | `uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git` | same | lines 1153–1184. Only role-installed tool currently using `uv tool install` directly (not via `python_uv_tools` defaults) |
335	| **OpenChamber** | npm `@openchamber/web` | `mise exec -- npm install -g` | lines 1188–1222 |
336	| **claude-hud** plugin | runs `files/claude_hud_sync.py --only-if-missing` | same | lines 1239–1247; install-only, explicit `just upgrade-plugins` for refresh |
337	
338	**SSOT for the AICAP agent stack**: `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh`
339	defines autodetect order + `AICAP_*_MODEL` defaults. Four Python
340	consumers regex-parse the same file (see AGENTS.md cross-file rule).
341	Adding a new agent here means: install in this role + add to the SSOT
342	+ four Python `AGENT_CONFIG` dicts.
343	
344	#### 3.5 Language toolchains (`python_uv_tools`, `ruby_gem_tools`, `rust_cargo_tools`, `dotnet_tools`, `js_cli_tools`)
345	
346	Wrappers around language-specific package managers. All consume a
347	`defaults/main.yml` list so the role's `tasks/main.yml` is a loop. See
348	[§ uv](#5-uv-python-cli-tools), [§ npm](#6-npm-global-node-clis),
349	[§ cargo](#7-cargo-rust-crates), [§ dotnet](#8-dotnet-global-net-tools),
350	[§ gem](#9-gem-ruby-gems) for the tool lists.
351	
352	| Role | Underlying manager | Tools (count) | Gate |
353	|---|---|---|---|
354	| `python_uv_tools` | `uv tool install` | 13 | `installPythonUvTools` |
355	| `llm_tools` | `uv tool install` + brew + cargo + curl-installer | 4 (litellm, llmfit, models, ollama) | `installLlmTools` |
356	| `js_cli_tools` | `mise exec -- npm install -g` / system npm | 1 (`readability-cli`) | `installJsCliTools` |
357	| `rust_cargo_tools` | `cargo install` (after `mise install rust@latest`) | `[]` in defaults + 2 hardcoded (`recon`, `pueue`) | (no gate; rust runtime always installed via mise) |
358	| `ruby_gem_tools` | `gem install` (after `mise install ruby@3`) | 2 (`try-cli`, `tmuxinator`) | (no gate; gated by `mise install ruby` skip on noRoot Linux) |
359	| `dotnet_tools` | `dotnet tool install --global` (after `mise use -g dotnet@latest`) | 1 (`azure-cost-cli`) | `installDotnetTools` |
360	
361	**Key invariant** (`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare
362	`extra_binaries:`): see AGENTS.md "Install vs upgrade is split on
363	purpose" hard invariant for the audit one-liner and the pitfall.
364	
365	#### 3.6 Editors + plugins (`neovim`, `lazyvim_deps`, `nerdfonts`)
366	
367	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
368	|---|---|---|
369	| `neovim` | `neovim` ≥ 0.11.2 (`state: latest` on macOS) | macOS: brew formula · Linux: apt → GitHub release tarball if too old (`/opt/nvim` + `/usr/local/bin/nvim` symlink) → user-level tarball to `~/.local`; **oldEL** pulls from `neovim/neovim-releases` (glibc 2.17 rebuild repo). 396	### 4. mise (runtime versions)
397	
398	**Config**: `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`
399	
400	`[settings]`: `ruby.compile = false`.
401	
402	**Modern hosts** (default):
403	
404	| Runtime | Version | Gated on |
405	|---|---|---|
406	| `node` | `lts` | always |
407	| `bun` | `1` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
408	| `rust` | `stable` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
409	| `go` | `latest` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
410	| `dotnet` | `10` | `installDotnetTools` |
411	| `ruby` | `3` | `installExtraRuntimes` (+ not `noRoot`) |
412	
413	**Version-pinning rationale**: `node=lts` / `rust=stable` / `go=latest` use
414	moving channels because each promises backward compatibility (Go's
415	[go1compat](https://go.dev/doc/go1compat) makes `latest` as safe as
416	rust's `stable`). `bun=1` and `dotnet=10` pin the **major** instead —
417	neither guarantees no-break across majors (bun ships behavior changes on
418	minors; .NET majors bump TFMs / SDK behavior), and `dotnet=10` is also the
419	current LTS (8/9 are at/near EOL by mid-2026). Bump `dotnet` deliberately
420	when the next LTS (12) lands. `ruby=3` tracks the 3.x line.
421	
422	`go` replaces the old macOS-only brew install from the `security_tools`
423	role, so Linux hosts now get a managed Go too (previously a gap).
424	
425	Ruby is **skipped in noRoot mode** (`profile=ubuntu_server` without
426	sudo) because it needs `libffi-dev` / `libyaml-dev` to build, which
427	require apt.
428	
429	**oldEL (CentOS/RHEL 7, glibc 2.17)**: only `ruby = "3"` — other
430	runtimes have glibc/libstdc++ requirements too new for EL7.
431	
432	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-mise` → `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade`
433	(honours the version constraints in the config; `lts`/`latest` move
434	forward, pinned versions don't).
435	
436	**Adding a runtime**: edit `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` directly.
437	Runtime-version gating across hosts is on the [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md).
438	
439	**Why mise (not nvm/rbenv/pyenv/asdf/n)**: unified, language-agnostic,
440	respects `.tool-versions`, doesn't fight shell init order. Python is
441	deliberately **not** mise-managed — that's uv's territory (faster + no
442	build-from-source for CPython, which the noRoot Linux path can't do).
443	The [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md) tracks
444	finer-grained per-host gating.
445

499	### 6. npm (global Node CLIs)
500	
501	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` for the
502	JS-tools-specific list. Scattered global-npm installs live in other
503	roles (`coding_agents`, `bitwarden`, `lazyvim_deps`, `devtools`).
504	
505	**Install dispatch** (universal pattern across roles):
506	
507	```yaml
508	# On Linux:
509	mise exec -- npm install -g <package>
510	# Falls back to system npm if mise has no node registered
511	# On macOS:
512	community.general.npm: { name: <package>, global: true }
513	```
514	
515	Linux explicitly uses `mise exec -- npm` to avoid the Ubuntu apt npm
516	(too old; system Node 12 fails `engine` checks for modern packages and
517	`/usr/local/lib/node_modules` is root-owned, breaking `--global` for
518	non-root users). See [`pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md).

614	### 10. curl-installer (self-managed CLIs)
615	
616	Tools that ship via vendor `install.sh` instead of any package manager.
