621	**Inventory**:
622	
623	| Tool | Install URL | Lands at | Source role |
624	|---|---|---|---|
625	| Homebrew | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/brew` (macOS) / `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/` (Linux) | bootstrap |
626	| uv | `https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/uv` (or `~/.cargo/bin/uv`) | bootstrap |
627	| mise | `https://mise.run` | `~/.local/bin/mise` | bootstrap |
628	| just | `https://just.systems/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/just` or `~/.local/bin/just` | `base` |
629	| starship | `https://starship.rs/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/starship` or `~/.local/bin/starship` | `starship` |
630	| atuin | `https://setup.atuin.sh` | `~/.atuin/bin/atuin` | `atuin` |
631	| docker | `https://get.docker.com` | system docker (rootless variant) | `docker` (Linux) |
632	| zoxide | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/zoxide` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
633	| direnv | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/direnv` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
634	| **Claude Code** | `https://claude.ai/install.sh` | `~/.claude/local/bin/claude` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
635	| **OpenCode** | `https://opencode.ai/install` (+ `--no-modify-path`) | `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` | `coding_agents` (macOS + Linux) |
636	| **Cursor CLI** | `https://cursor.com/install` | `~/.local/bin/cursor-agent` | `coding_agents` |
637	| **Antigravity CLI** | `https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` (patched `--skip-path --skip-aliases`) | `~/.local/bin/agy` + `agyc` symlink | `coding_agents` |
638	| **RTK** | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/master/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/rtk` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
639	| **llmfit** | `https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/llmfit` (or system) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
640	| **Ollama** | `https://ollama.com/install.sh` | system path (Linux, sudo) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
641	| Ookla speedtest | `https://install.speedtest.net/app/cli/install.<distro>.sh` | system | `networking_tools` (Linux) |
642	
643	**Why curl-installer over a package manager**:
644	
645	- Fast-moving releases — vendor controls cadence (Claude, OpenCode,
646	  Cursor, Antigravity push daily/weekly)
647	- Self-update subcommand exists and the installer is the canonical
648	  reinstall path → `cat_agents` in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` can call
649	  either
650	- Avoids the "brew formula is 3 weeks stale" problem (see commit
651	  history for the OpenCode move from `anomalyco/tap` to official
652	  installer)
653	- No tap/PPA/repo to maintain
654	
655	**Adding a curl-installer tool**:
656	
657	1. Pick a role (or add to `coding_agents` if it's an agent)
658	2. Use the canonical pattern: `which` check → `creates:` guard on the
659	   binary path → `curl ... | bash [-s -- --no-modify-path]` shell task
660	3. If the installer mutates shell rc files, add a `--no-modify-path`
661	   flag (or equivalent — see OpenCode and Antigravity blocks). The
662	   chezmoi-managed PATH is the SSOT
663	4. Update `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_agents` if the tool has a
664	   self-update subcommand (or just an installer-as-upgrader path)
665	5. If the binary lands somewhere other than `~/.local/bin` (e.g.
666	   `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`), add an existence-gated PATH prepend
667	   to `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`
668	
669	### 11. GitHub-release downloads (user-level fallback)
670	
671	When apt/yum can't satisfy a version requirement (e.g. Apple Silicon
672	brew bottle missing, RHEL/CentOS package too old, noRoot host with no
673	sudo), roles fall back to downloading the latest GitHub release tarball
674	and extracting to `~/.local/bin` (user-writable, already on PATH).
675	
676	**Canonical pattern**:
677	
678	```yaml
679	- name: Get latest <tool> release
680	  ansible.builtin.uri:
681	    url: https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest
682	    return_content: true
683	  register: <tool>_release
684	
685	- name: Compute <tool> arch
686	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
687	    <tool>_arch: "{{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64'] else 'arm64' if ... else 'unsupported' }}"
688	
689	- name: Download / extract / copy into ~/.local/bin
690	  block:
691	    - get_url: { url: "https://github.com/.../{{ tag }}/{{ asset }}", dest: /tmp/..., retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120 }
692	    - unarchive: { src: ..., dest: /tmp/..., remote_src: true }
693	    - find:      { paths: /tmp/..., patterns: <binary>, file_type: file }
694	    - copy:      { src: ..., dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/<binary>", mode: '0755' }
695	  rescue:
696	    - debug: "<tool> installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
697	```
698	
699	**Tools using this pattern** (rough list — see each role's `tasks/main.yml`):
700	
701	- `base`: `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `git-lfs`
702	- `devtools`: `gh`, `glab`, `bat`, `bats`, `eza`, `git-delta`, `diffnav`, `git-graph`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `duckdb`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `btop`, `zellij`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `taplo`, `tv` (television), `lnav`, `tailspin`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`
```

1706	    fast enough to run every 5–10s on a 100-host fleet without strain.
1707	
1708	    Output per host: state (running/finished/idle), the latest run id,
1709	    PIDs (if running), exit code (if finished), and the last 5 log lines.
1710	    Always returns 0 — this is a probe, not a verdict.
1711	    """

1713	        if h.local:
1714	            return h, *_probe_local()

1720	            stdout = result.stdout or ""
1721	        except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
1722	            return h, {"STATE": "error"}, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}\n"
1723	        # Parse KEY=VAL lines until LOG_TAIL_BEGIN; the rest is log tail.
1724	        fields: dict[str, str] = {}
1725	        log_lines: list[str] = []
1726	        in_tail = False
1727	        for line in stdout.splitlines():
1728	            if line == "LOG_TAIL_BEGIN":
1729	                in_tail = True

```text
1	# Upgrades — Explicit, Opt-in Tool Refresh
2	
3	> How to actually move installed tools forward on a machine managed by this repo, and why `chezmoi apply` deliberately will *not* do that for you.
4	
5	> **See also**: [`tool-managers.md`](tool-managers.md) — the install-side companion to this doc. It maps every tool in the repo to its install mechanism (which manager owns it, where it lands, per-OS dispatch). When you're trying to figure out "why doesn't `just upgrade-X` move tool Y forward?", that's where the coverage gaps are documented.
6	
7	## Why install and upgrade are split
8	
9	`chezmoi apply` (and the ansible phase it triggers) is **install-only by design**. Ansible roles use `state: present` + `creates:` so that running `chezmoi apply` on a running box is idempotent and never silently bumps every tool to whatever happens to be latest that day. This matters because:
10	
11	- **Predictability** — rerunning apply after editing one role file shouldn't ripple-upgrade unrelated tools.
12	- **Offline / flaky network** — install-only can be satisfied by what's already on disk; `--upgrade` workflows always hit the network.
13	- **Review friction** — you *want* to see "chezmoi says 10 casks would move; proceed?" as a separate decision from "apply my dotfile changes".
14	
15	The explicit upgrade path lives in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh), exposed via `just upgrade-*` recipes in [`justfile`](../../justfile). It is the **only** thing that intentionally moves tools forward on this repo's flow.
16	
17	Two side-effects worth knowing about:
18	
19	- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` entries have `refreshPeriod = "168h"` — chezmoi itself will re-fetch those weekly on apply. That's a bounded "nudge", not an upgrade mechanism for installed binaries.
20	- Homebrew casks that carry a `homebrew_cask` entry with `state: present` freeze to that version until a Brewfile hash change forces a re-bundle with `--no-upgrade`. Still install-only; `upgrade-brew` is what actually bumps them.
21	
22	## Entry points
23	
24	```bash
25	just upgrade-all          # externals → brew → mise → uv → npm → cargo → dotnet → gem → flatpak → warp → agents → plugins
26	just upgrade-dry-run      # same, but commands are printed, not executed
27	just upgrade-<category>   # run one category in isolation
28	```
29	
30	Or use the script directly when you want the flags:
31	
32	```bash
33	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh                           # same as 'all'
34	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh brew uv                   # two categories
35	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --only brew,mise          # same, via --only
36	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --skip agents,plugins     # all, minus those
37	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --dry-run all             # preview
38	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --help
39	```
40	
41	The script runs categories in the canonical `ALL_CATEGORIES` order regardless of CLI arg order — dependencies between categories are real (see [§ Run order](#run-order)).
42	
43	## Category matrix
44	
45	| Category | What actually happens |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `externals` | `chezmoi upgrade` (the chezmoi binary itself) + `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` (force-refresh the 168h externals: oh-my-zsh, TPM, toolkami.rb, fzf). First because a chezmoi version bump may change how later steps behave. |
48	| `brew` | `brew update` → `brew upgrade` → `brew upgrade --cask --greedy` → `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile` *without* `--no-upgrade` → `Brewfile.{darwin,linux}` → `brew cleanup`. macOS pre-warms the shared sudo session via [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) so cask pkg installers that shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` find a live ticket. |
49	| `mise` | `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade` (honours the version constraints in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`). `self-update` warns, rather than fails, when mise was installed via brew/apt. |
50	| `uv` | Detects install style by binary path (Homebrew vs curl-installer) and dispatches to the right channel: `brew upgrade uv` for Homebrew/Linuxbrew installs, `uv self update` for the standalone curl installer. Then `uv tool upgrade --all`. Covers every tool listed in [`python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml) and [`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml). The `python_uv_tools` ansible role does the same dispatch automatically when uv is below `min_uv_version` — see [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md). |
51	| `npm` | `npm -g update`, falling back to `mise exec -- npm -g update` when `npm` is not directly on PATH (same detection as [`js_cli_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml) / [`bitwarden`](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml)). |
52	| `cargo` | If absent, bootstraps the `cargo-update` crate, then `cargo install-update -a`. Covers pueue (Linux) plus any future entries in [`rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
53	| `dotnet` | Parses tool names from [`dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `dotnet tool update --global <name>` per tool (via the mise dotnet shim). Falls back to `dotnet tool list --global` if parsing finds nothing. |
54	| `gem` | `gem update --system` + `gem update` via the mise ruby shim. |
55	| `flatpak` | `flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes` for user-scope Flathub apps (Discord et al. when `discordChannel=flatpak` — see [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md)). Skipped when `flatpak` is absent OR when no user-scope apps are installed. System-scope (`flatpak update --system`) is intentionally NOT covered — it requires `sudo` and is rare in this repo's flow; run manually if needed. |
56	| `warp` | **Linux only.** `sudo apt-get update` + `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal` via the shared sudo session. macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask `warp` + `--greedy`); this category short-circuits with `SKIPPED` on Darwin. The on-disk binary is replaced but the running Warp process is **not** restarted — quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version. The in-app `warp_finish_update <token>` graceful-restart only works from inside a live Warp session (Warp-injected shell function, not on `$PATH` otherwise) — see [`docs/tools/warp.md`](../tools/warp.md) for the full mechanism. |
57	| `agents` | Re-runs the official `curl \| bash` installers for **tools already present** only — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Ollama (Linux), llmfit (Linux), RTK. Bootstrap list mirrors [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml). |
58	| `atuin` | macOS: `brew upgrade atuin` (no-op when atuin was installed via the upstream installer rather than brew). Linux: re-runs `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh \| env ATUIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh` so the upstream installer drops the new binary into `~/.atuin/bin/` while leaving PATH wiring to [`dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh). Skipped with `SKIPPED` if `atuin` is not on PATH. The local SQLite history (`~/.local/share/atuin/`) and config (`~/.config/atuin/config.toml`) are untouched. |
59	| `plugins` | `nvim --headless "+Lazy! sync" +qa` → `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all` → refresh installed `claude-hud` via [`claude_hud_sync.py`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py) → `pre-commit autoupdate` (on the dotfiles repo root) → `tldr --update` → `gh extension upgrade --all`. Each step is guarded on the relevant binary being present. |
60	
61	### Run order
62	
63	```mermaid
64	flowchart LR
65	    externals["externals<br/>(chezmoi + externals)"] --> brew
66	    brew["brew<br/>(formulas + casks greedy + Brewfile)"] --> mise
67	    mise["mise<br/>(self-update + runtimes)"] --> uv
68	    uv["uv<br/>(self update + tools)"] --> npm
69	    npm["npm<br/>(-g update)"] --> cargo
70	    cargo["cargo<br/>(install-update -a)"] --> dotnet
71	    dotnet["dotnet<br/>(tool update --global)"] --> gem
72	    gem["gem<br/>(gem update)"] --> flatpak
73	    flatpak["flatpak<br/>(--user update)"] --> warp
74	    warp["warp<br/>(Linux apt-only)"] --> atuin
75	    atuin["atuin<br/>(brew or setup.atuin.sh)"] --> agents
76	    agents["agents<br/>(curl \| bash installers)"] --> plugins
77	    plugins["plugins<br/>(Lazy, TPM, pre-commit, tldr, gh)"] --> summary((Summary))
78	```
79	
80	Rationale: package managers themselves go first (`externals` to maybe swap chezmoi; `brew` because mise/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem may be Homebrew-installed; `mise` before the language-scoped ones because `mise upgrade` can swap the runtime `npm`/`cargo`/`dotnet`/`gem` belong to). `agents` + `plugins` last because they depend on everything above being current.
81	
82	`claude-hud` stays out of [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl): it uses a versioned cache path and rewrites `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, so it fits the explicit `plugins` upgrade path better than chezmoi externals. Upstream `v0.0.12+` also switched usage rendering to Claude Code's official stdin `rate_limits`, which means the old credential-derived `Max` badge may disappear after upgrade.
83	
84	## Semantics: best-effort, not all-or-nothing
85	
86	Each category is wrapped in a `run_category` helper:
87	
88	- Individual command failures inside a category do **not** abort the rest of the category. Everything is best-effort.
89	- A category failure does **not** abort the next category. The script keeps going.
90	- Categories return `77` when the prerequisite is missing (e.g. no `dotnet` binary) — that is reported as **SKIPPED**, not FAILED.
91	- The final summary groups into three buckets:
92	
93	```text
94	[INFO] Upgrade Summary
95	[SUCCESS] OK:      externals brew mise uv npm cargo agents plugins
96	[WARN] SKIPPED: gem (prerequisite missing)
97	[ERROR] FAILED:  dotnet
98	[ERROR]    - dotnet: rc=1
99	```
100	
101	Overall process exit code is `1` iff at least one category is in FAILED. `--dry-run` always exits `0` because no real command runs.
102	
103	## Sample: `just upgrade-dry-run`
104	
105	```text
106	────────────────────────────────────────────
107	[INFO] upgrade_tools.sh — categories: externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins (dry-run)
108	[WARN] DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed
109	────────────────────────────────────────────
110	[INFO] ── category: externals ──
111	[INFO] Upgrading chezmoi binary itself
112	+ chezmoi upgrade
113	[INFO] Force-refreshing chezmoi externals (.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
114	+ chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
115	[SUCCESS] category 'externals' completed
116	────────────────────────────────────────────
117	[INFO] ── category: brew ──
118	+ brew update
119	+ brew upgrade
120	+ brew upgrade --cask --greedy
121	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
122	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
123	+ brew cleanup
124	[SUCCESS] category 'brew' completed
125	...
126	```
127	
128	## Things intentionally excluded
129	
130	- **No `state: latest` rewrites of ansible roles.** `chezmoi apply` semantics stay conservative; the upgrade path uses package-manager commands directly.
131	- **No `apt upgrade` / system package bumps.** Keeps the default scope sudo-light and noise-free. Run `sudo apt upgrade && sudo apt autoremove` manually if you want that.
132	- **No Linux Steam upgrade category.** The Ubuntu Desktop Steam launcher/runtime packages are apt-managed through Valve's repo, so they move with your normal system apt upgrade cadence; the Steam client itself self-updates on launch. macOS Steam is a Homebrew cask and is covered by `just upgrade-brew`.
133	- **No daemon restart** for LiteLLM / Ollama / pueued / anything `systemd`-managed. We only refresh the binaries; restarting is your call.
134	- **No automatic scheduling.** There is no cron, launchd, or systemd timer wired up. Running `just upgrade-all` is an intentional action you take when you have time to review diffs / deal with breakage.
135	- **`scripts/**` is ignored by chezmoi** ([`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) line 29) — the script is *not* deployed to `$HOME`. It runs from the dotfiles repo checkout directly (where `chezmoi cd` takes you). That is a deliberate choice: upgrade logic is repo-local, not per-user.
136	
137	## Troubleshooting
138	
139	- **`chezmoi upgrade` fails.** `chezmoi upgrade` only works when chezmoi was installed via the official install script or `go install`. Homebrew/apt installs will surface an error — upgrade via *that* channel instead. The script treats this as a warning, not a failure.
140	- **`mise self-update` fails.** mise refuses when installed via a system package manager. Treated as a warning.
141	- **`uv self update` no-ops on Homebrew uv.** Handled automatically — `cat_uv()` detects the install style and runs `brew upgrade uv` instead. See [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md) and [`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
142	- **macOS cask pkg installer hangs on sudo.** The script calls `sudo_session_init "upgrade-brew"` on macOS, which prompts once and warms the ticket. If you ran the script over SSH with no TTY, that step becomes `non-interactive` and cask pkg bumps may stall. Fix: run locally, or `ssh -t`, or pre-warm with `sudo -v` yourself before `just upgrade-brew`.
143	- **`cargo install-update -a` fails halfway through.** One crate break does not abort the rest (best-effort). Re-run `just upgrade-cargo` — cargo-update is itself rebuilt if missing.
144	- **`pre-commit autoupdate` bumped a hook that now errors.** That is a repo-file change, not an environment change. Review `.pre-commit-config.yaml` diff; `git checkout -p .pre-commit-config.yaml` to partially revert if needed.
145	
146	## Extending
147	
148	Three ways to add a new tool to the upgrade flow:
149	
150	1. **Tool already managed by an existing category (brew / uv / npm / cargo / dotnet / gem / mise).** Nothing to do — the generic `upgrade-<category>` picks it up because it uses the package manager's own bulk command.
151	2. **New `curl | bash` installer.** Add a guarded block inside `cat_agents()` in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh). Gate on the binary being present so the upgrade path never bootstraps on machines that don't have the tool.
152	
153	   ```bash
154	   if command -v newtool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
155	     info "Upgrading newtool"
156	     _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://newtool.dev/install.sh | bash" || any_fail=1
157	     ran_any=1
158	   fi
159	   ```
160	
161	3. **Brand-new strategy (e.g. GitHub release binary with custom download logic).** Add a `cat_<name>` function, register it in:
162	   - `ALL_CATEGORIES` array
163	   - The dispatch `case` in the main loop
164	   - A matching `just upgrade-<name>` recipe in [`justfile`](../../justfile)
165	   - This doc's [category matrix](#category-matrix)
166	
167	Keep the return-value contract: `0` = success, `77` = skipped (prerequisite missing), any other non-zero = failure.
168	
169	## Cross-references
170	
171	- [`AGENTS.md` § Hard repo invariants](../../AGENTS.md#install-vs-upgrade-is-split-on-purpose) — short version (install-vs-upgrade rule) written for AI agents touching this repo.
172	- [`README.md` § Keeping tools up-to-date](../../README.md) — short version written for humans arriving from the front page.
173	- [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) — the implementation.
174	- [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) — the sudo-session helper reused for macOS cask installers.
175	- [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) — the `refreshPeriod` entries that `upgrade-externals` force-refreshes.
176	- Ansible role defaults consumed for enumeration: [`dotnet_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`python_uv_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`llm_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml).

```text
1	# Backlog Research
2	
3	Long-form research, design notes, and paused troubleshooting for items listed in
4	[`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md). One file per topic, named with a slug that matches
5	the TODO entry.
6	
7	## Why this exists
8	
9	`TODO.md` is the **index** — short titles with priority/effort tags. This folder
10	is the **knowledge base** — the actual investigation, options considered,
11	benchmarks, error messages, and decisions that informed the TODO entry. The goal
12	is **resume-friendliness**: when you (or an agent) come back to an item three
13	months later, the doc here lets you pick up in 5 minutes instead of re-running
14	30 minutes of investigation.
15	
16	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `backlog/**`) — it
17	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
18	
19	## When to add a doc here
20	
21	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` file when **any** of these apply:
22	
23	- The TODO item carries a `P?` tag (it requires evaluation; record what was tried)
24	- You did meaningful troubleshooting but didn't ship a fix (capture the trace
25	  before it evaporates)
26	- Multiple options were considered (record the trade-offs, not just the winner)
27	- An external blocker exists (waiting on upstream release, host availability)
28	- The implementation is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
29	
30	`[S]` items rarely need a doc unless there's surprising context.
31	
32	## When NOT to add a doc here
33	
34	- Item is `[S]` and obvious (e.g., "change a TOML key") — just put the file path
35	  in the TODO entry
36	- Already covered by a `docs/this_repo/*.md` or `docs/tools/*.md` page
37	  (cross-link instead, that's user-facing reference)
38	- Speculation only ("would be cool to...") with no investigation — keep it as a
39	  one-liner in `TODO.md` first; promote to a doc when you actually look into it
40	
41	## File template
42	
43	```markdown
44	# <Topic title>
45	
46	**Status**: P? / P1 / P2 / P3 / blocked / deferred / superseded
47	**Effort**: S / M / L / XL
48	**Related**: `TODO.md` · code paths · related docs
49	
50	## Context
51	
52	Why this surfaced. Trigger (conversation, bug, new tool, recurring annoyance).
53	Date helps — "2026-04, came up while reviewing starship prompt".
54	
55	## Investigation
56	
57	What's already been tried / read / measured. **This is the section that saves
58	future-you time.** Be specific:
59	
60	- Commands run + relevant output
61	- Docs/issue/SO links read
62	- Benchmark numbers
63	- Error messages copy-pasted in full (not paraphrased)
64	
65	## Options considered
66	
67	| Option | Pros | Cons |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| A. … | … | … |
70	| B. … | … | … |
71	
72	## Current blocker / open questions
73	
74	Why this is still on the backlog. One of:
75	
76	- Waiting on upstream X (link)
77	- Need host/data Y to verify
78	- Trade-offs unclear, need user preference
79	- Effort estimate exceeds current budget
80	
81	## Decision (if any)
82	
83	`2026-04 deferred — waiting for X release` or
84	`2026-04 chose option B because …`
85

80:- [ ] **[?/M] fleet-apply: optional `sshpass` / interactive-password SSH login support** — currently `password_source` only feeds remote sudo (`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`); SSH login itself is key-only, so password-only hosts classify as `unreachable` in `fleet-status`. Schema comment + new pitfall (`pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`) now document the limitation. Concrete trigger: `zyc_friend` (IDC server, 2026-05-08) has `Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive` — sshd deliberately omits `publickey` AND uses `keyboard-interactive` (PAM) instead of plain `password`, so even after `ssh-copy-id` deposits the key, login still requires the IDC password. A real fix needs: (a) optional `sshpass -f` invocation when `password_source.ssh_login = true` (or a separate `ssh_password_source`), (b) `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password` to handle PAM-only sshds (sshpass defaults to `password` method only), (c) graceful fallback when `sshpass` not installed, (d) parallel-safe (no TTY prompts), (e) opt-in only — default stays key-only for security. Recommended user fix today: ask the IDC admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`, OR remove the host from the fleet and `ssh <host> chezmoi update --apply` manually. Promote when ≥2 hosts in the fleet legitimately can't accept a pubkey.
```

1	# `fleet exec` — cross-host argv-list command runner with AI summary
2	
3	**Status**: Done 2026-05-13 — shipped as `scripts/fleet/exec.py`.
4	**Effort**: M (~600 LOC including copy-pasted AICAP block; ~250 of that is AI infrastructure that will collapse into shared `scripts/aisum/` on next refactor).
5	
6	## Resolution (2026-05-13)
7	
8	Shipped exactly as planned with one refinement: the AI prompt cache excludes
9	`elapsed_ms` from its hash key. The initial implementation included
10	`elapsed_ms` per host, which varies every run — every invocation produced a
11	cache miss. Excluding it from the hash payload (the LLM doesn't need
12	millisecond precision to classify) means identical command outputs reuse the
13	cached classification regardless of SSH timing variance. Verified locally:
14	first run 14.8s, second run 1.6s (~9× speedup on cache hit).
15	
16	All other API decisions held:
17	- Argv after `--` as default; `--shell bash|zsh|sh` opt-in for pipes/globs.
18	- `--login` opt-in for rc-loaded env; `--no-augment-path` escape hatch
19	  (mutually exclusive with `--login`).
20	- AI tiers: `succeeded` / `differed` / `failed` with majority-output
21	  detection.
22	- `--report --out PATH` markdown output.
23	- `--out-dir DIR` writes per-host stdout/stderr/json files.
24	
25	The AICAP code was copy-pasted from `executable_pqsum`, making `fleet exec`
26	the **4th** Python consumer of `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh`. The
27	extraction TODO is now P2 — next AI-tooling change should land
28	`scripts/aisum/__init__.py` first.
29	
30	
31	**Related**: `scripts/fleet/{tmux,info,pueue}.py`, `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`, `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/pueue.md` (lessons learned about SSH PATH)
32	
33	## Why
34	
35	The user surfaced this need 2026-05-13 while reviewing `fleet pueue`:
36	
37	> 然後是不是fleet加一個 可以方便我同時在多臺host上執行command並且等待收集結果的subcommand？
38	
39	The existing `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` are specialised probes — each runs a fixed bash blob and parses structured output. They don't help when the user needs ad-hoc command execution across the fleet (`pueue --version` everywhere, `df -h /` everywhere, `systemctl --user status pueued` everywhere).
40	
41	This is the most common Ansible / parallel-ssh use case, but the user doesn't want ansible's overhead for one-shot commands. Fleet already has the asyncssh + semaphore + inventory plumbing — `fleet exec` is a thin wrapper that exposes it directly.
42	
43	## Design — confirmed via AskUserQuestion (2026-05-13)
44	
45	### Shape: argv list after `--`, not a shell string
46	
47	```bash
48	fleet exec [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND [ARG...]
49	```
50	
51	Examples:
52	
53	```bash
54	fleet exec -- pueue --version
55	fleet exec -- df -h /
56	fleet exec --hosts ts_nas,jingle207 -- systemctl --user status pueued
57	fleet exec --serial -- ls -la /var/log/nginx/
58	```
59	
60	**Rationale**: no shell expansion on the orchestrator side means no quoting / injection footguns. The argv is passed through asyncssh's `conn.run(argv_list)` (which uses execvp-style on the remote, no shell). For users who explicitly want pipes / globs / redirects, add `--shell bash|zsh|sh` to wrap the command in `bash -c "<reassembled string>"`.
61	
62	**Trade-off accepted**: `fleet exec -- echo "hello world" | wc` doesn't pipe — the `| wc` is parsed by the LOCAL shell. Users wanting cross-host piping use `--shell`.
63	
64	### PATH augmentation (same prelude as pueue)
65	
66	`fleet exec` uses the SAME PATH-augmenting prelude lesson learned from `scripts/fleet/pueue.py`:
67	
68	```
69	$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$PATH
70	```
71	
72	Without this `fleet exec -- pueue --version` finds no pueue on hosts where it lives in `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `~/.cargo/bin`. Same false-negative class as the original pueue probe bug.
73	
74	**Flag**: `--no-augment-path` skips the prelude when the user explicitly wants the minimal SSH PATH (debugging "what does ssh see by default").
75	
76	**Flag**: `--login` wraps the command in `bash -lc "..."` so the user's rc files load. Slower (~150-500ms per host) but matches "as if I SSH'd in and ran it". Caveat: `bash -lc` on hosts where the user's primary shell is zsh misses the zshrc-set PATH additions (cargo, pyenv, mise, conda init blocks) — limitation, not a bug.
77	
78	### Render: table by default, `--json` for piping
79	
80	Default rendering:
81	
82	```
83	                          fleet exec — pueue --version
84	┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━┓
85	┃ HOST         ┃ RC ┃ STDOUT     ┃   ms ┃
86	┡━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━┩
87	│ self         │  0 │ pueue 4.0.1│  120 │
88	│ hanru_mac    │  0 │ pueue 4.0.2│  610 │
89	│ ts_nas       │  0 │ pueue 4.0.1│  990 │
90	│ jingle207    │  0 │ pueue 4.0.2│  450 │
91	│ david_ubuntu │  0 │ pueue 4.0.2│  720 │
92	└──────────────┴────┴────────────┴──────┘
93	```
94	
95	- `STDOUT` shows the first line, truncated to terminal width.
96	- Non-zero exit codes render the RC cell in red; stdout truncates to make room for stderr's first line.
97	- Per-host SSH/timeout failures show `RC=N/A` and the error class.
98	
99	`--json` emits a JSON array, one record per host:
100	
101	```json
102	[
103	  {
104	    "host": "self",
105	    "rc": 0,
106	    "stdout": "pueue 4.0.1\n",
107	    "stderr": "",
108	    "elapsed_ms": 120
109	  },
110	  ...
111	]
112	```
113	
114	`--out-dir DIR` writes per-host `DIR/<host>.stdout` + `DIR/<host>.stderr` + `DIR/<host>.json` (rc + elapsed). Useful for long outputs that don't fit the table.
115	
116	### AI mode — `fleet exec --ai`
117	
118	Confirmed in scope per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-13. Mirrors the `fleet pueue --ai` pattern: pipe the merged per-host JSON to a new prompt template (`AIEXEC_PREAMBLE`) that classifies hosts:
119	
120	- **`succeeded`** — rc=0 AND stdout matches the cluster majority
121	- **`differed`** — rc=0 BUT stdout differs from the majority (e.g. different version, different config)
122	- **`failed`** — rc≠0 OR SSH/timeout error
123	
124	Output JSON:
125	
126	```json
127	{
128	  "command": "pueue --version",
129	  "majority_output": "pueue 4.0.2",
130	  "hosts": [
131	    {"host": "self",      "tier": "differed",  "summary": "pueue 4.0.1 (older — upgrade candidate)"},
132	    {"host": "hanru_mac", "tier": "succeeded", "summary": "pueue 4.0.2"},
133	    {"host": "ts_nas",    "tier": "differed",  "summary": "pueue 4.0.1 (older)"},
134	    {"host": "jingle207", "tier": "succeeded", "summary": "pueue 4.0.2"},
135	    {"host": "david_ubuntu", "tier": "succeeded", "summary": "pueue 4.0.2"}
136	  ],
137	  "fleet_summary": "3/5 hosts on pueue 4.0.2; self + ts_nas trailing on 4.0.1 — both upgrade candidates"
138	}
139	```
140	
141	Implementation: lives in a new `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleetexec-ai` (separate Python uv-script, **not** in `executable_pqsum` — different domain). OR: extract the existing AGENT_CONFIG / detect_agent / invoke_agent / cache_lookup helpers from `executable_pqsum` into a shared module **first** (`scripts/aisum/__init__.py`, per the existing TODO follow-up), then `executable_fleetexec-ai` imports from it. The shared-module refactor is already listed; doing it before adding the 4th consumer is the cleanest path.
142	
143	`fleet exec --ai --report` emits markdown (mirrors `pqsum ai --report`).
144

146	
147	- `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` — add `exec` to USAGE + dispatch dict
148	- `scripts/fleet/exec.py` — new module, ~150 LOC, mirrors `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` skeleton

154	### Out of scope
155	
156	- **Per-host write confirmations** (the `--clean` y/N model from pqsum) — `fleet exec` is "run this everywhere", any safety check is the user's job.
157	- **Long-running streaming output** — `fleet exec` captures completed stdout/stderr only. For watch / tail use `fleet tail` (apply-log specific) or a future `fleet stream`.
158	- **stdin passthrough** — `fleet exec --stdin file.txt -- some-cmd` would feed file.txt to each remote command's stdin. Plausible follow-up, not in v1.
159	- **Pty allocation** (`-t` over SSH) — non-interactive only in v1. Interactive commands (vim, less) don't fit the fan-out model.
160	
161	## Promote when
162	
163	At least two of these become true:
164	
165	- (a) User runs the same command across hosts 3+ times in a row manually (`for h in hosts; do ssh $h cmd; done`).
166	- (b) The AICAP shared-module extraction lands (so adding the 4th AI consumer doesn't pay the duplication tax).
167	- (c) A specific cross-host audit need surfaces ("which hosts are running kernel 6.x?", "which have ssd?").
168	
169	## Cross-references
170	
171	- Cross-file invariants from this work (PATH augmentation, daemon protocol drift handling) live in `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` and should be copied into `scripts/fleet/exec.py` verbatim. If a future refactor extracts a shared `scripts/fleet/_ssh_probe.py` helper, both files become callers.
172	- The `--shell bash|zsh` flag is the same surface as Ansible's `ansible_shell_executable` — semantic parity acceptable.
173	- For users on hosts where pueue itself is the wrong version (jingle207's 4.0.1 vs 4.0.2 daemon drift), `fleet exec --ai -- pueue --version` would surface the mismatch as `differed` tier with version pinpointed. This is the audit use case (c) above.
174

---pitfall centos7-noroot---
# `centos_server` profile on a noRoot CentOS 7 box installs nothing

## Symptom

Run `chezmoi apply` on a CentOS Linux 7.9 box where the user has no
`sudo` (typical corporate/data-center development server):

```
$ sudo -v
sudo: PAM account management error: Permission denied
sudo: a password is required
```

`chezmoi apply` completes cleanly, ansible reports `0 failed`, configs
deploy under `~/.config/`, but `command -v rg fd jq nvim starship`
returns nothing. The dotfiles-deployed `~/.zshrc` references binaries
that don't exist; opening a new shell prints `command not found` for
half the prompt.

## Root cause

The Linux ansible roles have two parallel install paths for each tool:

1. **System-level** (`apt:` / `yum:`) — gated by `become: true, tags:
   [sudo]`. Skipped on `noRoot=true` via `--skip-tags sudo`. Correct.
2. **User-level fallback** — downloads pre-built binaries from GitHub
   releases into `~/.local/bin/`, no sudo required.

The user-level fallback is the one that's *supposed* to fire on a
noRoot box. It was historically gated on
`when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` — which made sense when
the only Linux profiles were `ubuntu_*`, but is wrong as soon as a
RedHat-family box (CentOS, Rocky, Alma) shows up. The user-level path
has no apt-specific behaviour — it's `curl | tar | install`. There's
no reason for it to be gated on the package-manager family.

So on CentOS 7 with `noRoot=true`, both paths are gated out:

- system-level: skipped by `--skip-tags sudo`
- user-level: skipped by `os_family == "Debian"` predicate

The role is a no-op and the user gets a working `~/.zshrc` pointing at
binaries that were never installed.

## Fix

Broaden the user-level (non-sudo-tagged) `when:` predicates from:

```yaml
when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
```

to:

```yaml
when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
```

Applied across `dot_ansible/roles/{base,starship,security_tools,rust_cargo_tools}/tasks/main.yml`
when the `centos_server` profile was introduced. The
```

```text
1	# `fleet-status` reports `unreachable` even though `ssh <host>` works interactively
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `just fleet-status` shows a host as ✗ `unreachable` with note like
5	  `PermissionDenied: Permission denied for user <user> on host <ip>`
6	- `just fleet-apply --hosts <host>` fails the same way at the readiness preflight
7	- Manually running `ssh <host>` (or `ssh <ssh_alias>`) succeeds — but **prompts
8	  for a password** before letting you in
9	- Other hosts in the same `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` succeed (they all use
10	  SSH key / `ssh-agent` / 1Password agent auth)
11	- The host's inventory entry has a `password_source = { type = "plain", value = "..." }`
12	  (or `bitwarden` / `prompt`) — and you reasonably assumed that covers SSH login
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-05-08, on `zyc_friend` (an IDC server reachable only via
15	password auth). User had set `password_source = { type = "plain", ... }` and
16	expected `fleet-status` / `fleet-apply` to use that for the SSH login.
17	
18	**Affects**: any host where `~/.ssh/config` doesn't yield a usable key (no
19	`IdentityFile`, no agent forward, key not authorised on remote, password-only
20	sshd policy).
21	
22	## Root cause
23	
24	In `scripts/fleet_apply.py`, `password_source` is **only** consumed by
25	`_resolve_passwords()` (~line 203) to populate `Host.sudo_password`, which is
26	then written to a 0600 temp file on the remote and exported as
27	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (see `build_remote_command()` ~line 426). That env
28	var is picked up by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` → `sudo_session_init` to skip
29	the `/dev/tty` prompt during chezmoi's `run_*` scripts.
30	
31	**SSH login itself uses `subprocess` → `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` (effectively)
32	with no `sshpass` involvement.** When key auth fails, sshd asks for a password,
33	`BatchMode` forbids it, the connection dies with `Permission denied`, and the
34	host is classified `unreachable` by `_classify_readiness()` (~line 2007).
35	
36	So the password schema works at two completely different stages:
37	
38	| Stage | Auth mechanism | Reads `password_source`? |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| SSH login (transport) | key / agent only | ❌ NO |
41	| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from `password_source` | ✅ YES |
42	
43	The schema doc (`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` lines
44	49–54) labels `type = "plain"` as "last resort — relies on file mode 0600",
45	which reads as if it covers everything. It doesn't say *what* it covers.
46	
47	## Why it's designed this way
48	
49	Three deliberate choices, listed so you don't "fix" this by accident:
50	
51	1. **No `sshpass` dependency.** Avoids extra binary install + maintenance, and
52	   most modern sshd configs ship with `PasswordAuthentication no` anyway.
53	2. **Parallel apply incompatible with TTY prompts.** `fleet-apply` runs N hosts
54	   concurrently; an interactive password prompt would deadlock the orchestrator.
55	3. **Security posture.** SSH password auth has known weaknesses (online
56	   brute-force surface). The repo philosophy nudges users toward key-based.
57	
58	## Fix (per-host)
59	
60	Recommended:
61	
62	```sh
63	ssh-copy-id <host>                              # push your pubkey
64	ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> true && echo OK     # verify key auth works non-interactively
65	just fleet-status                                # confirm host now classifies correctly
66	```
67	
68	### Gotcha: `ssh-copy-id` succeeds but ssh STILL asks for password
69	
70	Seen on `zyc_friend` (IDC server) 2026-05-08. `ssh-copy-id` reports
71	`Number of key(s) added: 1` and the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` entry IS on the
72	remote, but next login still prompts. `ssh -v` reveals:
73	
74	```
75	Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive
76	```
77	
78	Note `publickey` is **absent**. The remote sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no`
79	(common in corporate / IDC security baselines). The key was deposited but the
80	server refuses to consider it. Two consequences:
81	
82	1. `ssh-copy-id` itself runs over `keyboard-interactive` (PAM), not over
83	   key auth — it succeeds at the file-write step but proves nothing about
84	   future logins.
85	2. Even adding `sshpass` support to fleet-apply (the deferred TODO) wouldn't
86	   trivially work — `sshpass` defaults to the `password` method, but PAM-only
87	   sshds need `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`.
88	
89	Fix: ask the remote admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in
90	`/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (+ `systemctl reload sshd`). If they refuse, drop the
91	host from the fleet inventory and apply manually.
92	
93	Verify pubkey auth is allowed before troubleshooting your own keys:
94	
95	```sh
96	ssh -v <host> true 2>&1 | grep "Authentications that can continue"
97	# Must include `publickey` for fleet-apply to ever work.
98	```
99	
100	If the remote forbids key auth (rare; usually a misconfigured `sshd_config`
101	with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), edit the remote sshd or remove the host from
102	the fleet inventory and apply manually:
103	
104	```sh
105	ssh <host>
106	# inside the remote shell:
107	chezmoi update --apply
108	```
109	
110	## Detection
111	
112	Quick triage when a host shows `unreachable`:
113	
114	```sh
115	# 1. Does manual SSH work?
116	ssh <host> true && echo "ssh works"
117	
118	# 2. Does it work non-interactively (the mode fleet uses)?
119	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <host> true
120	# If this prompts or errors → no usable key auth → fleet can't reach it
121	```
122	
123	If step 1 prompts for a password but step 2 errors with `Permission denied
124	(publickey,password)`, you've hit this pitfall.
125	
126	## Related
127	
128	- `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema doc (consider
129	  amending the `password_source` comment to clarify it's sudo-only)
130	- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` → "Readiness probe" — describes the
131	  `_classify_readiness` state vocabulary
132	- `docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md` → "Non-interactive password injection" — the
133	  consumer side of `password_source` / `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
134	- `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md` — adjacent sudo-helper trap
135
```

```text
     1	# `fleet-status` reports `unreachable` even though `ssh <host>` works interactively
     2	
     3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
     4	- `just fleet-status` shows a host as ✗ `unreachable` with note like
     5	  `PermissionDenied: Permission denied for user <user> on host <ip>`
     6	- `just fleet-apply --hosts <host>` fails the same way at the readiness preflight
     7	- Manually running `ssh <host>` (or `ssh <ssh_alias>`) succeeds — but **prompts
     8	  for a password** before letting you in
     9	- Other hosts in the same `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` succeed (they all use
    10	  SSH key / `ssh-agent` / 1Password agent auth)
    11	- The host's inventory entry has a `password_source = { type = "plain", value = "..." }`
    12	  (or `bitwarden` / `prompt`) — and you reasonably assumed that covers SSH login
    13	
    14	**First seen**: 2026-05-08, on `zyc_friend` (an IDC server reachable only via
    15	password auth). User had set `password_source = { type = "plain", ... }` and
    16	expected `fleet-status` / `fleet-apply` to use that for the SSH login.
    17	
    18	**Affects**: any host where `~/.ssh/config` doesn't yield a usable key (no
    19	`IdentityFile`, no agent forward, key not authorised on remote, password-only
    20	sshd policy).
    21	
    22	## Root cause
    23	
    24	In `scripts/fleet_apply.py`, `password_source` is **only** consumed by
    25	`_resolve_passwords()` (~line 203) to populate `Host.sudo_password`, which is
    26	then written to a 0600 temp file on the remote and exported as
    27	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (see `build_remote_command()` ~line 426). That env
    28	var is picked up by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` → `sudo_session_init` to skip
    29	the `/dev/tty` prompt during chezmoi's `run_*` scripts.
    30	
    31	**SSH login itself uses `subprocess` → `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` (effectively)
    32	with no `sshpass` involvement.** When key auth fails, sshd asks for a password,
    33	`BatchMode` forbids it, the connection dies with `Permission denied`, and the
    34	host is classified `unreachable` by `_classify_readiness()` (~line 2007).
    35	
    36	So the password schema works at two completely different stages:
    37	
    38	| Stage | Auth mechanism | Reads `password_source`? |
    39	|---|---|---|
    40	| SSH login (transport) | key / agent only | ❌ NO |
    41	| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from `password_source` | ✅ YES |
    42	
    43	The schema doc (`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` lines
    44	49–54) labels `type = "plain"` as "last resort — relies on file mode 0600",
    45	which reads as if it covers everything. It doesn't say *what* it covers.
    46	
    47	## Why it's designed this way
    48	
    49	Three deliberate choices, listed so you don't "fix" this by accident:
    50	
    51	1. **No `sshpass` dependency.** Avoids extra binary install + maintenance, and
    52	   most modern sshd configs ship with `PasswordAuthentication no` anyway.
    53	2. **Parallel apply incompatible with TTY prompts.** `fleet-apply` runs N hosts
    54	   concurrently; an interactive password prompt would deadlock the orchestrator.
    55	3. **Security posture.** SSH password auth has known weaknesses (online
    56	   brute-force surface). The repo philosophy nudges users toward key-based.
    57	
    58	## Fix (per-host)
    59	
    60	Recommended:
    61	
    62	```sh
    63	ssh-copy-id <host>                              # push your pubkey
    64	ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> true && echo OK     # verify key auth works non-interactively
    65	just fleet-status                                # confirm host now classifies correctly
    66	```
    67	
    68	### Gotcha: `ssh-copy-id` succeeds but ssh STILL asks for password
    69	
    70	Seen on `zyc_friend` (IDC server) 2026-05-08. `ssh-copy-id` reports
    71	`Number of key(s) added: 1` and the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` entry IS on the
    72	remote, but next login still prompts. `ssh -v` reveals:
    73	
    74	```
    75	Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive
    76	```
    77	
    78	Note `publickey` is **absent**. The remote sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no`
    79	(common in corporate / IDC security baselines). The key was deposited but the
    80	server refuses to consider it. Two consequences:
    81	
    82	1. `ssh-copy-id` itself runs over `keyboard-interactive` (PAM), not over
    83	   key auth — it succeeds at the file-write step but proves nothing about
    84	   future logins.
    85	2. Even adding `sshpass` support to fleet-apply (the deferred TODO) wouldn't
    86	   trivially work — `sshpass` defaults to the `password` method, but PAM-only
    87	   sshds need `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`.
    88	
    89	Fix: ask the remote admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in
    90	`/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (+ `systemctl reload sshd`). If they refuse, drop the
    91	host from the fleet inventory and apply manually.
    92	
    93	Verify pubkey auth is allowed before troubleshooting your own keys:
    94	
    95	```sh
    96	ssh -v <host> true 2>&1 | grep "Authentications that can continue"
    97	# Must include `publickey` for fleet-apply to ever work.
    98	```
    99	
   100	If the remote forbids key auth (rare; usually a misconfigured `sshd_config`
   101	with `PubkeyAuthentication no`), edit the remote sshd or remove the host from
   102	the fleet inventory and apply manually:
   103	
   104	```sh
   105	ssh <host>
   106	# inside the remote shell:
   107	chezmoi update --apply
   108	```
   109	
   110	## Detection
   111	
   112	Quick triage when a host shows `unreachable`:
   113	
   114	```sh
   115	# 1. Does manual SSH work?
   116	ssh <host> true && echo "ssh works"
   117	
   118	# 2. Does it work non-interactively (the mode fleet uses)?
   119	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <host> true
   120	# If this prompts or errors → no usable key auth → fleet can't reach it
   121	```
   122	
   123	If step 1 prompts for a password but step 2 errors with `Permission denied
   124	(publickey,password)`, you've hit this pitfall.
   125	
   126	## Related
   127	
   128	- `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema doc (consider
   129	  amending the `password_source` comment to clarify it's sudo-only)
   130	- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` → "Readiness probe" — describes the
   131	  `_classify_readiness` state vocabulary
   132	- `docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md` → "Non-interactive password injection" — the
   133	  consumer side of `password_source` / `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
   134	- `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md` — adjacent sudo-helper trap
```
</details></tool-use>

155: 3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
156: 4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.

158: **Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
159: 
160: ### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
161: 
162: Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
163: 
164: - **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
165: - **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
166: - **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
167: - **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
168: - **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
169: - **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
170: - **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
171:   - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
172:   - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
173:   - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
174:   - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
175: 
176: ### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
177: 
178: - **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
179: - **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
180: 
181: Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
182: 
183: ### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
184: 
185: The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
186: 
187: 1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
188: 2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
189: 
190: **Hard rules**:
191: 
192: - **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
193: - **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
194: - **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
195: - **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
196: 
197: See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
198: 
199: ### Key tmux settings for coding agents

79:- [ ] **[M] fleet-apply long-run sudo session expiry** — `jingle207` ran for 7m50s under `just fleet-apply` and failed at task `Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction` with `sudo: a password is required` even though the run started with `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` populated. Either (a) the sudo password file gets cleaned up by the wrapper's `_cleanup` trap before late tasks need it, or (b) Linux sudo `timestamp_timeout` (default 5m for many distros, 15m for some) expires mid-run and `sudo -S` doesn't re-prompt automatically. Investigation needed: instrument `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` to refresh the cache periodically, or have `sudo_session_init` re-validate via `sudo -S -v -p ''` before each privileged task. See AGENTS.md → "Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts" for the existing contract.
80:- [ ] **[?/M] fleet-apply: optional `sshpass` / interactive-password SSH login support** — currently `password_source` only feeds remote sudo (`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`); SSH login itself is key-only, so password-only hosts classify as `unreachable` in `fleet-status`. Schema comment + new pitfall (`pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`) now document the limitation. Concrete trigger: `zyc_friend` (IDC server, 2026-05-08) has `Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive` — sshd deliberately omits `publickey` AND uses `keyboard-interactive` (PAM) instead of plain `password`, so even after `ssh-copy-id` deposits the key, login still requires the IDC password. A real fix needs: (a) optional `sshpass -f` invocation when `password_source.ssh_login = true` (or a separate `ssh_password_source`), (b) `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password` to handle PAM-only sshds (sshpass defaults to `password` method only), (c) graceful fallback when `sshpass` not installed, (d) parallel-safe (no TTY prompts), (e) opt-in only — default stays key-only for security. Recommended user fix today: ask the IDC admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`, OR remove the host from the fleet and `ssh <host> chezmoi update --apply` manually. Promote when ≥2 hosts in the fleet legitimately can't accept a pubkey.
81:- [ ] **[S] fleet-apply `--serial` mode misses drift downgrade** — `_classify_drift()` in `scripts/fleet/apply.py` correctly downgrades `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` to drift in parallel mode, but `just fleet-apply-one HOST` (which uses `--serial`) reports `rc=1` for the same condition instead of `drift`. Verified on `hanru_mac` 2026-04-24: only diff was `~/.config/worktrunk` directory mode (40700 → 40755), and serial-mode reported failed; identical condition under parallel was correctly classified. Likely a code path that bypasses `_classify_drift` when `--serial` is passed.
108:- [ ] **[?/XL] Raycast config sync for non-Pro users** — git-tracked, redacted cross-machine sync for hotkeys / quicklinks / snippets / aliases / extensions. Full scaffold was built (key-name redactor, extensions-manifest walker, secrets.env.example emitter, chezmoi `syncRaycast` prompt with 3-file parity, `just raycast-*` recipes) but paused: Raycast's `.rayconfig` export is AES-encrypted with a non-public KDF that mixes in keychain-bound material — we brute-forced 150+ scheme combinations (PBKDF2/scrypt/SHA*/EVP_BytesToKey) against password `12345678` with zero plausible decodes, and Raycast forces a non-empty password field so even the empty-password bypass is closed. Cheapest revival spike: inspect the separate `Export Quicklinks` / `Export Snippets` commands for a plaintext format. Adjacent pitfall (`raycast-library-files-not-portable-across-machines.md`) stays live. → [research](backlog/raycast-sync-non-pro.md)
133:- ✅ **fleet-apply: `self` (local) host stuck-running** (2026-05) — `run_one_local` was using `await proc.wait()` which on asyncio waits for stream EOF, not OS-level process exit. Orphan grandchildren of chezmoi (ansible/brew/mas children that survived the `run_onchange_*` scripts) held our stdout/stderr fds open, so the wait never returned and the live table tickered the elapsed clock indefinitely. Fixed via `os.kill(pid, 0)` polling on the actual chezmoi PID, plus 5s grace cancel of the `_drain` tasks. Tested with synthetic orphan-child scenario (60s → 2s). → [pitfall](pitfalls/fleet-apply-self-stuck-running.md) (option-3 walkthrough including the false-summit option-1 attempt)

213	## Readiness probe (`just fleet-status`)
214	
215	`fleet-apply` defaults to `chezmoi update --init`, which is **three things in
216	sequence** under the hood:
217	
218	1. `git -C <source> pull` — bring in new template commits
219	2. `chezmoi init` — re-render `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` (re-evaluates `promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` calls; **NEW prompt keys without saved answers will fail non-interactively** with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY`)
220	3. `chezmoi apply` — render templates, write targets, run `run_*` scripts (ansible, Brewfile, etc.)
221	
222	The readiness probe inspects each host once over SSH and predicts what each of
223	those three sub-steps would do, **without changing anything**. Cheaper than
224	`fleet-apply-dry-run` (which runs full `chezmoi diff`) and more actionable
225	than `fleet-apply-status` (which only sees live processes, not pending
226	drift / missing init / new prompt keys).
227	
228	```bash
229	just fleet-status                              # all hosts, with `git fetch`
230	just fleet-status --hosts lab-box,vps-tokyo    # subset
231	just fleet-status-quick                        # skip remote `git fetch` (faster, may show stale 'behind')
232	just fleet-status --readiness-json | jq .      # machine-readable
233	```
234	
235	### State matrix
236	
237	The probe classifies each host into exactly one primary state and zero or
238	more secondary notes (e.g. a `behind` host with drift will show
239	`behind: 3 commits, drift: 2 files` in the notes column).
240	
241	| State | Symbol | Meaning | Recovery |
242	|---|---|---|---|
243	| `up-to-date` | ✓ green | Source dir at `origin/HEAD`, no drift, init done | Nothing to do |
244	| `ready-to-update` | ↻ blue | Source is behind origin → `fleet-apply` will pull + apply cleanly | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
245	| `behind` | → cyan | Same as `ready-to-update` but used when there are also other notes (drift / dirty co-existing) | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
246	| `drift` | ⚠ yellow | Remote target was hand-edited; would trigger "could not open a new TTY" prompt without `--force`. With default `--keep-going`, applies the rest of the fleet and skips this file | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a `*.local` override |
247	| `dirty` | ⚠ yellow | Remote source dir has uncommitted changes (someone hand-edited the template on the remote) | ssh in & commit/stash before applying |
248	| `ahead` | ? magenta | Remote source dir has local commits not on origin — `git pull` would diverge | ssh in & `git push` or reset before applying |
249	| `busy` | ⏳ yellow | A `chezmoi update/apply/init` or `ansible-playbook` is already running, OR the chezmoi state lock is held | Wait, then re-probe; OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state |
250	| `init-in-progress` | ⏳ yellow | Source dir is missing/incomplete BUT a `chezmoi update/apply/init` PID is alive — typically mid-clone, or paused at an interactive prompt in another SSH session. Distinct from `no-source` (which is permanent until human intervention) | Wait for the in-flight init to finish, OR ssh in & check the other session |
251	| `toml-mismatch` | ! yellow bold | The local `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` declares prompt keys (`promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` / etc.) that are missing from the remote's saved `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. **This is the `david_ubuntu` failure mode** — `fleet-apply` will crash on this host with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY` on `chezmoi init` | ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts |
252	| `not-init` | ✗ red | `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` doesn't exist — host was never `chezmoi init`'d | ssh in & run `chezmoi init` interactively (one-off; needs TTY) |
253	| `no-source` | ✗ red | `chezmoi source-path` returns nothing or the path is not a git repo | ssh in & re-init (or fix custom `chezmoi.toml` `sourceDir =`) |
254	| `no-chezmoi` | ✗ red | `chezmoi` binary not found in augmented PATH | ssh in & install chezmoi (`curl https://chezmoi.io/get \| sh`) |
255	| `unreachable` | ✗ red | SSH connection failed (timeout, auth, host key, network) | check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent |
256	
257	### Output format
258	
259	```
260	fleet-status — readiness probe across 6 host(s)
261	                                readiness probe
262	┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
263	┃ host       ┃ state                  ┃ notes                                    ┃
264	┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
265	│ self       │ ✓ up-to-date           │                                          │
266	│ hanru_mac  │ ↻ ready-to-update      │ behind: 3 commits                        │
267	│ ts_nas     │ ⏳ busy                │ pids=12345                               │
268	│ jingle207  │ ⚠ drift                │ drift: .config/mise/config.toml          │
269	│ david_ub   │ ! toml-mismatch        │ missing prompt keys: installTunnelTools  │
270	│ idc-srv    │ ✗ unreachable          │ TimeoutError: 30s                        │
271	└────────────┴────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘
272	
273	Hints:
274	  ✗ unreachable (1: idc-srv)
275	      → check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent
276	  ! toml-mismatch (1: david_ub)
277	      → ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts (their default values are usually fine)
278	  ⏳ busy (1: ts_nas)
279	      → wait for the running run, OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state
280	  ⚠ drift (1: jingle207)
281	      → `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a *.local override
282	  ↻ ready-to-update (1: hanru_mac)
283	      → `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` (or whole fleet)
284	
285	Summary: 2/6 hosts ready for `just fleet-apply`, 4 need attention
286	```
287	
288	### Exit code
289	
290	Always 0 (probe is informational). Use `--readiness-json` and parse for
291	fine-grained gating in CI:
292	
293	```bash
294	# Pre-apply gate: refuse to apply if any host is unreachable.
295	if just fleet-status --readiness-json | jq -e 'any(.state == "unreachable")' >/dev/null; then
296	    echo "abort: at least one host unreachable"
297	    exit 1
298	fi
299	just fleet-apply
300	```
301	
302	### How `toml-mismatch` works
303	
304	The probe greps the **local** `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` for `promptBool` /
305	`promptString` / `promptInt` / `promptChoice` (with or without `Once`)
306	calls and extracts the second positional argument (the prompt key name).
307	Then it compares against the set of top-level keys in the remote's saved
308	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. Any keys missing on the remote = the
309	remote will trigger an interactive prompt during `chezmoi update --init`,
310	which has no TTY → fails with the familiar `could not open a new TTY`.
311	
312	False positives are unlikely — only newly-added prompt keys trigger this
313	state. False negatives are possible (e.g. if you wrap a prompt in a
314	template conditional that the remote's profile evaluates to false), but
315	those don't actually break `fleet-apply` either, so they're not a regression.
316	
317	### Empty inventory UX
318	
319	`just fleet-status` on a fresh box without `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`
320	exits 0 with:
321	
322	```
323	no fleet configured yet — Fleet config not found: ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
324	hint: run `just fleet-edit` to add machines, then re-run `just fleet-status`.
325	```
326	
327	`just fleet-edit` itself seeds an empty template (with `[defaults]` and a
328	commented-out `[[hosts]]` example) on first run, so you don't need to
329	remember the schema. `just fleet-apply` keeps its old strict behaviour
330	(exit 2 on missing config) — readiness is the only command that's
331	forgiving here.
332	
333	## Inventory file
334	
335	Path: `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. Seeded **once** by chezmoi from
336	[`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl).
337	[`just az-dev-vm`](az-dev-vm.md) also appends/updates a `[[hosts]]` entry here
338	automatically when it provisions an Azure dev VM (and removes it on
339	`az-dev-vm-down`).
340	The `create_private_` prefix means:
341	
342	- `create_` → chezmoi seeds the file on first apply, then never touches it
343	  again. Your edits survive every `chezmoi apply`.
344	- `private_` → file mode 0600. Safe to keep plaintext sudo passwords here.
345	- To reset the seed: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
346	
347	### Schema
348	
349	```toml
350	[defaults]                    # merged into every host (host keys override)
351	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # PATH binary; e.g. "~/.local/bin/chezmoi" if no-root
352	connect_timeout = 15
353	command_timeout = 1800
354	
355	[[hosts]]
356	name            = "lab-box"   # required, unique display name
357	ssh_alias       = "lab-box"   # preferred: matches `Host lab-box` in ~/.ssh/config
358	# OR explicit connection (used when no ssh_alias):
359	hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
360	user            = "dwlee"
361	port            = 22
362	identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
363	
364	no_root_machine = false       # MUST mirror the chezmoi `noRoot=` value used at
365	                              # `chezmoi init` time on that remote (see below)
366	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # override defaults per-host
367	local           = false       # set true to run chezmoi locally (no SSH); see
368	                              # "Local host execution" section below
369	extra_env       = { FOO = "bar" }   # extra env vars for the remote chezmoi run
370	
371	password_source = { type = "...", ... }   # see "Password sources" below
372	```
373	
374	### Password sources
375	
376	| `type` | Extra keys | Behaviour |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| `none` (default) | — | No password injected. Suitable for `no_root_machine = true` hosts. |
379	| `plain` | `value = "..."` | Read straight from TOML. Relies on file mode 0600. |
380	| `prompt` | — | `getpass()` once at startup, never persisted to disk. |
381	| `bitwarden` | `item = "ssh-host-sudo"` | `bw get password <item>` at startup. Requires `bw unlock` + `BW_SESSION` exported. |
382	
383	### `no_root_machine` semantics
384	
385	This flag **describes** the remote, it does not change it. Each remote was
386	configured at `chezmoi init` time with a `noRoot` boolean (see
387	[`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48`](../../.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)) that's now baked into
388	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` on that machine.
389	
390	- Set `no_root_machine = true` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = true` —
391	  fleet_apply skips sudo entirely (no password file written, run-scripts'
392	  `sudo_session_init` returns "non-interactive" branch and skips sudo work).
393	- Set `no_root_machine = false` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = false`
394	## How sudo password reaches the remote
395	
396	`scripts/fleet/apply.py` does **not** echo the password into the command line.
397	The remote command (assembled by `build_remote_command()`) reads stdin into
398	`~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` (mode 0600, `umask 077`), exports
399	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=$PWD/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass`, runs
400	`chezmoi update`, then `trap … EXIT` removes the file (even on crash).
401	
402	On the remote, `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh::sudo_session_init` was extended
403	with a non-interactive injection path: when `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
404	points to a readable file, the password is validated with `sudo -S -v`, then
405	adopted into the shared state dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/`)
406	exactly the same way an interactive prompt would be — including the watchdog
407	that holds the sudo timestamp warm and writes `ansible-become.yml` for
408	ansible roles. **Subsequent run-scripts inside the same `chezmoi update` see
409	the cached state and never re-prompt.**
410	
411	Pass file lifecycle:
412	- `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` is the orchestrator's drop-off; removed
413	  by the SSH command's `trap` once chezmoi exits.
414	- `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/sudo.pass` is the shared state dir
415	  managed by `sudo_shared.sh`; cleaned up by the existing watchdog when the
416	  ancestor `chezmoi` PID exits.
417	
418	## Connection: ssh_config alias vs explicit
419	
420	`asyncssh.connect(host=...)` reads `~/.ssh/config` like the OpenSSH client.
421	Prefer `ssh_alias`:
422	
423	```
424	# ~/.ssh/config
425	Host lab-box
426	    HostName 10.0.0.42
427	    User dwlee
428	    ProxyJump bastion
429	    IdentityAgent ~/.1password/agent.sock     # 1Password SSH agent
430	```
431	
432	```toml
```
