```text
1	# Upgrades — Explicit, Opt-in Tool Refresh
2	
3	> How to actually move installed tools forward on a machine managed by this repo, and why `chezmoi apply` deliberately will *not* do that for you.
4	
5	> **See also**: [`tool-managers.md`](tool-managers.md) — the install-side companion to this doc. It maps every tool in the repo to its install mechanism (which manager owns it, where it lands, per-OS dispatch). When you're trying to figure out "why doesn't `just upgrade-X` move tool Y forward?", that's where the coverage gaps are documented.
6	
7	## Why install and upgrade are split
8	
9	`chezmoi apply` (and the ansible phase it triggers) is **install-only by design**. Ansible roles use `state: present` + `creates:` so that running `chezmoi apply` on a running box is idempotent and never silently bumps every tool to whatever happens to be latest that day. This matters because:
10	
11	- **Predictability** — rerunning apply after editing one role file shouldn't ripple-upgrade unrelated tools.
12	- **Offline / flaky network** — install-only can be satisfied by what's already on disk; `--upgrade` workflows always hit the network.
13	- **Review friction** — you *want* to see "chezmoi says 10 casks would move; proceed?" as a separate decision from "apply my dotfile changes".
14	
15	The explicit upgrade path lives in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh), exposed via `just upgrade-*` recipes in [`justfile`](../../justfile). It is the **only** thing that intentionally moves tools forward on this repo's flow.
16	
17	Two side-effects worth knowing about:
18	
19	- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` entries have `refreshPeriod = "168h"` — chezmoi itself will re-fetch those weekly on apply. That's a bounded "nudge", not an upgrade mechanism for installed binaries.
20	- Homebrew casks that carry a `homebrew_cask` entry with `state: present` freeze to that version until a Brewfile hash change forces a re-bundle with `--no-upgrade`. Still install-only; `upgrade-brew` is what actually bumps them.
21	
22	## Entry points
23	
24	```bash
25	just upgrade-all          # externals → brew → mise → uv → npm → cargo → dotnet → gem → flatpak → warp → agents → plugins
26	just upgrade-dry-run      # same, but commands are printed, not executed
27	just upgrade-<category>   # run one category in isolation
28	```
29	
30	Or use the script directly when you want the flags:
31	
32	```bash
33	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh                           # same as 'all'
34	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh brew uv                   # two categories
35	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --only brew,mise          # same, via --only
36	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --skip agents,plugins     # all, minus those
37	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --dry-run all             # preview
38	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --help
39	```
40	
41	The script runs categories in the canonical `ALL_CATEGORIES` order regardless of CLI arg order — dependencies between categories are real (see [§ Run order](#run-order)).
42	
43	## Category matrix
44	
45	| Category | What actually happens |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `externals` | `chezmoi upgrade` (the chezmoi binary itself) + `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` (force-refresh the 168h externals: oh-my-zsh, TPM, toolkami.rb, fzf). First because a chezmoi version bump may change how later steps behave. |
48	| `brew` | `brew update` → `brew upgrade` → `brew upgrade --cask --greedy` → `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile` *without* `--no-upgrade` → `Brewfile.{darwin,linux}` → `brew cleanup`. macOS pre-warms the shared sudo session via [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) so cask pkg installers that shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` find a live ticket. |
49	| `mise` | `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade` (honours the version constraints in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`). `self-update` warns, rather than fails, when mise was installed via brew/apt. |
50	| `uv` | Detects install style by binary path (Homebrew vs curl-installer) and dispatches to the right channel: `brew upgrade uv` for Homebrew/Linuxbrew installs, `uv self update` for the standalone curl installer. Then `uv tool upgrade --all`. Covers every tool listed in [`python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml) and [`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml). The `python_uv_tools` ansible role does the same dispatch automatically when uv is below `min_uv_version` — see [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md). |
51	| `npm` | `npm -g update`, falling back to `mise exec -- npm -g update` when `npm` is not directly on PATH (same detection as [`js_cli_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml) / [`bitwarden`](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml)). |
52	| `cargo` | If absent, bootstraps the `cargo-update` crate, then `cargo install-update -a`. Covers pueue (Linux) plus any future entries in [`rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
53	| `dotnet` | Parses tool names from [`dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `dotnet tool update --global <name>` per tool (via the mise dotnet shim). Falls back to `dotnet tool list --global` if parsing finds nothing. |
54	| `gem` | `gem update --system` + `gem update` via the mise ruby shim. |
55	| `flatpak` | `flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes` for user-scope Flathub apps (Discord et al. when `discordChannel=flatpak` — see [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md)). Skipped when `flatpak` is absent OR when no user-scope apps are installed. System-scope (`flatpak update --system`) is intentionally NOT covered — it requires `sudo` and is rare in this repo's flow; run manually if needed. |
56	| `warp` | **Linux only.** `sudo apt-get update` + `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal` via the shared sudo session. macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask `warp` + `--greedy`); this category short-circuits with `SKIPPED` on Darwin. The on-disk binary is replaced but the running Warp process is **not** restarted — quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version. The in-app `warp_finish_update <token>` graceful-restart only works from inside a live Warp session (Warp-injected shell function, not on `$PATH` otherwise) — see [`docs/tools/warp.md`](../tools/warp.md) for the full mechanism. |
57	| `agents` | Re-runs the official `curl \| bash` installers for **tools already present** only — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Ollama (Linux), llmfit (Linux), RTK. Bootstrap list mirrors [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml). |
58	| `atuin` | macOS: `brew upgrade atuin` (no-op when atuin was installed via the upstream installer rather than brew). Linux: re-runs `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh \| env ATUIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh` so the upstream installer drops the new binary into `~/.atuin/bin/` while leaving PATH wiring to [`dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh). Skipped with `SKIPPED` if `atuin` is not on PATH. The local SQLite history (`~/.local/share/atuin/`) and config (`~/.config/atuin/config.toml`) are untouched. |
59	| `plugins` | `nvim --headless "+Lazy! sync" +qa` → `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all` → refresh installed `claude-hud` via [`claude_hud_sync.py`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py) → `pre-commit autoupdate` (on the dotfiles repo root) → `tldr --update` → `gh extension upgrade --all`. Each step is guarded on the relevant binary being present. |
60	
61	### Run order
62	
63	```mermaid
64	flowchart LR
65	    externals["externals<br/>(chezmoi + externals)"] --> brew
66	    brew["brew<br/>(formulas + casks greedy + Brewfile)"] --> mise
67	    mise["mise<br/>(self-update + runtimes)"] --> uv
68	    uv["uv<br/>(self update + tools)"] --> npm
69	    npm["npm<br/>(-g update)"] --> cargo
70	    cargo["cargo<br/>(install-update -a)"] --> dotnet
71	    dotnet["dotnet<br/>(tool update --global)"] --> gem
72	    gem["gem<br/>(gem update)"] --> flatpak
73	    flatpak["flatpak<br/>(--user update)"] --> warp
74	    warp["warp<br/>(Linux apt-only)"] --> atuin
75	    atuin["atuin<br/>(brew or setup.atuin.sh)"] --> agents
76	    agents["agents<br/>(curl \| bash installers)"] --> plugins
77	    plugins["plugins<br/>(Lazy, TPM, pre-commit, tldr, gh)"] --> summary((Summary))
78	```
79	
80	Rationale: package managers themselves go first (`externals` to maybe swap chezmoi; `brew` because mise/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem may be Homebrew-installed; `mise` before the language-scoped ones because `mise upgrade` can swap the runtime `npm`/`cargo`/`dotnet`/`gem` belong to). `agents` + `plugins` last because they depend on everything above being current.
81	
82	`claude-hud` stays out of [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl): it uses a versioned cache path and rewrites `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, so it fits the explicit `plugins` upgrade path better than chezmoi externals. Upstream `v0.0.12+` also switched usage rendering to Claude Code's official stdin `rate_limits`, which means the old credential-derived `Max` badge may disappear after upgrade.
83	
84	## Semantics: best-effort, not all-or-nothing
85	
86	Each category is wrapped in a `run_category` helper:
87	
88	- Individual command failures inside a category do **not** abort the rest of the category. Everything is best-effort.
89	- A category failure does **not** abort the next category. The script keeps going.
90	- Categories return `77` when the prerequisite is missing (e.g. no `dotnet` binary) — that is reported as **SKIPPED**, not FAILED.
91	- The final summary groups into three buckets:
92	
93	```text
94	[INFO] Upgrade Summary
95	[SUCCESS] OK:      externals brew mise uv npm cargo agents plugins
96	[WARN] SKIPPED: gem (prerequisite missing)
97	[ERROR] FAILED:  dotnet
98	[ERROR]    - dotnet: rc=1
99	```
100	
101	Overall process exit code is `1` iff at least one category is in FAILED. `--dry-run` always exits `0` because no real command runs.
102	
103	## Sample: `just upgrade-dry-run`
104	
105	```text
106	────────────────────────────────────────────
107	[INFO] upgrade_tools.sh — categories: externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins (dry-run)
108	[WARN] DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed
109	────────────────────────────────────────────
110	[INFO] ── category: externals ──
111	[INFO] Upgrading chezmoi binary itself
112	+ chezmoi upgrade
113	[INFO] Force-refreshing chezmoi externals (.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
114	+ chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
115	[SUCCESS] category 'externals' completed
116	────────────────────────────────────────────
117	[INFO] ── category: brew ──
118	+ brew update
119	+ brew upgrade
120	+ brew upgrade --cask --greedy
121	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
122	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
123	+ brew cleanup
124	[SUCCESS] category 'brew' completed
125	...
126	```
127	
128	## Things intentionally excluded
129	
130	- **No `state: latest` rewrites of ansible roles.** `chezmoi apply` semantics stay conservative; the upgrade path uses package-manager commands directly.
131	- **No `apt upgrade` / system package bumps.** Keeps the default scope sudo-light and noise-free. Run `sudo apt upgrade && sudo apt autoremove` manually if you want that.
132	- **No Linux Steam upgrade category.** The Ubuntu Desktop Steam launcher/runtime packages are apt-managed through Valve's repo, so they move with your normal system apt upgrade cadence; the Steam client itself self-updates on launch. macOS Steam is a Homebrew cask and is covered by `just upgrade-brew`.
133	- **No daemon restart** for LiteLLM / Ollama / pueued / anything `systemd`-managed. We only refresh the binaries; restarting is your call.
134	- **No automatic scheduling.** There is no cron, launchd, or systemd timer wired up. Running `just upgrade-all` is an intentional action you take when you have time to review diffs / deal with breakage.
135	- **`scripts/**` is ignored by chezmoi** ([`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) line 29) — the script is *not* deployed to `$HOME`. It runs from the dotfiles repo checkout directly (where `chezmoi cd` takes you). That is a deliberate choice: upgrade logic is repo-local, not per-user.
136	
137	## Troubleshooting
138	
139	- **`chezmoi upgrade` fails.** `chezmoi upgrade` only works when chezmoi was installed via the official install script or `go install`. Homebrew/apt installs will surface an error — upgrade via *that* channel instead. The script treats this as a warning, not a failure.
140	- **`mise self-update` fails.** mise refuses when installed via a system package manager. Treated as a warning.
141	- **`uv self update` no-ops on Homebrew uv.** Handled automatically — `cat_uv()` detects the install style and runs `brew upgrade uv` instead. See [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md) and [`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
142	- **macOS cask pkg installer hangs on sudo.** The script calls `sudo_session_init "upgrade-brew"` on macOS, which prompts once and warms the ticket. If you ran the script over SSH with no TTY, that step becomes `non-interactive` and cask pkg bumps may stall. Fix: run locally, or `ssh -t`, or pre-warm with `sudo -v` yourself before `just upgrade-brew`.
143	- **`cargo install-update -a` fails halfway through.** One crate break does not abort the rest (best-effort). Re-run `just upgrade-cargo` — cargo-update is itself rebuilt if missing.
144	- **`pre-commit autoupdate` bumped a hook that now errors.** That is a repo-file change, not an environment change. Review `.pre-commit-config.yaml` diff; `git checkout -p .pre-commit-config.yaml` to partially revert if needed.
145	
146	## Extending
147	
148	Three ways to add a new tool to the upgrade flow:
149	
150	1. **Tool already managed by an existing category (brew / uv / npm / cargo / dotnet / gem / mise).** Nothing to do — the generic `upgrade-<category>` picks it up because it uses the package manager's own bulk command.
151	2. **New `curl | bash` installer.** Add a guarded block inside `cat_agents()` in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh). Gate on the binary being present so the upgrade path never bootstraps on machines that don't have the tool.
152	
153	   ```bash
154	   if command -v newtool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
155	     info "Upgrading newtool"
156	     _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://newtool.dev/install.sh | bash" || any_fail=1
157	     ran_any=1
158	   fi
159	   ```
160	
161	3. **Brand-new strategy (e.g. GitHub release binary with custom download logic).** Add a `cat_<name>` function, register it in:
162	   - `ALL_CATEGORIES` array
163	   - The dispatch `case` in the main loop
164	   - A matching `just upgrade-<name>` recipe in [`justfile`](../../justfile)
165	   - This doc's [category matrix](#category-matrix)
166	
167	Keep the return-value contract: `0` = success, `77` = skipped (prerequisite missing), any other non-zero = failure.
168	
169	## Cross-references
170	
171	- [`AGENTS.md` § Hard repo invariants](../../AGENTS.md#install-vs-upgrade-is-split-on-purpose) — short version (install-vs-upgrade rule) written for AI agents touching this repo.
172	- [`README.md` § Keeping tools up-to-date](../../README.md) — short version written for humans arriving from the front page.
173	- [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) — the implementation.
174	- [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) — the sudo-session helper reused for macOS cask installers.
175	- [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) — the `refreshPeriod` entries that `upgrade-externals` force-refreshes.
176	- Ansible role defaults consumed for enumeration: [`dotnet_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`python_uv_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`llm_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml).
177
```
</details></tool-use>

875	## Coverage gaps (install-only, no automated upgrade)
876	
877	Tools that `chezmoi apply` installs but **no `upgrade_tools.sh` category
878	ever refreshes**. These tools stay frozen at install-time version until
879	manually removed and re-installed.
880	
881	| Class | Why no upgrade | How to refresh |
882	|---|---|---|
883	| **GitHub-release user-level fallbacks** (~30 tools — see [§ 11](#11-github-release-downloads-user-level-fallback)) | `creates:` guard means ansible never re-downloads | `rm ~/.local/bin/<tool>` then `chezmoi apply` |
884	| **Vendor apt-repo packages** on Debian (terraform, azure-cli, vscode, opentofu, ngrok, lazygit-from-PPA) | Rely on `sudo apt upgrade` outside this repo | `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` (not chezmoi's job) |
885	| **Docker convenience-script install** | No upgrade target | re-run `curl get.docker.com \| sh` |
886	| **OrbStack** | Macos brew cask | Covered by `cat_brew --cask --greedy` |
887	| **Cursor `.deb`** / **Discord `.deb`** / **VSCode (Microsoft apt)** | apt-side, not chezmoi-side | apt-upgrade |
888	| **Zen Browser AppImage** / **AppImageLauncher Lite** | One-shot download, `creates:` guard | Delete AppImage, re-apply |
889	| **Hack Nerd Font** | `latest` URL, no version tracking | Delete font dir, re-apply |
890	| **fontconfig / libfuse2 / libnotify-bin / playerctl / wmctrl / xdotool** | System packages, no upgrade automation | apt-upgrade |
891	| **auditd rules** | Config files, not a "tool" with versions | Edit rule template, re-apply |
892	| **claude-hud / LazyVim plugins / TPM plugins / pre-commit / tldr cache / gh extensions** | **Covered** by `cat_plugins` in upgrade_tools.sh | `just upgrade-plugins` |
893	
894	**Why this matters**: a developer who runs `just upgrade-all` on a Linux
895	host gets brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + dotnet + gem + flatpak +
896	agents + plugins moved forward. But ~30 GitHub-release-installed CLIs
897	(many of them widely-used: ripgrep, fd, jq, git-delta, lazygit, …)
898	stay pinned to install time forever. This is **partially mitigated**
899	by:
900	
901	- These tools on **macOS** all go via brew, which `cat_brew` covers
902	- On **Linux non-noRoot**, distro packages get apt-upgrade outside the repo
903	- The gap is sharpest on **noRoot Linux** where GitHub releases are
904	  the only install path AND there's no upgrade automation
905	
906	**Coverage gap on `cat_agents`**: only `claude / opencode / cursor-agent
907	/ ollama / llmfit / rtk / specstory` get the self-update-then-curl loop.
908	**Missing**: `agy` (Antigravity), `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar`,
909	`specify-cli`, `openchamber`, `codex` — these rely on brew / uv / npm
910	categories instead.
911	
912	**Tracked on backlog**: no formal item yet, but adding a `releases`
913	category to `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (audit installed binaries
914	against latest GitHub tag, prompt for refresh) would close this. See
915	[upgrades.md](upgrades.md#category-matrix) for the current category
916	list.
917	
918	---
919	
920	## Tool index (A–Z)
```

1	# Research: sshpass / SSH password automation, and how `fleet` handles it
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	User linked https://sshpass.com/ and https://github.com/kevinburke/sshpass and asked (1) whether
6	`sshpass` is the right tool for automating password-based SSH login, what the broader landscape of
7	alternatives looks like, and (2) whether this repo's `fleet` CLI (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`,
8	backed by `scripts/fleet/*.py`) uses a similar technique to connect to fleet hosts.
9	
10	This is a pure research/explanation request — no code or doc changes were requested, and the user
11	didn't respond to confirm scope, so per the "just answer" default: **no files will be modified.**
12	The deliverable is a direct chat answer, synthesizing external research with the exact mechanism this
13	repo already uses (and has already documented as a deliberate, non-obvious design decision).
14	
15	## What to deliver (chat answer, no file edits)
16	
17	### Part 1 — sshpass and the broader landscape
18	
19	- **What `sshpass` is**: a thin wrapper that answers OpenSSH's interactive password prompt
20	  non-interactively, via a pty trick. Two forks exist: the original (farrokhi, SourceForge mirror)
21	  and `kevinburke/sshpass` (a GitHub mirror of the same SourceForge source, read-only, no PR
22	  acceptance — not a functional fork, just a mirror for `go get`-able/brew-tap-able access).
23	- **Security tiers of sshpass's own flags** (worst → best):
24	  - `-p <pass>` — plaintext on argv, visible to any local user via `ps`. Worst option.
25	  - `-e` (`SSHPASS` env var) — not in `ps` output, but still readable via `/proc/<pid>/environ` on Linux.
26	  - `-f <file>` — password from a file descriptor/path; best when combined with `chmod 0400`. This is
27	    the "least bad" way to use sshpass if you must.
28	- **Why sshpass is broadly discouraged for production/scripted use**: plaintext password has to exist
29	  *somewhere* (env, file, vault) for sshpass to read it; it doesn't eliminate the "credential at rest"
30	  problem, it just moves where the plaintext briefly lives. Compliance frameworks (PCI-DSS/HIPAA/CIS)
31	  generally frown on plaintext-password SSH automation.
32	- **Better alternatives, roughly in order of preference for automation**:
33	  1. **SSH key-based auth** (ed25519/rsa key + `ssh-copy-id`) — no password in the loop at all; the
34	     gold standard for scripted/unattended SSH.
35	  2. **ssh-agent / IdentityAgent forwarding** (incl. 1Password SSH agent, YubiKey-backed keys) — keys
36	     never touch disk unencrypted; agent handles signing.
37	  3. **`expect`** — scriptable interactive-session automation; more flexible than sshpass (can handle
38	     arbitrary prompts, 2FA flows) but still needs the secret sourced from somewhere.
39	  4. **Secrets managers** (Vault, Bitwarden/1Password CLI, AWS Secrets Manager) feeding into key
40	     material or short-lived credentials, rather than long-lived plaintext passwords.
41	  5. **Library-level SSH with password auth** (Python `paramiko` supports password auth directly;
42	     `asyncssh` supports it too but is typically used for concurrent/async key-based fleets) — only
43	     meaningfully safer than sshpass if the password itself is sourced securely (vault/keyring), since
44	     the library still needs the plaintext in memory at connect time.
45	  - Net: **the tool matters less than where the plaintext secret lives and how briefly**. Keys avoid
46	    the problem entirely; sshpass/expect/paramiko-password all still require a plaintext secret at
47	    some point, so the real differentiator is secret sourcing + minimizing exposure window, not the
48	    ssh-automation tool itself.
49	
50	### Part 2 — how `fleet` in this repo actually works (verified from code + existing docs)
51	
52	Direct, concrete answer to "does fleet use something like sshpass": **No — fleet deliberately never
53	uses sshpass or any password for the SSH *login* itself.** Two completely separate stages, confirmed
54	by both code and this repo's own pitfall doc:
55	
56	| Stage | Mechanism | Uses `password_source` / sshpass-like technique? |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| SSH login (transport) | `asyncssh.connect(**kwargs)` in `scripts/fleet/apply.py:_connect_kwargs` (558-578) — `client_keys` from `identity_file`, else falls back to `~/.ssh/config` + local ssh-agent (incl. 1Password SSH agent via `IdentityAgent`), exactly like the OpenSSH client. **`password=` is never passed.** | No |
59	| Remote `sudo` (after login) | `password_source` (`plain` / `prompt` / `bitwarden` / `none`) resolved in `resolve_passwords()` (apply.py:193-235); value is written to the **already-authenticated SSH channel's stdin** on the remote (`proc.stdin.write(...)`, no PTY, no argv, no env var) and consumed remotely via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` by `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` (`sudo_run` pipes it to `sudo -S` via file redirection, never argv/env). | Yes, but this is sudo-only, not SSH-login |
60	
61	Key files to point at if the user wants to read code directly:
62	- `scripts/fleet/apply.py` — `Host` dataclass (61-90), `load_hosts`/`resolve_passwords` (103-235),
63	  `build_remote_command` (242-488, sudo-file injection ~419-430), `_connect_kwargs` (558-578),
64	  `run_one` (829-980, stdin password feed ~883-900).
65	- `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — `sudo_session_init` (179-302), `sudo_run` (304-316).
66	- `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema, with an explicit comment (lines 8-13)
67	  warning that `password_source` does **not** cover SSH login.
68	- `pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md` — the authoritative writeup of exactly
69	  this SSH-vs-sudo distinction, including the real-world trigger host (`zyc_friend`, an IDC server with
70	  `PubkeyAuthentication no` + PAM `keyboard-interactive` sshd) and why sshpass wouldn't even trivially
71	  fix that case (needs `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`).
72	- `TODO.md:80` — an existing, still-open, deliberately-deferred backlog item: *optional* sshpass /
73	  interactive-password SSH login support, opt-in only, for the rare password-only host. Design already
74	  sketched (per-host `ssh_login` password gate, PAM preferred-auth flag, graceful fallback if sshpass
75	  missing, parallel-safety concern since `fleet-apply` runs hosts concurrently and a TTY prompt would
76	  deadlock the orchestrator).
77	
78	Why fleet is built this way (already documented as deliberate, not an oversight):
79	1. Avoids an extra binary dependency (`sshpass`) most hosts don't need.
80	2. Parallel `fleet-apply` runs N hosts concurrently — an interactive password prompt would deadlock.
81	3. Security posture: nudges every fleet host toward key-based auth rather than password auth.
82	
83	### Answer to give the user
84	
85	Explain both halves conversationally: (a) sshpass's role/security tiers/alternatives in general, with
86	sources; (b) fleet's actual behavior — key/agent-only SSH login, sudo password piped over an
87	already-authenticated channel via stdin (never argv/env, never sshpass) — and point to the exact
88	pitfall doc + TODO item already tracking the known gap (password-only hosts like `zyc_friend`) in case
89	the user wants to act on it later.
90	
91	## Verification
92	
93	N/A — no code changes. This plan's execution is a chat response citing the file:line locations above
94	(user can `cat`/open them to verify) plus the external sources gathered:
95	- https://sshpass.com/are-there-alternatives-to-sshpass-for-secure-automation/
96	- https://www.cyberciti.biz/faq/noninteractive-shell-script-ssh-password-provider/
97	- https://frontegg.com/blog/ssh-password-authentication-security-risks-and-top-5-alternatives
98	- https://computingforgeeks.com/sshpass-ssh-login-with-password-linux-macos/
99	- https://linux.die.net/man/1/sshpass
100	- https://github.com/kevinburke/sshpass (mirror repo itself)
101

---
# Security tools role - pre-commit and gitleaks for secret scanning
#
# pre-commit is installed via `uv tool install --python 3.13` on BOTH macOS and
# Linux so the Python bootstrap is identical across machines. This avoids the
# macOS Homebrew `python@3.14` pyexpat / libexpat ABI mismatch that breaks
# virtualenv creation for hook repos (symptom:
# `Symbol not found: _XML_SetAllocTrackerActivationThreshold`). See
# `docs/tools/pre-commit.md` for the full rationale.
#
# `uv` itself is installed by `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` before any
# ansible role runs, so we can depend on it here unconditionally.

- name: Check uv is available (prereq for pre-commit install)
  ansible.builtin.command: uv --version
  register: uv_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Fail if uv is missing
  when: uv_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.fail:
    msg: >-
      `uv` not found on PATH — pre-commit install depends on it.
      Re-run `chezmoi apply` so `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`
      can install uv, or install it manually from https://astral.sh/uv.

- name: Install pre-commit via uv (pinned Python 3.13, all OSes)
  ansible.builtin.command: uv tool install pre-commit --python 3.13
  register: precommit_install
  changed_when: "'already installed' not in (precommit_install.stdout | default('') ~ precommit_install.stderr | default(''))"

- name: Install gitleaks (macOS)
  # Go is managed by mise (dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl, gated on
  # installExtraRuntimes), not brew — keeps the language runtime cross-platform
  # and out of the security_tools role. Only gitleaks belongs here.
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - gitleaks
    state: present

- name: Check if gitleaks is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.command: gitleaks version
  register: gitleaks_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Get latest gitleaks version
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
    - gitleaks_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.uri:
    url: https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/latest
    return_content: true
  register: gitleaks_release

- name: Install gitleaks binary (Debian/Ubuntu, system-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gitleaks_check.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Set gitleaks version and arch (system)
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        gitleaks_version: "{{ gitleaks_release.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}"
        gitleaks_arch: >-
          {{
            'x64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else 'armv7' if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armhf']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Skip gitleaks on unsupported architecture (system)
      when: gitleaks_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "Unsupported architecture for gitleaks: {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Download gitleaks (system)
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v{{ gitleaks_version }}/gitleaks_{{ gitleaks_version }}_linux_{{ gitleaks_arch }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        mode: "0644"
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Extract gitleaks (system)
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp
        remote_src: true

    - name: Install gitleaks to /usr/local/bin
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /tmp/gitleaks
        dest: /usr/local/bin/gitleaks
        mode: "0755"
        remote_src: true

    - name: Clean up gitleaks temp files (system)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        - /tmp/gitleaks
        - /tmp/LICENSE
        - /tmp/README.md

  rescue:
    - name: Warn gitleaks system install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "gitleaks system-level installation failed — skipping (will try user-level fallback)"

    - name: Clean up gitleaks temp files after failure (system)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        - /tmp/gitleaks
        - /tmp/LICENSE
        - /tmp/README.md

# --- gitleaks (user-level fallback) ---
- name: Re-check if gitleaks is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v gitleaks
  register: gitleaks_recheck
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install gitleaks from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
    - gitleaks_recheck.rc != 0
    - gitleaks_arch_user | default('') | trim != ''
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (gitleaks)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest gitleaks release (user)
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: gitleaks_release_user

    - name: Set gitleaks version and arch (user)
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        gitleaks_version_user: "{{ gitleaks_release_user.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}"
        gitleaks_arch_user: >-
          {{
            'x64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else 'armv7' if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armhf']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Download gitleaks (user)
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v{{ gitleaks_version_user }}/gitleaks_{{ gitleaks_version_user }}_linux_{{ gitleaks_arch_user }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        mode: "0644"
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Extract gitleaks (user)
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp
        remote_src: true

    - name: Install gitleaks to ~/.local/bin
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /tmp/gitleaks
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/gitleaks"
        mode: "0755"
        remote_src: true

    - name: Clean up gitleaks temp files (user)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        - /tmp/gitleaks
        - /tmp/LICENSE
        - /tmp/README.md

  rescue:
    - name: Warn gitleaks user install failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "gitleaks user-level installation failed — skipping"

    - name: Clean up gitleaks temp files after failure (user)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/gitleaks.tar.gz
        - /tmp/gitleaks
        - /tmp/LICENSE
        - /tmp/README.md

149:### Why `centos_server` is its own profile (and not auto-detected)
151:Per [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) the rule is *profile is for user-role choices, OS/arch facts go through `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch`*. CentOS-vs-Ubuntu looks like an OS fact at first glance — chezmoi exposes `.chezmoi.osRelease.id` natively, so we *could* split `ubuntu_server` behaviour by sniffing the distro. We deliberately don't:
153:- Profile names are the existing UX surface — the ansible router script in `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` already branches on `.profile`, so adding `centos_server` keeps the divergent role behaviour discoverable in one place.
154:- Inside ansible roles, `ansible_os_family` (Debian / RedHat) does the package-manager disambiguation independently. The chezmoi profile picks **playbook + tag set**; ansible facts pick **package manager**. The two layers don't fight.
155:- The carve-out is narrow: package-manager *family* is load-bearing for which roles can run. Future RedHat-family additions (Fedora, Alma, Rocky) all reuse `centos_server` — no new profile per distro.
157:#### Local install-test for `centos_server`
168:Both base images are gated behind compose profiles (`centos`, `rocky`) so default `docker compose up` still only builds the Ubuntu devbox.
197:Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit OS only) works with the `ubuntu_server` profile and gets full tool support. Raspberry Pi 4 may run 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (armhf userland) with a 64-bit kernel (`arm_64bit=1` default), which causes `uname -m` to report `aarch64` while userland is 32-bit.

## 1. `mkdocs.yml` — full nav structure and exact syntax patterns

  - `mkdocs.yml:368` — inside the main `nav: → Repo Internals:` list

- `docs/tools/pueue.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md` all live under `nav: → Tools: → Productivity:` (lines 306–320):

**Exact nav syntax pattern** (`- "Title": path/to/file.md`, quoted only when title contains special YAML chars like parens/colons): e.g. `- "fleet hosts": tools/fleet-hosts.md`. To add a **new page**, you'd insert a new `- Title: tools/new-page.md` line in the appropriate list; to add a **new section to an existing page**, no `mkdocs.yml` change is needed at all — only a new `##`/`###` heading inside the existing `.md` file (anchors are auto-generated by the `toc:` extension, `mkdocs.yml:215-221`).

**Bilingual convention**: This repo uses the `i18n` plugin (`docs_structure: suffix`, `mkdocs.yml:47-176`). Nearly every page has a `*.zh-TW.md` sibling (confirmed `fleet-apply.zh-TW.md` exists). If a new page title isn't already covered by an existing `nav_translations:` mapping, one must be added under `plugins: → i18n: → languages: → zh-TW: → nav_translations:` (lines 58-176). If it's a new **section** in an existing page (no new nav title), no `nav_translations` change is needed — only the zh-TW content mirror.

**Most important finding — an existing pitfall doc is the canonical source of truth for this exact problem**: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`. It documents:
- `password_source` is **sudo-only**; SSH login uses `BatchMode=yes` key/agent auth with **no `sshpass` involvement**.
- Root cause in `scripts/fleet/apply.py::_resolve_passwords()` / `build_remote_command()`.
- The `zyc_friend` (IDC server) real-world trigger: sshd advertises `Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive` (no `publickey`), so even `ssh-copy-id` doesn't fix it — needs `sshpass` **and** `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password`.
- Its own "Related" section (lines 126-134) explicitly says: `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema doc (consider amending the `password_source` comment to clarify it's sudo-only) and points at `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` → "Readiness probe" and `docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md` → "Non-interactive password injection".

```

## 6. `TODO.md` — exact line and format for the existing entry

File: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/TODO.md` (144 lines total). The exact entry, at **line 80**, under the `## P3 — Someday / nice to have` section (header at line 71):

```
80:- [ ] **[?/M] fleet-apply: optional `sshpass` / interactive-password SSH login support** — currently `password_source` only feeds remote sudo (`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`); SSH login itself is key-only, so password-only hosts classify as `unreachable` in `fleet-status`. Schema comment + new pitfall (`pitfalls/fleet-apply-password-source-not-for-ssh-login.md`) now document the limitation. Concrete trigger: `zyc_friend` (IDC server, 2026-05-08) has `Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive` — sshd deliberately omits `publickey` AND uses `keyboard-interactive` (PAM) instead of plain `password`, so even after `ssh-copy-id` deposits the key, login still requires the IDC password. A real fix needs: (a) optional `sshpass -f` invocation when `password_source.ssh_login = true` (or a separate `ssh_password_source`), (b) `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password` to handle PAM-only sshds (sshpass defaults to `password` method only), (c) graceful fallback when `sshpass` not installed, (d) parallel-safe (no TTY prompts), (e) opt-in only — default stays key-only for security. Recommended user fix today: ask the IDC admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`, OR remove the host from the fleet and `ssh <host> chezmoi update --apply` manually. Promote when ≥2 hosts in the fleet legitimately can't accept a pubkey.
```

**Exact checkbox/tag conventions** confirmed from surrounding lines (73-95):
- Checkbox: `- [ ] ` (unchecked; presumably `- [x] ` when done, though no example currently in this file — nearby resolved items like `backlog/fleet-exec.md` just get their TODO line **deleted** entirely rather than checked off, based on the "Resolution" pattern seen there).
- Priority/effort tag: bold, bracketed, `**[PRIORITY/EFFORT] Title** — description`. Priority values seen: `P?`-tier items use `[?/M]`, `[?/S]`, `[?/L]` (uncertain priority, known effort); the `## P3` section also has plain `[S]`, `[M]`, `[L]` tags without `?` once priority is settled (e.g. line 73 `[S]`, line 86 `[L]`). A real fix needs: (a) optional `sshpass -f` invocation when `password_source.ssh_login = true` (or a separate `ssh_password_source`), (b) `-o PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password` to handle PAM-only sshds (sshpass defaults to `password` method only), (c) graceful fallback when `sshpass` not installed, (d) parallel-safe (no TTY prompts), (e) opt-in only — default stays key-only for security. Recommended user fix today: ask the IDC admin to enable `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`, OR remove the host from the fleet and `ssh &lt;host&gt; chezmoi update --apply` manually. # Research Report: fleet-apply SSH password-login support (TODO.md:80)

## 1. `scripts/fleet/apply.py`

### PEP 723 header (lines 1–9)
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
```
Only three deps today, no `sshpass`/`expect`/`paramiko`. This matters for point 5 below.

### `Host` dataclass (lines 64–90)
```python
PasswordSourceType = Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Host:
    name: str
    ssh_alias: str | None = None
    hostname: str | None = None
    user: str | None = None
    port: int | None = None
    identity_file: str | None = None
    no_root_machine: bool = False
    chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
    local: bool = False
    extra_env: dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
    # Resolved later (not from TOML directly)
    password_source_type: PasswordSourceType = "none"
    password_source_arg: str | None = None  # plain value, bw item id, etc.
    sudo_password: str | None = None  # populated by resolve_passwords()
```
No SSH-login-password field exists today. A new field (e.g. `ssh_login_password: str | None = None` plus a resolved `ssh_login_password_source_type`/`_arg` pair, mirroring the sudo naming) would slot in right after `sudo_password`.

### `load_hosts()` (lines 103–159)
Parses `[[hosts]]` + merges `[defaults]`. The `password_source` nested table is popped and normalized to a flat `(type, arg)` pair, then filtered against `Host`'s actual field names before construction:
```python
merged = {**defaults, **raw}
ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
    raise ValueError(...)
ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")

host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
host = Host(**host_kwargs, password_source_type=ps_type, password_source_arg=ps_arg)
```
Because it uses `dataclasses.fields(Host)` to filter unknown keys, adding a new field to `Host` is enough for `load_hosts` to accept it from TOML directly (no parser changes needed) — but a *nested table* like a hypothetical `ssh_login = { password_source = {...} }` would need the same manual `.pop()`+normalize treatment as `password_source` above (a flat top-level key would be simpler and reuse the existing dispatch pattern almost verbatim).

### `resolve_passwords()` + `_bw_get_password()` (lines 168–235)
```python
def _bw_get_password(item: str) -> str:
    """Call `bw get password <item>`; raise on failure with a helpful message."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(["bw", "get", "password", item], capture_output=True,
                                 text=True, timeout=30, check=False)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise RuntimeError("`bw` (Bitwarden CLI) not found in PATH — ...") from e
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"bw get password {item!r} failed (rc={result.returncode}): ...")
    return result.stdout.strip("\n")

def resolve_passwords(hosts: list[Host], console: Console) -> list[Host]:
    for h in hosts:
        if h.password_source_type == "none":
            continue
        if h.password_source_type == "plain":
            h.sudo_password = h.password_source_arg or ""
            ...
        if h.password_source_type == "prompt":
            try:
                h.sudo_password = getpass.getpass(f"sudo password for [{h.name}] ...")
            except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
                h.sudo_password = None
            continue
        if h.password_source_type == "bitwarden":
            ...
            h.sudo_password = _bw_get_password(h.password_source_arg)
    return hosts
```
Dispatch is a flat `type` string ("plain"/"prompt"/"bitwarden"/"none") mutating `sudo_password` in-place. This is a directly reusable pattern for a second password channel (`ssh_login_password`) — you could literally call a parameterized version of this function twice (once for sudo, once for ssh-login) or generalize it to take a `(type, arg)` pair and target attribute name. Note: `prompt` here calls `getpass.getpass()` synchronously once at startup for ALL hosts before the parallel phase begins — this is exactly why an SSH-login "prompt" type would also be safe (it's resolved before `asyncio.gather`, not mid-connection), but a `sshpass`-driven **interactive PAM fallback mid-connect** would not be — see point (e) below on the "no TTY prompts" design constraint.

### `_connect_kwargs()` (lines 558–578) — the single connection-kwargs builder
```python
def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs. ..."""
    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
    if host.user:
        kwargs["username"] = host.user
    if host.port:
        kwargs["port"] = host.port
    if host.identity_file:
        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
    return kwargs
```
Key/agent-only today — no `password`, no `preferred_auth`, no `kbdint_password` kwargs passed to asyncssh. This is the single most important function for the design: **it is the one and only place** that builds `asyncssh.connect()` kwargs across the entire codebase.

### Call sites of `asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(...))`
This is **not duplicated per-command in the sense of re-deriving kwargs** — `_connect_kwargs()` itself is a single shared helper, re-exported via `scripts/fleet/__init__.py`:
```python
from scripts.fleet.apply import (
    DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH, LOCAL_LOG_DIR, REMOTE_LOG_DIR, REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH,
    Host, _connect_kwargs, load_hosts, resolve_passwords,
)
```
But the actual `asyncssh.connect()` **call** (wrapped in `asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout)` + `except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`) is duplicated inline at **10 call sites**:

| File | Line(s) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 875 | `run_one()` — the actual apply |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 1500 | `--kill-orphans` |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 1717 | `--status` |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 2448 | `_collect_readiness_rows()` / `--readiness` (`fleet-status`) |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 2753 | `--compact` |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` | 2959 | `--tail` |
| `scripts/fleet/exec.py` | 259 | `fleet exec` |
| `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` | 240 | `fleet tmux` |
| `scripts/fleet/info.py` | 306 | `fleet info` |
| `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` | 184 | `fleet pueue` |

Every site follows the identical idiom:
```python
connect_kw = _connect_kwargs(host)  # (or inline **_connect_kwargs(h))
async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
    conn = await asyncssh.connect(**connect_kw)
```
**Design implication**: if you make `_connect_kwargs()` conditionally return a `password=`/`preferred_auth=` kwarg when an opt-in SSH-login password source is configured, **all 10 call sites get it for free** with zero other code changes — this is the cleanest insertion point, not a per-command retrofit.

### `_classify_readiness()` (lines 2009–2106)
Signature: `def _classify_readiness(fields: dict[str, str], drift: list[str], expected_keys: set[str]) -> tuple[str, list[str]]`. This function only maps *already-fetched* probe fields to a state string — it never touches SSH errors directly. The `unreachable` state instead comes from the **caller**, `_collect_readiness_rows()` (lines 2408–2461):
```python
async def _probe_one(h: Host) -> dict:
    row: dict = {"host": h.name, "state": "unreachable", "notes": [], "fields": {}, "drift": [], "error": None}
    ...
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
            conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(h))
        async with conn:
            result = await conn.run(probe_cmd, check=False)
        stdout = result.stdout or ""
    except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
        row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        return row          # <-- row["state"] stays "unreachable" (the default)
    ...
```
**Exact exception handling**: `except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)` — this is the *only* catch clause across all 6 apply.py call sites (and identical in exec/tmux/info/pueue). `asyncssh.PermissionDenied` is a subclass of `asyncssh.Error`, so it's already caught generically, not special-cased. **This is exactly the insertion point for a key→password fallback**: wrap the `conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(h))` line in a try/except that catches `asyncssh.PermissionDenied` specifically, and on that exception (and only if an opt-in ssh-login password is configured) retries `asyncssh.connect()` with `password=`/`preferred_auth=` added. Because this exact block is repeated 10 times, the fallback logic would ideally live in a **new shared helper** (e.g. `async def _connect(host) -> asyncssh.SSHClientConnection`) that all 10 call sites adopt — which would also be the natural refactor per `scripts/fleet/__init__.py`'s own TODO comment: *"Eventually the shared `Host`/`load_hosts` plumbing could carve out to `scripts/fleet/_lib.py`; for now `apply.py` owns it."*

### Does asyncssh support `password=` directly? (yes — no new dependency needed)
Per asyncssh's public `connect()` / `SSHClientConnectionOptions` API (this repo doesn't have asyncssh installed locally to introspect — `ModuleNotFoundError` when checked — but per public asyncssh docs, confirmed by the user's own framing and the prior research plan below):
- `asyncssh.connect(host, password="...")` performs native password authentication in-process, no subprocess/pty needed.
- `preferred_auth` (a comma-separated string or sequence, e.g. `"keyboard-interactive,password"`) controls auth method ordering/inclusion — this directly addresses TODO.md:80's point (b), which currently requires `sshpass`'s `-o PreferredAuthentications=...` workaround.
- asyncssh also supports `kbdint_challenge`/automatic single-prompt password response for `keyboard-interactive` (PAM) auth, meaning it can answer PAM password prompts too, not just plain `password` auth — this is the exact `zyc_friend` failure mode (`gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive`, no `publickey`).

**Conclusion for design**: since `asyncssh>=2.18` is already a hard dependency and its `connect()` already accepts `password=`/`preferred_auth=` natively, **there is no technical reason to shell out to `sshpass`** — doing password/PAM auth via asyncssh's own kwargs is strictly better: it avoids the new external-binary dependency (point (c) "graceful fallback when sshpass not installed" becomes moot — nothing to fall back from), avoids pty/subprocess/expect-style fragility, and is trivially async-parallel-safe (point (d)) since it's just another `await asyncssh.connect(...)` call, no TTY involved either way. The TODO.md:80 sketch (written before this level of code inspection) assumed `sshpass -f`; the actual code-level finding is that `sshpass` isn't needed at all.

### Error propagation / retry feasibility
Because every connect call is a bare `await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(host))` inside a `try/except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`, adding "try key auth, then fall back to password auth" is straightforward **if centralized**: replace the direct call with a call to a new `async def _connect(host, connect_timeout)` that:
1. Calls `_connect_kwargs(host)` (key/agent only, current behavior) and attempts `asyncssh.connect(**kwargs)`.
2. On `asyncssh.PermissionDenied` (or broader `asyncssh.Error`), if `host` has an opt-in SSH-login password source resolved, retries with `kwargs | {"password": host.ssh_login_password, "preferred_auth": "keyboard-interactive,password"}`.
3. Re-raises (or lets propagate) any other exception unchanged, preserving the outer `except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)` at each of the 10 call sites without modification.

This keeps the "opt-in only, default stays key-only" invariant (point (e)) trivially: the fallback branch only activates when the new host field is set, and does nothing differently for the other ~9 existing hosts in a typical fleet.

## 2. `sshpass` availability

**Debian/Ubuntu apt**: yes — `sshpass` is a normal package in Debian `main` / Ubuntu `universe` (enabled by default on stock installs), installable with plain `apt install sshpass`, no PPA/GPG key/third-party repo needed. This matches the "simple package" apt list pattern already used in `dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml:47-59` (`nmap`, `arp-scan`, `mtr`, `iperf3`, `httpie`, `tcpdump` — no repo setup).

**Homebrew on macOS — important, non-obvious finding**: I checked live on this machine (`brew info --json=v2 sshpass`) and `sshpass` is currently a first-party `homebrew/core` formula (`tap: homebrew/core`, `deprecated: false`, `disabled: false`, stable 1.10, bottled). So the "Homebrew-core removed sshpass years ago, use `hudochenkov/sshpass` tap" folklore is **stale as of this environment (2026-07-02)** — it appears Homebrew re-added it to core at some point. **No third-party tap is needed for `brew install sshpass` today.** (Still worth a one-line comment in the ansible task noting this history, since it's a commonly-cited gotcha and could regress again — but design-wise, treat it as a plain `homebrew:` list entry, not a tap+trust block like `workmux`.)

**Repo's Brewfile taps**: `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl:11` has `tap "nikitabobko/tap"` (aerospace) and `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl:38` has `tap "wxtsky/tap"` (CodeIsland). The devtools role additionally registers `dlvhdr/formulae` and `raine/workmux` (lines 9-23), tracked in the "Trust untrusted third-party taps" loop (`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:208-211` full inventory: `nikitabobko/tap`, `wxtsky/tap`, `hashicorp/tap`, `teamookla/speedtest`, `specstoryai/tap`, `steipete/tap`, `marcus/tap`, `dlvhdr/formulae`, `raine/workmux`). If a tap were ever needed again for sshpass, you'd add a `homebrew_tap:` task + append the name to that trust-loop's `loop:` list and to this doc inventory — but per the live check above, this step can be **skipped entirely**.

## 3. `expect` availability

**Debian/Ubuntu apt**: `expect` is packaged (`apt install expect`) but is **not guaranteed preinstalled** on minimal/server/cloud/Docker base images — it must be explicitly declared as a dependency, same as `sshpass`.

**macOS**: confirmed empirically on this machine — `/usr/bin/expect` exists out of the box (`expect version 5.45`, a universal x86_64/arm64e Mach-O binary shipped by the OS, not by Homebrew — path is `/usr/bin`, not `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin`). **This means macOS needs zero install step for `expect`** — the `fleet` design can just assume/check for it, matching the existing `ccze`-style comment pattern in `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:111-113` ("ccze is not available on Homebrew... the `lessl` zsh wrapper is guarded on `command -v ccze` so it becomes a no-op on macOS" — inverse case here: guard is a no-op on Linux, not macOS).

**Repo-wide grep**: no existing usage of `expect`(1) or `sshpass` anywhere in `dot_ansible/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `dot_config/`, or the two test Dockerfiles (`Dockerfile.centos7`, `Dockerfile.rocky9`) — every "expect" hit in `docs/` is the English word, not the tool (verified via `grep -rn "sshpass\|expect"`). `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md` uses "expect(s) the prompt" only in the generic-English sense describing Fabric's sudo-password flow, not the Tcl `expect` binary. `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md:137` and `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl:12` show the *current* state of the art for unreachable-key-auth hosts is just "Fix with `ssh-copy-id`" — i.e., there is genuinely no password-fallback mechanism today, confirming this is a net-new feature.

**No.** `find dot_ansible/roles/devtools` shows only `tasks/main.yml` — no `defaults/` or `vars/` directory at all for this role. ```yaml

# Goal

Implement TODO.md:80 in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi`: give the `fleet` CLI (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet`, backed by `scripts/fleet/*.py`, using `asyncssh>=2.18`) an OPT-IN fallback to password-based SSH login for hosts where key/agent auth is impossible (e.g. sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no` and only allows `keyboard-interactive`/PAM — the real-world trigger host `zyc_friend`, an IDC server). Today SSH login is 100% key/agent-only; such hosts permanently show as `unreachable` in `fleet-status`.

# Confirmed design decisions (already decided, do not re-litigate)

1. **No new external binary.** Use asyncssh's own native `password=` and `preferred_auth=` kwargs on `asyncssh.connect()` — NOT sshpass, NOT expect. asyncssh already supports keyboard-interactive/PAM auto-response via the `password` kwarg. Zero new PEP 723 dependencies needed (asyncssh>=2.18 already covers this).
2. **New, separate TOML schema field**: `ssh_login_password_source` (same 4-way schema as the existing `password_source`: `type` ∈ {`plain`,`prompt`,`bitwarden`,`none`}, `value`/`item` extra key) — kept fully independent from the existing `password_source` (which remains sudo-only), because a host's SSH login password may differ from its sudo password.
3. **Do not install sshpass/expect anywhere** in ansible/Brewfile — keep zero new dependencies.
4. Must stay **opt-in only** — hosts without the new field keep today's exact key/agent-only behavior. #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "asyncssh>=2.18",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
"""
scripts/fleet/apply.py — Run `chezmoi update --init` (or `apply` / `diff`)
across a fleet of remote hosts in parallel, with optional sudo password
injection. (Renamed from `scripts/fleet_apply.py` on 2026-05-13 alongside
the `fleet chezmoi` namespace refactor.)

Why this exists:
    Pushing dotfile changes to N machines by hand (ssh, type password, wait,
    grep logs) is error-prone. This wraps that flow:

      * Host list + connection details live in ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
      * Connection prefers ssh_config alias (ProxyJump, IdentityAgent, etc. all
        kept) — falls back to explicit hostname/user/port/identity_file.
      * Sudo password sources: plaintext (TOML), interactive prompt (asked once
        at startup), Bitwarden CLI (`bw get password <item>`), or omitted.
      * Per-host `no_root_machine = true` skips sudo entirely (matches the
        chezmoi `noRoot=true` init choice on that host).
      * Live Rich table of progress + per-host log files under
        logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log

Exit code: number of failed hosts (0 = all good, capped at 125).

See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full schema, examples, troubleshooting.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import dataclasses
import getpass
import os
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import tomllib
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import asyncssh
import tyro
from rich.console import Console
from rich.live import Live
from rich.table import Table


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PasswordSourceType = Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Host:
    """One remote machine. See machines.toml schema in docs."""

    name: str
    ssh_alias: str | None = None
    hostname: str | None = None
    user: str | None = None
    port: int | None = None
    identity_file: str | None = None
    no_root_machine: bool = False
    chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
    # When True, bypass SSH entirely and run chezmoi as a local
    # subprocess on the orchestrator machine. Useful for including the
    # control box itself in a fleet apply (e.g. you keep your own
    # workstation in sync with the same `just fleet-apply` invocation).
    # Local hosts skip all SSH-specific config (ssh_alias/hostname/
    # user/port/identity_file are ignored) and reuse the caller's
    # ambient PATH so chezmoi_path = "auto" still works without the
    # remote-style PATH augmentation. Sudo password injection is
    # skipped — chezmoi inherits the caller's tty/sudoers state.
    local: bool = False
    extra_env: dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
    # Resolved later (not from TOML directly)
    password_source_type: PasswordSourceType = "none"
    password_source_arg: str | None = None  # plain value, bw item id, etc.
    sudo_password: str | None = None  # populated by resolve_passwords()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TOML loading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = Path(
    os.environ.get("FLEET_CONFIG")
    or (Path.home() / ".config" / "fleet" / "machines.toml")
).expanduser()


def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).

    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
    `password_source` table is normalized into (type, arg) on Host.
    """
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
        )
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        data = tomllib.load(f)

    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
    if not raw_hosts:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")

    hosts: list[Host] = []
    seen_names: set[str] = set()
    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
        name = raw.get("name")
        if not name:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
        if name in seen_names:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
        seen_names.add(name)

        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
        ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{path}: host {name!r} has invalid password_source.type={ps_type!r}"
            )
        ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")

        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
        host = Host(
            **host_kwargs,
            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
        )

        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{path}: host {name!r} must define either `ssh_alias` "
                f"(preferred) or `hostname` (or set `local = true` to run "
                f"on the orchestrator machine without SSH)."
            )
        hosts.append(host)
    return hosts, defaults



# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Password resolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _bw_get_password(item: str) -> str:
    """Call `bw get password <item>`; raise on failure with a helpful message."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bw", "get", "password", item],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
            check=False,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "`bw` (Bitwarden CLI) not found in PATH — install with "
            "`npm install -g @bitwarden/cli` or set password_source.type to "
            "'plain'/'prompt'/'none'."
        ) from e
    if result.returncode != 0:
        stderr = (result.stderr or "").strip()
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"bw get password {item!r} failed (rc={result.returncode}): {stderr}\n"
            f"Hint: run `bw unlock` first; ensure BW_SESSION is exported."
        )
    return result.stdout.strip("\n")


def resolve_passwords(hosts: list[Host], console: Console) -> list[Host]:
    """Mutates each host.sudo_password in-place. Returns the same list.

    For `prompt` hosts: asks once each on stdin (NOT batched — different
    machines may have different passwords). For `bitwarden`: one `bw` call per
    host. For `plain`: copies value through. For `none`: leaves None.

    Hosts whose resolution FAILS keep sudo_password=None; run_one() then treats
    them as "no password available" (fail-fast at sudo phase unless
    no_root_machine=true).
    """
    for h in hosts:
        if h.password_source_type == "none":
            continue
        if h.password_source_type == "plain":
            h.sudo_password = h.password_source_arg or ""
            if not h.sudo_password:
                console.print(
                    f"[yellow]warn[/]: host {h.name!r} password_source=plain but value is empty"
                )
            continue
        if h.password_source_type == "prompt":
            try:
                h.sudo_password = getpass.getpass(
                    f"sudo password for [{h.name}] {h.user or ''}@"
                    f"{h.ssh_alias or h.hostname}: "
                )
            except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
                console.print(f"[yellow]warn[/]: host {h.name!r} prompt cancelled")
                h.sudo_password = None
            continue
        if h.password_source_type == "bitwarden":
            if not h.password_source_arg:
                console.print(
                    f"[red]error[/]: host {h.name!r} password_source=bitwarden missing `item`"
                )
                continue
            try:
                h.sudo_password = _bw_get_password(h.password_source_arg)
            except RuntimeError as e:
                console.print(f"[red]error[/]: {h.name}: {e}")
                h.sudo_password = None
    return hosts


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Remote command construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Path the orchestrator writes the password to on the remote (0600, in $HOME).
# Picked up by sudo_session_init via CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE — see the
# corresponding extension in scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh.
REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH = ".cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass"
# Per-run log dir on the remote. fleet-apply tees chezmoi's combined output
# here so a dropped SSH session doesn't lose progress visibility — `just
# fleet-apply-tail HOST` reads the latest file. Survives across runs (one
# file per timestamp); see _gc_local_logs / `--keep-logs` for retention.
REMOTE_LOG_DIR = ".cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs"
# Same layout for local hosts so --status / --tail can probe both kinds
# uniformly. Absolute path; the SSH side uses the relative form because
# the remote shell starts in $HOME.
LOCAL_LOG_DIR = Path.home() / ".cache" / "chezmoi-fleet" / "logs"


def build_remote_command(
    host: Host,
    mode: Literal["update", "apply", "diff"],
    init: bool,

    """
    drift_paths: list[str] = []
    for raw in diag_lines:
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        m = _DRIFT_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            drift_paths.append(m.group(1))
            continue
        # Anything else in stderr → not a pure-drift case.
        return False, []
    return bool(drift_paths), drift_paths


def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs.

    asyncssh reads ~/.ssh/config by default for the `host` arg. When ssh_alias
    is set we pass it as `host` and let asyncssh resolve hostname/user/port/
    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.
    """
    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
    if host.user:
        kwargs["username"] = host.user
    if host.port:
        kwargs["port"] = host.port
    if host.identity_file:
        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
    return kwargs


def _gc_local_logs(keep: int) -> None:
    """Trim LOCAL_LOG_DIR to the `keep` most recent .log files (+ .exit).

    Mirrors the remote GC done by build_remote_command. keep<=0 disables.
    Silent on errors (best-effort cleanup).
    """
    if keep <= 0:
        return
    try:
        logs = sorted(
            LOCAL_LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"),
            key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
            reverse=True,
        )
    except OSError:
        return
    for stale in logs[keep:]:
        for ext in (".log", ".exit"):
            try:
                (LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{stale.stem}{ext}").unlink(missing_ok=True)

            #     and the wrapper's trap fires.
            proc = await conn.create_process(cmd, stdin=asyncssh.PIPE)

```text
    Use case: you Ctrl+C'd a fleet-apply run locally but suspect the remote
    chezmoi/ansible is still chugging along (the wrapper's SIGHUP trap
    doesn't always fire — e.g. asyncssh closing the channel "cleanly"
    skips HUP). This sub-command answers "what's still running where?"
    without disturbing anything. Read-only — no chezmoi command sent.

    `watch > 0` re-probes every `watch` seconds and exits when no host is
    in `running` state (or on Ctrl+C). Useful as a passive "wait until
    everyone's done" cursor after killing the controller. Polls are kept
    short to dominate latency, not host load — pgrep + a 1-line ls is
    fast enough to run every 5–10s on a 100-host fleet without strain.

    Output per host: state (running/finished/idle), the latest run id,
    PIDs (if running), exit code (if finished), and the last 5 log lines.
    Always returns 0 — this is a probe, not a verdict.
    """
    async def _probe_one(h: Host) -> tuple[Host, dict, str]:
        if h.local:
            return h, *_probe_local()
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
                conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(h))
            async with conn:
                result = await conn.run(_STATUS_PROBE_CMD, check=False)
            stdout = result.stdout or ""
        except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
            return h, {"STATE": "error"}, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}\n"
        # Parse KEY=VAL lines until LOG_TAIL_BEGIN; the rest is log tail.
        fields: dict[str, str] = {}
        log_lines: list[str] = []
        in_tail = False
        for line in stdout.splitlines():
            if line == "LOG_TAIL_BEGIN":
                in_tail = True
                continue
            if line == "LOG_TAIL_END":
                in_tail = False
                continue
            if in_tail:
                log_lines.append(line)
            elif "=" in line:
                k, _, v = line.partition("=")
                fields[k] = v
        return h, fields, "\n".join(log_lines) + ("\n" if log_lines else "")

            snap = _parse_via_pqsum(body, host.name)
            if snap is None:
                return HostResult(host=host.name, source="parse-error", error="pqsum parse failed", elapsed_ms=elapsed)
            return HostResult(host=host.name, source="ok", snapshot=snap, elapsed_ms=elapsed)
        return HostResult(host=host.name, source=source, elapsed_ms=elapsed)

class _ClientKbdIntAuth(ClientAuth):
    """Client side implementation of keyboard-interactive auth"""

    _handler_names = get_symbol_names(globals(), 'MSG_USERAUTH_INFO_')

    async def _start(self) -> None:
        """Start client keyboard interactive authentication"""

        submethods = await self._conn.kbdint_auth_requested()

        if submethods is None:
            self._conn.try_next_auth(next_method=True)
            return

        self.logger.debug1('Trying keyboard-interactive auth')

        await self.send_request(String(''), String(submethods))

    async def _receive_challenge(self, name: str, instruction: str, lang: str,
                                 prompts: KbdIntPrompts) -> None:
        """Receive and respond to a keyboard interactive challenge"""

        responses = \
            await self._conn.kbdint_challenge_received(name, instruction,
                                                       lang, prompts)

        if responses is None:
            self._conn.try_next_auth(next_method=True)
            return

        self.send_packet(MSG_USERAUTH_INFO_RESPONSE, UInt32(len(responses)),
                         b''.join(String(r) for r in responses),
                         trivial=not responses)

    def _process_info_request(self, _pkttype: int, _pktid: int,
                              packet: SSHPacket) -> None:
        """Process a keyboard interactive authentication request"""

        name_bytes = packet.get_string()
        instruction_bytes = packet.get_string()
        lang_bytes = packet.get_string()

        try:
            name = name_bytes.decode('utf-8')
            instruction = instruction_bytes.decode('utf-8')
            lang = lang_bytes.decode('ascii')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            raise ProtocolError('Invalid keyboard interactive '
                                'info request') from None

        num_prompts = packet.get_uint32()
        prompts = []
        for _ in range(num_prompts):
            prompt_bytes = packet.get_string()
            echo = packet.get_boolean()

            try:
                prompt = prompt_bytes.decode('utf-8')
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                raise ProtocolError('Invalid keyboard interactive '
                                    'info request') from None

            prompts.append((prompt, echo))

        self.create_task(self._receive_challenge(name, instruction,
                                                 lang, prompts))

    _packet_handlers = {
        MSG_USERAUTH_INFO_REQUEST: _process_info_request
    }

def get_supported_client_auth_methods() -> Sequence[bytes]:
    """Return a list of supported client auth methods"""

    return [method for method in _client_auth_handlers
            if method != b'none']


def lookup_client_auth(conn: 'SSHClientConnection',
                       method: bytes) -> Optional[ClientAuth]:
    """Look up the client authentication method to use"""

    if method in _auth_methods:
        return _client_auth_handlers[method](conn, method)
    else:
        return None


def get_supported_server_auth_methods(conn: 'SSHServerConnection') -> \
        Sequence[bytes]:
    """Return a list of supported server auth methods"""

    auth_methods = []

    for method in _auth_methods:
        if _server_auth_handlers[method].supported(conn):
            auth_methods.append(method)

    return auth_methods


def lookup_server_auth(conn: 'SSHServerConnection', username: str,
                       method: bytes, packet: SSHPacket) -> \
        Optional[ServerAuth]:
    """Look up the server authentication method to use"""

    handler = _server_auth_handlers.get(method)

    if handler and handler.supported(conn):
        return handler(conn, username, method, packet)
    else:
        conn.send_userauth_failure(False)
        return None
